body.text: Oṃ namo bhagavate śrīguṇasāgarāya //
body.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the glorious <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Śrīguṇasāgara</s> (Ocean of Auspicious Qualities)!

children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Śrī Śākyaketu</s>, accompanied by hosts of gods, the God of gods, the Supreme God,
the one who ferries across the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the treasury of all virtues, <s>Gautama</s>, Lord <s>Buddha</s>,
who roars the lion's roar in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the remover of all fears, the umbrella of <s>Dharma</s>, the lord of sages —
I shall declare the jewel of <s>Dharma</s>, spoken by the best of sages, desired by all the worlds.
Then King <s>Aśoka</s>, lord of the earth, at <s>Kukkuṭārāma</s>,
again addressed <s>Upagupta</s>, eager for the twenty-two tales.
"Venerable one, I wish to hear the auspicious tale of <s>caitya</s> worship,
that nectar of <s>Dharma</s> issuing from the lotus of your mouth."
Having heard this request, <s>Upagupta</s> instructed:
"Listen, <s>Aśoka</s>, I shall narrate the twenty-two <s>avadānas</s> (noble deeds)."

body.text: I. puṇyaprotsāhanakathā
body.translated_text: I. The Narrative of Encouragement to Merit (<s>Puṇyaprotsāhanakathā</s>)

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Teacher, the Fully Awakened One, the Guide of the World, was dwelling
at <s>Rājagṛha</s>, at the great and radiant <s>Gṛddhakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak), the abode of bliss,
together with a great assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, twelve hundred in number,

children.text: mahadbhir bodhisattvaiś ca aśītyā ca sahasrakaiḥ // Dak_1.2 //
children.translated_text: and with great <s>bodhisattvas</s>, eighty thousand in all.
Honored by gods, <s>dānavas</s>, <s>gandharvas</s>, <s>yakṣas</s>, <s>kiṃnaras</s>, and humans,

children.text: puraskṛtyārcitas tasthau pūrṇenduḥ khe grahair iva // Dak_1.3 //
children.translated_text: he stood worshipped at the forefront, like the full moon in the sky among the planets.
Illuminating with great radiance, surveying the assembly,

children.text: trikālakalyāṇaṃ dharmaṃ dideśa parṣadāṃ punaḥ // Dak_1.4 //
children.translated_text: he again taught the <s>Dharma</s>, which is auspicious in the three times, to the assemblies.

body.text: ādau kalyāṇaṃ madhye kalyāṇaṃ paryavasāne kalyāṇaṃ svartham suvyañjanaṃ kevalaṃ paripūrṇaṃ pariśuddhaṃ paryavadātaṃ brahmacaryaṃ saṃprakāśayati sma //
body.translated_text: Auspicious in the beginning, auspicious in the middle, auspicious at the end, with good meaning, with good phrasing, complete, wholly perfect, pure, and stainless — he proclaimed the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>).

children.translated_text: Then <s>Ānanda</s>, the self-knowing one, with palms joined in joy,

children.text: sarvajñaṃ dharmarājaṃ taṃ natvā bhaktipuraḥsaraḥ // Dak_1.5 //
children.translated_text: having bowed to the Omniscient One, the King of <s>Dharma</s>, with devotion foremost,
"O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I wish to hear, for the welfare of people,

children.text: dharmāṇām uttamaṃ dharmaṃ vada vādīndra vādirāṭ // Dak_1.6 //
children.translated_text: the supreme <s>Dharma</s> among all <s>dharmas</s> — speak, O best of debaters, O king of orators!"

children.text: iti saṃprārthite tena śākyasiṃhas tataḥ svayam /
children.translated_text: Thus implored by him, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s> then himself

children.text: samādhiṃ vidadhe tatra dharmasaṃdarśanaṃ varam // Dak_1.7 //
children.translated_text: entered into <s>samādhi</s> there, the excellent vision of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: athāsya subhrūvivarād babhūva vinirgatā sā prahatāndhakārā /
children.translated_text: Then from the space between his beautiful brows there emerged, dispelling darkness,

children.text: sarvāsu dikṣu pratibhāsiteva madhyāhnasūryasya gabhastimālā // Dak_1.8 //
children.translated_text: a garland of rays like those of the midday sun, illuminating all directions.
Then his disciples, with the assemblies, showered the <s>Bhagavān</s>

children.text: supuṣpair vāyunā ghūrṇā nagaṃ bālalatā iva // Dak_1.9 //
children.translated_text: with beautiful flowers, like young creepers swaying in the wind around a tree.

body.text: cacāla vasudhā sābdhi

children.translated_text: with six types of upheaval, along with the mountains;

children.text: papāta puṣpaṃ meghebhyo nedur vādyaṃ surarṣayaḥ // Dak_1.10 //
children.translated_text: flowers rained from the clouds, and the celestial sages sounded instruments.

body.translated_text: The earth trembled together with the oceans,

children.translated_text: Then all the hosts of gods came to <s>Gṛddhakūṭa</s> —
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śaṃkara</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Kāmeśvara</s>, and others.

body.text: asurā

children.translated_text: <s>khagas</s> (birds), <s>gandharvas</s>,
<s>kiṃnaras</s>, and great serpents (<s>mahoragas</s>),
the world-protectors (<s>lokapālas</s>), and others such as <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and the rest.

body.translated_text: The <s>asuras</s>,

children.translated_text: There, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> and having prostrated,

children.text: devāś cānye gaṇāḥ sarve pratasthur vismayāt puraḥ // Dak_1.13 //
children.translated_text: the gods and all other hosts stood before him in amazement.

children.text: atha śrībhagavāñ chāstā vyutthāya ca samādhinā /
children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Teacher, having arisen from <s>samādhi</s>,

children.text: parṣadgaṇaṃ samālokya prahasan tūṣṇīm abhūt tadā // Dak_1.14 //
children.translated_text: surveying the assembly, smiling, remained silent then.
Then <s>Ānanda</s>, the greatly wise one, knowing the sage's assent,

children.text: āsanāt sahasotthāya bhagavantam uvāca saḥ // Dak_1.15 //
children.translated_text: suddenly rising from his seat, spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:
"O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I wish to drink that which issues from the lotus of your mouth —

children.text: vākpīyūṣaṃ tṛṣārto 'pi girijaṃ kam ivārditaḥ // Dak_1.16 //
children.translated_text: the nectar of words, though I am parched with thirst, like one afflicted seeking mountain-born water."

children.text: kaś cin mahādhano loke vidvān bhogī ca bhāgyavān /
children.translated_text: "Someone in the world is greatly wealthy, learned, prosperous, and fortunate,

children.text: daridro vyādhito duḥkhī śilpavān ko 'pi bāliśaḥ // Dak_1.17 //
children.translated_text: while another is poor, diseased, miserable — skilled yet foolish.

children.text: suraloke gataḥ kaś cin niraye cātidāruṇe /
children.translated_text: Someone has gone to the realm of gods, another to a terrible hell —

children.text: kena karmavipākena tādṛk syād bhagavan katham // Dak_1.18 //
children.translated_text: by what ripening of <s>karma</s> does such come about, O <s>Bhagavān</s>?"
"Tell all that, O best of debaters, you who act for the welfare of all the worlds,
having shown compassion to me, who am drowning in the ocean of existence."
Thus addressed, the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke to the most excellent <s>bhikṣu</s>,
displaying his own majesty for the benefit of all the worlds.

children.text: mahābhāgeti sattvānāṃ yat tac ced dhṛdi rocate /
children.translated_text: "O great-fortunate one, if it pleases the hearts of beings,

children.text: ṣaṭsu gatiṣu magnānāṃ tac chṛṇuṣva śubhāśubham // Dak_1.21 //
children.translated_text: listen to the auspicious and inauspicious of those sunk in the six destinies.
It has been heard before, O great-fortunate one: good and evil among living beings —
born in the four types of birth, they are always bound by their respective <s>karmas</s>.
Egg-born, moisture-born, spontaneously born, and womb-born —

children.text: khagādyā aṇḍajāḥ proktā mānavādyā jarāyujāḥ // Dak_1.23 //
children.translated_text: birds and such are called egg-born; humans and such are womb-born.
Worms, insects, and such are moisture-born; gods and such are spontaneously born.

children.text: dṛśyante karmaṇā caite vrataśīlena dhīmatā // Dak_1.24 //
children.translated_text: These are seen according to their <s>karma</s>, through vows and moral conduct, by the wise.
According to the distinction of their destinies, beings are born thus,
in the four great continents, driven by the ripening of former <s>karma</s>.
Born in the six destinies — low, high, and middling —

children.text: bhikṣo karmavipākena gatis teṣāṃ pṛthak pṛthak // Dak_1.26 //
children.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣu</s>, by the ripening of <s>karma</s>, each of their destinies is different.
This <s>karma</s>, auspicious and inauspicious, born of body, speech, and mind —

children.text: phalaṃ bhukte janas tasya lokottare ca laukike // Dak_1.27 //
children.translated_text: a person experiences its fruit both in the supramundane and the worldly realms.
Then <s>Ānanda</s> again spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the teacher of the world:

children.text: pāpānāṃ mūlalokānāṃ vyaktayas tvaṃ pradarśaya // Dak_1.28 //
children.translated_text: "Reveal the manifestations of the root sins of the worlds.

children.text: kāyavāṅmanasā karma kāni kāni kṛtāni ca /
children.translated_text: What <s>karmas</s> have been done by body, speech, and mind?

children.text: yat sarvaṃ tad viśeṣaṃ ca vada me vādipuṃgava // Dak_1.29 //
children.translated_text: Tell me all that in detail, O bull among debaters."

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: śubhāśubhaphalaṃ nṝṇāṃ yac chṛṇuṣva sphuṭaṃ tataḥ /
children.translated_text: "The fruit of the auspicious and inauspicious for people — hear that clearly then:

children.text: dharmeṇa prāpyate modam amodam aśubhodbhavam // Dak_1.30 //
children.translated_text: through <s>Dharma</s> one attains joy; sorrow arises from what is inauspicious.

body.text: punaś ca vistareṇa //
body.translated_text: And again in detail:

children.translated_text: Bodily misconduct (<s>kāyaduścarita</s>) is declared to be threefold:
taking what is not given, taking of life, and sexual misconduct.
Verbal misconduct (<s>vākduścarita</s>) is declared to be fourfold:
falsehood, slander, harsh speech, and divisive talk — thus spoke the wise one.

children.text: manoduścaritaṃ karma tridhā bhinnaṃ vidur budhāḥ /
children.translated_text: Mental misconduct (<s>manoduścarita</s>) is known by the wise to be threefold:
covetousness, ill-will, and wrong views — these three kinds.
One who, being hostile, abandons compassion through killing other beings and such —
striking, harmful acts, and the like — that is called taking of life.
Through greed for another's possessions, by injustice and by force,
through theft, falsehood, and unrighteousness — that is known as taking what is not given.

body.text: vratinī dharmacāriṇyo 'śucī veśyā

children.translated_text: others' wives,

children.text: saṃbandhini prasaṅgādi kāmamithyā tad ucyate // Dak_1.36 //
children.translated_text: and relations and such connections — that is called sexual misconduct.

body.translated_text: Women under vows, women of righteous conduct, impure women, prostitutes,

children.text: viṣayeṣu ca lobheṣu sneheṣu ca bhayeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: In matters of desires, greed, affections, and fears,

children.text: asatyena probodhāya mṛṣāvādas tad ucyate // Dak_1.37 //
children.translated_text: to mislead through untruth — that is called false speech.
One who conceals one's own faults while exposing others' faults,
cursing with words that pierce vital points — that is known as harsh speech.
Through conduct of evil dealings, one creates enmity with friends and relatives,

children.text: svena ca guṇalabdhāya paiśunyaṃ vidadhā mataḥ // Dak_1.39 //
children.translated_text: and misappropriates for oneself what is gained by merit — that is regarded as slander.

body.text:
yasyāgre bhinnavādena paracittam adhīrayan /
parasparavidveṣaṃ syāt saṃbhinna vidadhā mata
body.translated_text: One who, through divisive speech in someone's presence, agitates another's mind, creating mutual hatred — that is regarded as divisive talk.

body.text: paradravyādisaṃpatti

children.translated_text: coveting with a greedy mind —

children.text: tad abhidhyā iti jñeyaṃ durjanaḥ parisevyate // Dak_1.41 //
children.translated_text: that is to be known as covetousness (<s>abhidhyā</s>); it is cultivated by the wicked.

body.translated_text: Another's wealth and possessions,

children.translated_text: Toward another's bodily endowments and such, with an evil mind one curses,

children.text: amaṅgalaṃ bhavatv iti vyāpādo 'yaṃ sa ucyate // Dak_1.42 //
children.translated_text: 'May misfortune befall!' — that is called ill-will (<s>vyāpāda</s>).

body.text:
paratra pāpapuṇyaṃ na sukhaduḥkhaṃ na vidyate /
durbodhaśāstraṃ śrutvā ca mithyādṛṣṭi

children.translated_text: he is a nihilist (<s>nāstika</s>).

body.translated_text: 'There is no merit or sin in the hereafter, nor pleasure nor pain' — having heard such misleading scriptures, that is wrong view (<s>mithyādṛṣṭi</s>);

children.translated_text: Thus, by the ten unwholesome deeds, that fool, through sin alone,
is tormented in the hereafter by the messengers of <s>Yama</s> with various afflictions.
Therefore, O <s>Ānanda</s>, I have spoken of the arising of fruit from the tree of the body:

children.text: yena yena kṛtaṃ karma tena tena prabhuñjate // Dak_1.45 //
children.translated_text: whatever <s>karma</s> is done by whomever, by that very one is it experienced.
Beings are submerged in the pool of birth, death, old age, and suffering;

children.text: tasmād bhīyā mahābhīme bhujaṅge bhītimān iva // Dak_1.46 //
children.translated_text: therefore, be afraid of the greatly terrible, as one fearful of a serpent.
Gods, <s>asuras</s>, humans, animals, <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), and hell-beings —

children.text: ṣagatau jāyate tasmiñ śubhāśubhena karmaṇā // Dak_1.47 //
children.translated_text: one is born in the six destinies according to auspicious and inauspicious <s>karma</s>.

body.text:
iti śrutvā athānando lokānām anuśocayan /
bhītasaṃsāradurvāra

children.translated_text: with hair standing on end,

body.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Ānanda</s>, lamenting for the worlds, fearful of the irresistible <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.translated_text: then <s>Maitreya</s>, of subdued senses, rising from his seat,

children.text: lokānāṃ ca hitārthāya avocaj jagatāṃ prabhum // Dak_1.49 //
children.translated_text: for the welfare of the worlds, spoke to the Lord of beings:
"O <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, Lord of heroes, increaser of the world's joy!

children.text: dākṣiṇyam phalasaṃpūrṇaṃ bhāṣasva vividhaṃ varam // Dak_1.50 //
children.translated_text: Speak of the fullness of the fruit of generosity (<s>dākṣiṇya</s>), various and excellent.
Encouragement to merit, hearing, the rarity of giving and merit,

children.text: bimbasnānam tathā gandhaṃ chattram dhātvāvaropaṇam // Dak_1.51 //
children.translated_text: bathing the image, likewise anointing, the parasol, the enshrinement of relics,
the <s>maṇḍala</s>, food, drink, clothing, the description of flowers and such,
prostration, the waving of lights and lamps, the monastery, and bedding and seats,

body.text:
kṣetraṃ vicitraṃ caivāntam ity etā bahudhā bhṛśam /
kathā dvāviṃśati

children.text: saṃkhyā vada me vādirāṭ prabho // Dak_1.53 //
children.translated_text: in number — tell me, O king of orators, O lord!

body.translated_text: the field, the marvelous, and also the end — these many tales, twenty-two

body.text: śīlakṣānti

children.text:
tathā vīryaṃ dhyānaṃ prajñā tathaiva ca /
ṣaḍ eva pāramitā
children.translated_text: and also vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) as well — the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),
all of them — speak of them, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O sage!"

body.translated_text: Moral conduct (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣānti</s>),

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: sādhu sādhu tva maitreya lokānāṃ hitakāraka /
children.translated_text: "Well done, well done, O <s>Maitreya</s>, benefactor of the worlds!
Listen to the splendid narrative of encouragement to merit, with a mind of loving-kindness.

body.text:
mānuṣyaṃ samavāpya duṣkaraśatair labdhvā durāpaṃ kṣaṇaṃ
mṛtyau niṣpratikāradāruṇatare nityaṃ pura

children.text:
sthāyini /
pātheyaṃ damadānasaṃyamamayaṃ yair na prabhūtaṃ kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: before one — those who have not abundantly prepared provisions consisting of self-control, generosity, and restraint
shall fall into the precipice of the terrible illness of <s>saṃsāra</s> and experience sufferings.

body.translated_text: Having obtained human birth through hundreds of difficult deeds, having gained a rare and hard-to-obtain opportunity, while death, most terrible and without remedy, ever stands

children.translated_text: Having obtained the rare human birth, fleeting like lightning, foam, and waves,

children.text: mānusye 'py akṣaṇaprāpte tadā puṇyaṃ kathaṃ smaret // Dak_1.57 //
children.translated_text: if even in human life one fails to obtain the right moment, how then shall one remember merit?
Having attained human existence, cross the great river of suffering;

children.text: puṇyam evātra kurvīta yataś cintāmaṇir nṛṇām // Dak_1.58 //
children.translated_text: one should perform merit here, for it is the wish-fulfilling gem for people.
By whose power human existence has been obtained again now,

children.text: puṇyaṃ tad vardhayasveha yasmād dhetuḥ sukhasya te // Dak_1.59 //
children.translated_text: increase that merit here, for it is the cause of your happiness.

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ yadupāśrayeṇa bhavatā labdhaṃ punaḥ sāṃprataṃ
children.translated_text: That human existence which you have obtained again now through its support,
endowed with various qualities such as beauty, nobility, high birth, and the like —

children.text: tat puṇyaṃ suhṛd eka eva jagatāṃ bandhuś ca janmāntare
children.translated_text: that merit alone is the one true friend and relative of beings across births;

children.text: tasmāt tūrṇam idaṃ kuru tvam asakṛt sarvārthasaṃpatkaram // Dak_1.60 //
children.translated_text: therefore, quickly perform this repeatedly, which accomplishes all aims and prosperity.
By whose support you have attained lordship, the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, honored by the world —

children.text: tāny eva puṇyāni vivardhayethā na karṣaṇīyo hy upakāripakṣaḥ // Dak_1.61 //
children.translated_text: increase those very merits; for one should not diminish the side of beneficence.

body.text:
viramata pāpataḥ kuruta puṇyam udārataraṃ
damayata durdama

children.translated_text: horse of the mind, which is restless toward sense objects!

children.text: daśati na yāvad eva maraṇāhir asahyaviṣaḥ // Dak_1.62 //
children.translated_text: Be always devoted to the welfare of others, like the lord of sages, before the serpent of death with unbearable venom strikes!"

body.translated_text: Cease from sin! Perform merit most generously! Tame the untamable

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ puṇyaprotsāhanakathā prathama

children.translated_text: chapter.

body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the Narrative of Encouragement to Merit (<s>Puṇyaprotsāhanakathā</s>), the first

body.text: II. dharmaśravaṇaprotsāhanakathā
body.translated_text: II. The Narrative of Encouragement to Hearing the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmaśravaṇaprotsāhanakathā</s>)

body.text:
jalanidhikūrmakarṇayugarandhrasamāgamavat
kṣaṇam a

children.text:
vāpyam adbhutam imaṃ samavetya calam /
praśamapuraikavarma vinipātabhayāpaharaṃ
children.translated_text: opportunity, which is the sole armor of the city of tranquility, removing the fear of downfall —

children.text: śṛṇuta sudurlabhaṃ kṣaṇam apīha muner vacanam // Dak_2.1 //
children.translated_text: Listen to the words of the sage, for even this moment is exceedingly rare!

body.translated_text: Like the meeting of the ocean turtle's neck with the hole in the yoke, having attained this wondrous, fleeting

children.text: yad durlabhaṃ kalpaśatair anekair mānuṣyam aṣṭākṣaṇadoṣamuktam /
children.translated_text: That which is difficult to obtain even in hundreds of <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages)—human birth free from the eight unfavorable conditions—

children.text: tat sāmprataṃ prāptam ato bhavadbhiḥ kāryo hi dharmaśravaṇāya yatnaḥ // Dak_2.2 //
children.translated_text: that you have now obtained; therefore you must make effort to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: pallavāgrajalabinducañcale kleśajālapariveṣṭite bhave
body.translated_text: In this existence, which is as unsteady as a drop of water on the tip of a leaf-bud, and which is enveloped in the net of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions),

body.text: yo na cintayati karmasatpathaṃ tasya janma bhavatīha niṣphalam // Dak_2.3 //
body.translated_text: he who does not contemplate the right path of <s>karma</s> (action)—his birth in this world becomes fruitless.

children.translated_text: Neither by those gone to the hells, nor by <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts), nor by those gone to animal births, nor by those with impaired faculties,
nor by teachers of the gods, nor by those dwelling in border regions, nor by those afflicted by wrong views—
when the sun of the sage, the light of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), has not yet risen, when the <s>Jina</s> (Victor) has not appeared—
even with humans and gods together, it is not possible to drink the nectar of the words of the lord of sages.

body.text: tasmāt kukāryaṃ vyapahāya sarvaṃ matvā svakāryaṃ paramāryadharmam

children.translated_text: the <s>Dharma</s> should indeed be heard with effort,

children.text: dharmo yasmād ataḥ sarvaguṇā bhavanti // Dak_2.5 //
children.translated_text: since from that all virtues arise.

body.translated_text: Therefore, abandoning all evil deeds, considering the supreme noble <s>Dharma</s> as one's own purpose,

children.text: maunīndraṃ vākyaratnaṃ janayati sudhiyām etad ādau pramodaṃ
children.translated_text: This jewel-word of the lord of sages first produces delight in the wise;
then, upon falling upon the ears, it destroys the mass of dense and powerful darkness of ignorance;
at the end of contemplation and meditation, it shatters the entire chain of the cycle of births;
it always disperses the entire series of afflictions—a treasure-house of all prosperity.
It removes the calamity born from the intensity of worldly existence, and bestows the unsurpassed bliss of <s>nirvṛti</s> (liberation);

children.text: tad idam evam avetya muner vacaḥ śṛṇuta saṃprati nirmalamānasāḥ // Dak_2.7 //
children.translated_text: understanding thus the words of the sage, listen now with pure minds!

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ dharmaśravaṇaprotsāhanakathā dvitīyaḥ pariccheda
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story encouraging the hearing of the <s>Dharma</s>, the second chapter

body.text: III. manuṣyadurlabhakathā
body.translated_text: III. The Story of the Rarity of Human Birth

children.text: yat prāpya janmajaladher api yānti pāram āropayanti śivam uttamabodhibījam /
children.translated_text: Having obtained which, beings cross even the ocean of birth, and plant the auspicious seed of supreme <s>bodhi</s> (awakening)—

children.text: cintāmaṇer api samabhyadhikaṃ guṇaughair mānuṣyakaṃ ka iha tad viphalīkaroti // Dak_3.1 //
children.translated_text: surpassing even the wish-fulfilling jewel in its flood of virtues—who in this world would render such human birth fruitless?

children.text: yo mānuṣyaṃ kuśalavibhavaiḥ prāpya kalpair analpair
children.translated_text: He who, having obtained human birth through meritorious powers over countless <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages),

children.text: mohāt puṇyadraviṇam iha na svalpam apy ācinoti /
children.translated_text: out of delusion does not accumulate even a small amount of merit-wealth here—

children.text: so 'smāl lokāt param upagatas tīvram abhyeti śokaṃ
children.translated_text: he, having departed from this world to the next, experiences intense grief,

children.text: ratnadvīpād vaṇig iva gataḥ svaṃ gṛhaṃ śūnyahastaḥ // Dak_3.2 //
children.translated_text: like a merchant who has returned to his own home from the Island of Jewels with empty hands.
By unwholesome paths of <s>karma</s> (action), human birth is not obtained again;

children.text: alabhyamāne mānuṣye duḥkham eva kutaḥ sukham // Dak_3.3 //
children.translated_text: when human birth is unobtainable, there is only suffering—whence happiness?

children.text: nātaḥ paraṃ vañcanāsti na ca moho 'sty ataḥ param /
children.translated_text: There is no greater deception than this, nor is there greater delusion than this—

children.text: yad īdṛśaṃ kṣaṇaṃ prāpya na kuryāt kuśalaṃ bahu // Dak_3.4 //
children.translated_text: that having obtained such a rare moment, one should not perform abundant merit.
From sin committed in a single moment, one remains in <s>Avīci</s> (hell) for a <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age);

children.text: naikajanmakṛtāt pāpāt kā punaḥ sugatau kathā // Dak_3.5 //
children.translated_text: from sin committed over many births, what further need be said about attaining a good rebirth?
Therefore the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) declared that human birth is extremely difficult to obtain,
comparable to a turtle inserting its neck through a hole in a yoke floating in the great ocean.

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ manuṣyadurlabhakathā tṛtīyaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story of the rarity of human birth, the third chapter.

body.text: IV. dānakathā
body.translated_text: IV. The Story of Generosity

body.text: annapānaśayanāsanasaṃpad ratnamālyavasanābharaṇāni
body.translated_text: Abundance of food, drink, beds, and seats; jewels, garlands, garments, and ornaments;

body.text: kīrtir uttamaguṇāś ca yuvatyo dānataḥ kathitam etad aśeṣam // Dak_4.1 //
body.translated_text: fame, excellent qualities, and young women—all this has been declared to come from <s>dāna</s> (generosity).

children.text: ājñādīptir bhogasaṃpat prakṛṣṭā rūpaudāryaṃ varṇamādhuryam ojaḥ /
children.translated_text: Radiance of authority, excellent wealth of enjoyments, beauty, generosity, sweetness of complexion, vitality,

children.text: vākṣaubhāgyaṃ kāntir ārogyam āyur etad dānād iṣṭam iṣṭaṇ phalaṃ ca // Dak_4.2 //
children.translated_text: charm of speech, loveliness, freedom from disease, and longevity—this desired fruit, both wished-for and cherished, comes from <s>dāna</s> (generosity).

body.text: aśvā

children.text:
kṣaumāṇi nāgā bahukusumasitaṃ cāmaraṃ cātapatraṃ
saudhaṃ saṃgītigarbhaṃ madhupaṭaharavāḥ puṣpamālā yuvatyaḥ /
bhojyaṃ ratnādihārā
children.translated_text: fine silks, elephants, white fly-whisks covered with abundant flowers, parasols, palaces filled with music, the sounds of drums and cymbals, flower garlands, young women, food, jeweled necklaces,
cities, kingdoms, lands, sovereignty, and the heavenly realm—

children.text: saṃbuddhatvaṃ ca buddhaiḥ kathitam iha phalaṃ dānakalpadrumasya // Dak_4.3 //
children.translated_text: and even <s>saṃbuddhatva</s> (full awakening)—the <s>Buddhas</s> have declared all this to be the fruit of the wish-fulfilling tree of <s>dāna</s> (generosity).

body.translated_text: Horses,

children.translated_text: That women with eyes rivaling the soft, spotless petals of blue lotuses,
with girdles clinging to their hips and thighs, with loosened red garments,
come into servitude, with trembling breasts and playfully arched brows—
that is the thunderous display of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), skilled in breaking open the doors of miserliness.

body.text:
aśvaiś cāmarabhāranāmitaśirorūpaiḥ khalīnonmukhair
nāgair bhinnamadaiś ca yan naravarā gacchanti chattrocchrayaiḥ /
bhṛtyaiḥ sābharaṇaiḥ kṛtāñjalipuṭair abhyarcyamānā
body.translated_text: That the best of men ride on horses with heads bowed under the weight of fly-whisks, mouths turned upward by bridles, and on elephants dripping with rut, beneath raised parasols, constantly honored by servants adorned with ornaments and with hands joined in reverence—

body.text: sadā tad dānasya phalaṃ vadanti munayaḥ pūrvārjitasyedṛśam // Dak_4.5 //
body.translated_text: the sages declare that to be the fruit of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) formerly accumulated.

children.translated_text: That kings are adorned with necklaces, bracelets of gold studded with diamonds,

children.text: keyūrair mukuṭaiś ca ratnakhacitaiḥ siṃhāsanasthāḥ sadā /
children.translated_text: with armlets and crowns set with jewels, always seated on lion-thrones,
amidst the women of the inner chambers, sporting in various amusements—

children.text: tad dānasya phalam vadanti munayaḥ śārdūlavikrīḍitam // Dak_4.6 //
children.translated_text: the sages declare that fruit of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) in the <s>Śārdūlavikrīḍita</s> (tiger-sport) meter.
In a palace studded with gems, jewels, and gold, adorned with parasols and banners,
resounding with vīṇā, flute, and song, radiant with the splendor of jewels,
that <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) sports accompanied by <s>Śacī</s>, surrounded by a thousand celestial women—

children.text: tad dānasya phalaṃ vadanti munayaḥ pūrvārjitasyedṛśam // Dak_4.7 //
children.translated_text: the sages declare that to be the fruit of <s>dāna</s> (generosity) formerly accumulated.

children.text: dātā priyatvam upayāti janasya śaśvat saṃsevyate ca bahubhiḥ samupetya sadbhiḥ /
children.translated_text: The giver always attains the affection of people, and is served by many good people who approach him;

children.text: kīrtiś ca dikṣu visaraty amalaṃ yaśo 'sya tat tat padaṃ samupayāti viśārado 'sau // Dak_4.8 //
children.translated_text: his fame spreads in all directions, his spotless glory—he attains each and every station, being wise.
Upon the dissolution of the body, being born among the gods in abodes of undiminished and various, excellent enjoyments,
obtaining birth in gardens with variegated clusters of blossoming, abundant wish-fulfilling trees,

children.text: udyāneṣu prakāmaṃ suciram atisukhaṃ nandanādiṣv akhinnaḥ
children.translated_text: in <s>Nandana</s> and other gardens, at will, for a long time, with supreme happiness, unwearied—
one attains through generous giving, being served by celestial maidens of excellent form.
<s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is indeed a great treasure that follows one, inaccessible to thieves and the like;
<s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is the washing away of the dust of jealousy, greed, and fault from the mind;
<s>Dāna</s> (generosity) is a comfortable vehicle for removing the weariness of the road of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence);
<s>Dāna</s> (generosity), disposed toward the enjoyment of manifold pleasures, is an ultimate true friend.
With girdles resting on their hips, with sweet voices, with a single brow playfully arched,
with large, beautiful eyes reaching near the ears, with garlands fastened at the edge of their hair,

children.text: yad dāsyaṃ svayam aṅganāḥ sukṛtinām āyānti pīnoravas
children.translated_text: that women of full breasts come of their own accord into the service of the meritorious—

children.text: tan māhātmyam uvāca saṃbhṛtaphalaṃ dānasya śauddhodaniḥ // Dak_4.11 //
children.translated_text: this greatness of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), rich in fruit, was declared by the son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>.

body.text: paryasyatsahakārabhaṅgasurabhi pre

children.translated_text: submerged blue lotuses stirring,
honey placed in a splendid golden vessel, red as the <s>bandhūka</s> flower—

children.text: kāminyā śapathopanītam asakṛd yat pīyate kāminā
children.translated_text: that which is repeatedly drunk by a lover from the oath-offering of his beloved—

children.text: hetuṃ tatra vadanti śuddhamatayo dānaṃ paraṃ śreyasaḥ // Dak_4.12 //
children.translated_text: those of pure intellect declare the cause therein to be <s>dāna</s> (generosity), the supreme good.

body.translated_text: Fragrant with the aroma of overturning mango blossoms, with

children.text: iti dānaguṇān niśamya saumya prayatātmā kuru dāna eva yatnam /
children.translated_text: Thus, O gentle one, having heard the virtues of <s>dāna</s> (generosity), with a disciplined mind make effort in generosity alone;

children.text: tribhavāgramahābhaye narāṇāṃ na hi dānāt param asti bandhur anyaḥ // Dak_4.13 //
children.translated_text: in the great fear of the summit of the three worlds, there is no kinsman other than <s>dāna</s> (generosity) for human beings.

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ dānakathā caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story of generosity, the fourth chapter.

body.text: V. puṇyakāmakathā
body.translated_text: V. The Story of the Desire for Merit

children.text: yad dṛśyate jagati cārutaraṃ priyaṃ vā rūpaṃ kulaṃ priyajano vibhavāḥ sukhaṃ vā /
children.translated_text: Whatever is seen in the world that is most beautiful or dear—beauty, family, loved ones, wealth, or happiness—

children.text: tat puṇyaśilpikṛtam eva vadanti santaḥ kalyāṇakāripuruṣasya tu puṇyam etat // Dak_5.1 //
children.translated_text: the saints declare that all to be crafted by <s>puṇya</s> (merit); this indeed is the merit of a man who performs good deeds.

body.text: atyucchritonnatasitadhvajapa

children.translated_text: in their rows, with armies seething with elephants, horses, infantry, and chariots,

children.text: uddhūtacāmaravirājitagātraśobhāḥ puṇyādhikāḥ kṣitibhujo bhuvi saṃcaranti // Dak_5.2 //
children.translated_text: their bodily splendor graced by uplifted fly-whisks—those abundant in <s>puṇya</s> (merit), the kings, move about on the earth.

body.translated_text: With arrays of exceedingly tall, raised white banners, colorful

children.translated_text: Clad in variegated garments of silk, <s>Kāśika</s> cloth, and fine fabric, their bodies adorned with strings of pearls, gold, and jewels—

children.text: yat ke cid eva puruṣāḥ śriyam udvahanti puṇyasya pūrvacaritasya kṛtapraśaṃsā // Dak_5.3 //
children.translated_text: that certain men bear such prosperity is the praise of <s>puṇya</s> (merit) performed in the past.

children.text: āyuḥ sudīrghaṃ sukule ca janma kāntaṃ vapur vyādhibhayaṃ na cāsti /
children.translated_text: Very long life, birth in a good family, a beautiful body, and no fear of disease,

children.text: dhanaṃ prabhūtaṃ parivārasaṃpad bhavanti puṇyasya mahāvipākāt // Dak_5.4 //
children.translated_text: abundant wealth, and the prosperity of retinue—these arise from the great fruition of <s>puṇya</s> (merit).

body.text: yac cakravartī pravarais tu ratnaiḥ sahasraputraiś ca samanvito 'pi

children.text: samudrasīmāṃ bubhuje dharitrīṃ tat puṇyaratnasya phalaṃ viśālam // Dak_5.5 //
children.translated_text: ruled the earth bounded by the oceans—that is the vast fruit of the jewel of <s>puṇya</s> (merit).

body.translated_text: That a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), endowed with the finest jewels and a thousand sons,

children.translated_text: Seated in the center of the finest, variegated lotus, always bowed to by <s>suras</s> (gods), <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>Indra</s>, and others,

children.text: yad brahmalokaṃ tv abhibhūya tejasā brahmā sadā bhāti tad eva puṇyataḥ // Dak_5.6 //
children.translated_text: that <s>Brahmā</s> always shines, surpassing even <s>Brahmaloka</s> (the world of Brahmā) in splendor—that is solely due to <s>puṇya</s> (merit).
That by hosts of <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings),

children.text: saṃpūjyate devaguruḥ sadaiva tat puṇyaratnasya phalaṃ viśālam // Dak_5.7 //
children.translated_text: <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), and excellent <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), the teacher of the gods is always worshipped—that is the vast fruit of the jewel of <s>puṇya</s> (merit).

children.text: rūpaṃ vīryaṃ ca śilpaṃ ca vihāya vivaśā narāḥ /
children.translated_text: Leaving behind beauty, valor, and craft, helpless, men

children.text: paralokam ito yānti karmavāyubhir īritāḥ // Dak_5.8 //
children.translated_text: depart from here to the other world, driven by the winds of <s>karma</s> (action).

children.text: puṇyaṃ tv ekam ihātyantam anugāmi sukhodayam /
children.translated_text: <s>Puṇya</s> (merit) alone here is the ultimate companion, the source of happiness;

children.text: puṇyam anyair ahāryatvād dhanānāṃ paramaṃ dhanam // Dak_5.9 //
children.translated_text: <s>puṇya</s> (merit), being impossible to steal by others, is the supreme wealth among all treasures.

children.text: ye merum api vegena vikiranti diśo daśa /
children.translated_text: Even those dissolution-winds that scatter <s>Meru</s> with their force in the ten directions—

children.text: te 'pi puṇyasya bhaṅgāya nālaṃ pralayavāyavaḥ // Dak_5.10 //
children.translated_text: even they are not capable of destroying <s>puṇya</s> (merit).
By the waters of the four oceans, overflowing unrestrainedly at the time of cosmic dissolution,

children.text: puṇyaṃ na kledam āyāti catuḥsāgaravāriṇā // Dak_5.11 //
children.translated_text: <s>puṇya</s> (merit) does not become dampened.
By seven blazing suns with burning rays and embers,

children.text: kṣitau vā dahyamānāyāṃ puṇyam ekaṃ na dahyate // Dak_5.12 //
children.translated_text: even when the earth is being consumed—<s>puṇya</s> (merit) alone is not burned.

body.text:
iti śrutvātha maitreyaḥ satyam eva muner vacaḥ /
bhītisaṃsāradurvāra

children.translated_text: with hair standing on end—

body.translated_text: Having heard this, <s>Maitreya</s>, [recognizing] the words of the sage as truth, terrified by the insurmountable <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence),

body.text:
tataḥ sa maitreyo harṣaiḥ śrutvātha vacanaṃ muneḥ /
jinapādāmbuja

children.translated_text: spoke thus to the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One):

body.translated_text: Then that <s>Maitreya</s>, with joy, having heard the words of the sage, bowing to the lotus feet of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor),

children.translated_text: "What would be the fruit of establishing <s>Buddha</s> images, and of restoring old ones,

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ syāt phalaṃ teṣāṃ caityānāṃ jinadhātukām // Dak_5.15 //
children.translated_text: and of those <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and relics of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor)?"

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke:

children.translated_text: "One who restores old <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary mounds) and images of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One)
would become endowed with miraculous power and strength, equal to a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch).

children.text: puṇyavān balavān bhūtvā na tasya vikalendriyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Being meritorious and powerful, he would not have impaired faculties;

children.text: tataś cānte sukhaṃ bhuktvā saṃbuddhatvaṃ prajāyate // Dak_5.17 //
children.translated_text: and then, having enjoyed happiness at the end, <s>saṃbuddhatva</s> (full awakening) arises."

body.text: maitreya āha //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> spoke:

children.text: bhagavañ jinaśārdūla sādhu ślāghyo 'si yad vibho /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), O tiger among <s>Jinas</s> (Victors), excellent! You are praiseworthy, O powerful Lord!

children.text: kena cit kṛtam astīti vada me jñānasāgara // Dak_5.18 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, O ocean of knowledge, has this been done by anyone?"

body.text: evam ukte 'tha bhagavā

children.text:
l lokānāṃ vismayāya ca /
nimittam ekam akarot tūṣṇī
children.translated_text: for the wonder of the worlds, made a single sign, and then in silence
remained still.

body.translated_text: When this was said, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One),

children.translated_text: Then, like lightning from the sky, there came one radiant with beams of light;

children.text: avabhāsya sabhāṃ sarvāṃs teṣāṃ kautūhalam abhūt // Dak_5.20 //
children.translated_text: illuminating the entire assembly, wonder arose among them.

body.text: maitreya āha //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> spoke:

body.text: bhagavann idam āścarya

children.translated_text: What is the cause of this marvel?
Whose is this radiant manifestation that has come, blazing with rays of light?"

body.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), this is wondrous!

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke:

children.translated_text: "O <s>Maitreya</s>, of King <s>Ratnavyūha</s> and of his celestial palace,

children.text: prabhā āgatya sarvatra bhāsayanti samantataḥ // Dak_5.22 //
children.translated_text: the radiances have come and illuminate everywhere in all directions.

body.text: maitreya āha //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> spoke:

children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), surely this radiance has come from him in such a manner;

children.text: kenedṛśaprabhāṃ prāpto hetubhūtaṃ ca me hṛdi // Dak_5.23 //
children.translated_text: by what means did he attain such radiance? The cause [I wish to know] in my heart."

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke:

children.text: atredānīn tu maitreya darśayiṣyāmy amuṃ nṛpam /
children.translated_text: "Now here, O <s>Maitreya</s>, I shall show you that king;
even by his past merit, his power is of great miraculous might."

body.text: atha sa rājā ratnavyūho ratnavimānam āruhya gaganadeśād ṛddhyā yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya sahasā tatrānuprāpto 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then that King <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, having mounted his jeweled celestial palace, came through the sky by his miraculous power to where the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) was, and having approached, arrived there suddenly.

body.text: atha sa rājā bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā lakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ suvarṇavarṇaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhāvirājitagātraṃ bhagavantaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajāto vimānād avatīrya tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādayoḥ praṇipatyaikānte sthitavān //
body.translated_text: Then that king, seeing the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) endowed with the thirty-two marks, golden in complexion, his body radiant with splendor surpassing a thousand suns, descended from his aerial chariot, circumambulated him three times, prostrated at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and stood to one side.

children.text: atha papraccha bhagavāñ jānann eva nṛpāgamam /
children.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, though knowing the king's arrival, asked:

children.text: kuśalaṃ tava rājendra bāhyābhyantaram eva ca // Dak_5.25 //
children.translated_text: "Is all well with you, O lord of kings, both externally and internally?"
"Speak, O greatly fortunate one, devoted to <s>dharma</s>,
O tiger among kings, well-wisher, dear to [all] beings, granting liberation."
Then he, joining his palms, having circumambulated three times,

children.text: nivedya copahārāṇi praṇamyovāca taṃ gurum // Dak_5.27 //
children.translated_text: having presented offerings and bowed, spoke to that teacher:
"O <s>Bhagavān</s>, it is well with me, thus being considered by you —
one who seeks the highest good, everywhere [guided] by the teacher, though being merely a final attendant."

children.text: nānyakāryaṃ me bhagavan tat tava darśanecchayā /
children.translated_text: "I have no other purpose, O <s>Bhagavān</s>; with the desire to see you

children.text: śravaṇāya sadā dharmaṃ tenāham iha āgataḥ // Dak_5.29 //
children.translated_text: and to hear the <s>dharma</s> always — for that I have come here."

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: deśayiṣyāmi te samyak tvam asi nṛpasattama /
children.translated_text: "I shall teach you properly; you are, O best of kings,
a worthy vessel for the <s>dharmas</s> that have become principles of conduct, O ruler of the earth."
"Listen, O king of mighty arms, to the supreme and best <s>dharma</s> of kings:
protect the strength of the king's <s>dharma</s>; follow the path of righteous conduct."

body.text: tadyathā //
body.translated_text: Namely:

children.text: yathaiva vṛkṣaṃ phalinaṃ sapuṣpaṃ saṇrakṣayet paurajanān ajasram /
children.translated_text: "Just as one should constantly protect a fruit-bearing, flower-laden tree

children.text: ādhārabhūtān nṛpateś ca nityaṃ bhūpāla itthaṃ kuru sarvataḥ syāt // Dak_5.32 //
children.translated_text: that is the perpetual support of the townspeople and the king — O ruler of the earth, do likewise everywhere."

children.text: phalodayaṃ pākavaśād yathaiva guṇo 'sti svādaṃ ca rasaṃ tathaiva /
children.translated_text: "Just as from ripening there comes the emergence of fruit, and there is the quality of sweetness and flavor,

children.text: balo jayaśrī na bhaven nareśa itthaṃ pi te ca prabalo janānām // Dak_5.33 //
children.translated_text: so too victory and royal splendor would not come, O lord of men, unless you are mighty over your people."

body.text: punaś ca śṛṇu mahārāja[n] //
body.translated_text: "And listen again, O great king:"

body.text: pāpe pravartate bālo jana

children.translated_text: looking upon [the world as] empty;
in the night of dense darkness, this is the time of sinful deeds."

body.translated_text: "The foolish person engages in sin,

children.translated_text: "But the self-perfected sages of divine vision are always present;

children.text: kva cit kiṃ cana śūnyaṃ vā dikṣu pūrṇās tapodhanaiḥ // Dak_5.35 //
children.translated_text: is anything anywhere empty? The directions are filled with those rich in austerity."

body.text: tatas t

children.translated_text: be one whose self is devoted, O best of rulers of the earth;
it is better to take a begging-bowl [than to] dwell in the house of an enemy."

body.translated_text: "Therefore

children.translated_text: "The evildoer who desires happiness, wherever he goes,

children.text: tatra tatraiva tatpāpair duḥkhaśastrair vihanyate // Dak_5.37 //
children.translated_text: there and everywhere he is struck by the weapons of suffering [arising from] those very sins."
"The desire of those who do good, wherever it goes,
there too it is honored with the reward of those very merits."
"Therefore, one should with effort abandon all accumulation of sin;

children.text: nirjitya dveṣasaṃrambhaṃ śubhe karma samācara // Dak_5.39 //
children.translated_text: having conquered the fury of hatred, practice virtuous deeds."

body.text:
na ca dveṣasamaṃ pāpaṃ na ca kṣāntisamaṃ tapaḥ /
tasmāt kṣāntiṃ prayatnena bhāvaye

children.translated_text: by various means."

body.translated_text: "There is no sin equal to hatred, and no austerity equal to patience; therefore one should cultivate patience with effort

children.text: manaḥ śamaṃ na gṛhṇāti na prītisukham aśnute /
children.translated_text: "The mind does not grasp tranquility, does not enjoy the happiness of affection,

children.text: na nidrāṃ na dhṛtiṃ yāti dveṣaśalye hṛdi sthite // Dak_5.41 //
children.translated_text: does not attain sleep or steadiness when the thorn of hatred is lodged in the heart."

body.text:
na dviṣantaḥ kṣayaṃ yānti durjanā gaganopamāḥ /
mārite krodhacitte tu naśya

children.translated_text: all enemies perish."

body.translated_text: "Enemies do not diminish; the wicked are like the sky [in their vastness]. But when the anger-mind is slain,

children.translated_text: "The creature, by the fire of anger that feeds on the fuel of false imaginings,

children.text: dahaty ātmānam evādau paraṃ dhakṣyati vā na vā // Dak_5.43 //
children.translated_text: burns himself first; whether he will burn the other or not [is uncertain]."

children.text: jarā rūpavatāṃ krodhaḥ tamaś cakṣuṣmatām api /
children.translated_text: "Old age [destroys the beauty] of the beautiful; anger [destroys the light] even of those with eyes;

children.text: vadho dharmārthakāmānāṃ tasmāt krodhaṃ nivārayet // Dak_5.44 //
children.translated_text: it is the slayer of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), and <s>kāma</s> (desire) — therefore one should ward off anger."
"From the doing of the undesired and from the obstruction of the desired —

children.text: krodhaṃ yo hanti nirbandhāt sa sukhīha paratra ca // Dak_5.45 //
children.translated_text: he who destroys the anger born [therefrom] with determination, he is happy here and hereafter."

children.text: tasmād dveṣaṃ vinirjitya cittaṃ rakṣa prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having conquered hatred, guard the mind with effort;

children.text: na śikṣā rakṣituṃ śakyā calaṃ cittam arakṣatā // Dak_5.46 //
children.translated_text: one who does not guard the fickle mind cannot guard [even] learning."

body.text:
adāntā mattamātaṅgā na kurvantīha tāṃ vyathām /
karoti yām avīcyādau mukta

children.translated_text: mind causes in <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell) and elsewhere."

body.translated_text: "Untamed, maddened elephants do not cause as much harm here as the elephant of the unrestrained

children.translated_text: "But if the elephant of the mind is bound on all sides by the rope of mindfulness,

children.text: bhayam astaṃgataṃ sarvaṃ sarvakalyāṇam āgatam // Dak_5.48 //
children.translated_text: all fear is dispelled and all well-being has arrived."

children.text: tasmāc cittaṃ samādhāya smṛtvā rakṣa prayatnataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, having composed the mind, guard it with effort through mindfulness;

children.text: cittād eva hi sarvatra bhayaṃ bhadraṃ ca jāyate // Dak_5.49 //
children.translated_text: for from the mind alone everywhere arises both fear and good fortune."

children.text: cittarakṣāvrataṃ tyaktvā kim anyair bahubhir vrataiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Having abandoned the vow of guarding the mind, what use are many other vows?

children.text: evaṃ buddhvā sadā rājan dharmeṇa pālaya prajāḥ // Dak_5.50 //
children.translated_text: Having thus understood, O king, always govern your subjects with <s>dharma</s>."

body.text: punaś ca mahārāja //
body.translated_text: "And again, O great king:"

children.text: yo 'sau drumo dāmaphalaṃ cinoti na vindati svādu ca hanti bījam /
children.translated_text: "The tree that gathers bondage-fruit, finds no sweetness, and destroys the seed,

children.text: kṣiṇoti deśaṃ karadurvahatvāt dharmaṃ nṛpo vai na ca nandatīti // Dak_5.51 //
children.translated_text: ruins the land through the unbearable burden of taxes — a king does not rejoice in <s>dharma</s> [thus]."

children.text: tasmād anītyā na daṇḍayet prajā nyāyena rājyaṃ pratipālayasva /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, do not punish your subjects unjustly; govern the kingdom with equity.

children.text: nṛpāś ca yeṣāṃ guṇam āvahanti teṣāṃ prajānāṃ pravahanti duḥkham // Dak_5.52 //
children.translated_text: Kings who bring forth [their own] virtues — for those subjects, they carry away suffering."

body.text: punaś ca mahārāja //
body.translated_text: "And again, O great king:"

body.text: svaduḥkhaduḥkhī paraduḥkhato 'pi sukhī svasaukhyaiś ca paraiḥ samāna

children.text: itthaṃ nṛpā ye satataṃ bhavanti rājñāṃ sadā sarvaguṇā bhavanti // Dak_5.53 //
children.translated_text: to others in one's own happiness — kings who are always thus possess all virtues of kings."

body.translated_text: "Suffering at one's own suffering, and also at the suffering of others; equal

children.text: dharmeṇa rājyaṃ paripūrayanti dharmeṇa lakṣmīḥ satataṃ vahanti /
children.translated_text: "They fill the kingdom with <s>dharma</s>; they always bear <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) through <s>dharma</s>;

children.text: dharmeṇa lokān paritarpayanti dharmeṇa kāmān sahasā labhante // Dak_5.54 //
children.translated_text: they satisfy the worlds through <s>dharma</s>; through <s>dharma</s> they swiftly obtain [their] desires."

body.text: punaś ca //
body.translated_text: "And again:"

children.text: dānena bhogā na paropatāpān nājñānamohāt paralokavantaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Enjoyments [come] through giving, not from tormenting others; those who possess the next world [attain it] not through ignorance and delusion.

children.text: parapratāpād yad ihaiva bhogās te prāpnuvante paralokaduḥkhāḥ // Dak_5.55 //
children.translated_text: Those enjoyments [obtained] through tormenting others in this very life — they [who obtain them] attain suffering in the next world."

children.text: ātmā nadī bhārata puṇyatīrthā satyodakā śīlataṭā dayormiḥ /
children.translated_text: "The self is a river, O <s>Bhārata</s>, with merit as its sacred bathing-place, truth as its water, good conduct as its banks, compassion as its waves;

children.text: atrābhiṣekaṃ kurute pravīṇa na vāriṇā śudhyati cāntarātmā // Dak_5.56 //
children.translated_text: the wise man bathes here — the inner self is not purified by [mere] water."

children.text: satyena śaucyaṃ na jalapraveśād dehasya bāhyamalam eva nāśam /
children.translated_text: "Purity [comes] through truth, not from entering water; [water brings] only the destruction of the body's external impurity.

children.text: satyena tiṣṭhanti sadaiva devāḥ sthitiḥ pṛthivyāḥ khalu eva satyaiḥ // Dak_5.57 //
children.translated_text: Through truth the gods always abide; the stability of the earth is indeed through truth."

children.text: śīlena svargā na giriprapātāt śīlena tulyā na bhavanti rakṣāḥ /
children.translated_text: "Through good conduct [one attains] heaven, not from falling off a mountain; no protections are equal to good conduct.

children.text: duḥśīlaśailāt skhalitā manuṣyāḥ patanti duḥkheṣu mahārṇaveṣu // Dak_5.58 //
children.translated_text: Those who slip from the mountain of bad conduct fall into great oceans of suffering."

children.text: jñānena mokṣaṃ na śarīraśoṣāt varṣeṇa ārdraṃ na paraṃ nidāghaiḥ /
children.translated_text: "Through knowledge [one attains] <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation), not from emaciation of the body; [the earth is] moistened by rain, not by extreme heat.

children.text: jñānair vihīnaḥ puruṣaḥ sa eva yathaiva paṅkasya sarassu snātaḥ // Dak_5.59 //
children.translated_text: A person devoid of knowledge is like one who has bathed in a lake of mud."
Having heard this, the lord of kings, with hair standing on end [from wonder], [said:]

children.text: saṃsāre ca mahāghore katham uttārayāmy aham // Dak_5.60 //
children.translated_text: "How shall I be delivered in this greatly terrible <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence)?"
Then that lord among kings, with fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

children.text: prasanno bhagavati buddhe cakāra śaraṇaṃ punaḥ // Dak_5.61 //
children.translated_text: pleased with the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, again took refuge [in him].

children.text: bhagavan buddha vīreśa śrutvā me rocate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, lord of heroes, having heard [your teaching], my mind delights;

children.text: saṃbodhau vyākaroṣi tvaṃ yācayāmīty ahaṃ prabho // Dak_5.62 //
children.translated_text: do you prophesy [me] for <s>saṃbodhi</s> (supreme enlightenment) — this I request, O lord."

children.text: atha śrībhagavāñ chāstā jñātvā tasyāśayaṃ śubham /
children.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Teacher, knowing his wholesome intention,
prophesied without delay: "You shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s>.
An <s>Arhat</s> named <s>Ratnākara</s>, a fully enlightened <s>Buddha</s>, a leader of the world,
a king of <s>dharma</s>, a lord of the world, omniscient, an <s>Arhat</s>, a lord among sages —
you shall become a master of all sciences, a teacher, a mine of virtues.

children.text: buddhakāryaṃ tataḥ kṛtvā dīrghakālaṃ ca sthāsyati // Dak_5.65 //
children.translated_text: Then, having accomplished the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, [the teaching] shall endure for a long time."

body.text: atha sa bhūpatīndreśa

children.text: tasya satyāśiṣaṃ pratigrāhyādau praṇamya pramodād gamisyāmīty ārocya vimānam āruhya ṛddhyā labdhalābha iva vaṇik svagṛhaṃ prākramat śrīsvam eva rājyam //
children.translated_text: having received his true blessing, first bowed, announced joyfully 'I shall depart,' mounted his aerial chariot, and like a merchant who has obtained his profit through supernatural power, proceeded to his own dwelling — his own kingdom.

body.translated_text: Then that lord among kings

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ puṇyakāma

children.translated_text: story,
the fifth
chapter.

body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the <s>Puṇyakāma</s>

body.text: VI. jīrṇoddhāraṇabimbakathā
body.translated_text: VI. The Story of the Restoration of the Ruined Image

body.text: tataḥ kautūhalajātā bhikṣavo bhagavantam etad avocat //
body.translated_text: Then the monks, filled with curiosity, said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: bhagavan kena puṇyena kuśalena ca karmaṇā /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, by what merit and wholesome deed
is that king so exceedingly handsome, beautiful and captivating to behold?"
"Of what city is such an excellent form of a man,
endowed with the fullness of beauty, difficult to obtain even for a god?"

body.text: bhagavan āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.translated_text: "O monks, that king shines with the splendor of great merit;

children.text: vaiśālyāś ca nagaryāś ca ratnavyūho nṛpottamaḥ // Dak_6.3 //
children.translated_text: he is <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the best of kings, of the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>."

children.text: nagarī kīdṛśī syāc ca ṛddhā sphītamanoramā /
children.translated_text: "What kind of city would it be? Prosperous, thriving, and delightful,

children.text: subhikṣā ramaṇīyā ca sujanaiḥ kovidair vṛtā // Dak_6.4 //
children.translated_text: well-provisioned, charming, filled with good people and learned ones,
sixteen <s>yojanas</s> in length and breadth likewise,
endowed with various festivals, far removed from wicked people."

children.text: yathā paurajanacittaṃ tathā rājñaḥ samaṃ manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "The mind of the townspeople was in accord with the king's mind;
endowed with extensive gardens, beautifully adorned with lotus pools;

body.text: pārśve tu vāditā eva pakṣiṇo bhṛṅganisvanaiḥ // Dak_6.6 //
body.translated_text: on its sides, music was played, and birds [sang] with the sounds of bees."

body.text: mahiṣī tasya saṃpannā śubhavyūha

children.translated_text: was his son,
beautiful, handsome, and lovely as <s>Puṣpadhanvan</s> (Kāmadeva, the god of love)."

body.translated_text: "His queen was accomplished; <s>Śubhavyūha</s>

children.translated_text: "He obtained all royal splendor together with its attendant services;
accomplished in the science of archery, well-versed in the knowledge of the <s>śāstras</s> (scriptures)."
"Endowed with great supernatural power and strength, equal in splendor to a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal monarch);

children.text: śāstrāgamavidhijñaś ca kṛtakṛtyaḥ sa vijñavān // Dak_6.9 //
children.translated_text: knower of the procedures of scriptures and traditions, he was accomplished and wise."
"Such a jewel among kings, powerful in all the world,
obtained such fruit through previous wholesome deeds."

body.text: maitreya uvāca // bhagavann aparaṃ kena kuśalamūlena samanvāgataḥ sa rājā īdṛśo vibhūtir āsīt kena karmaṇeti //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> said: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, by what other root of wholesome merit was that king endowed with such magnificence? By what deed?"

body.text: bhagavān āha // maitreya śṛṇu /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "O <s>Maitreya</s>, listen:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ sa maitreya pūrvajanma

children.translated_text: he was a boatman;

children.text: nityaṃ samudratīreṣu vasati nāvikaḥ sa ca // Dak_6.11 //
children.translated_text: that boatman always dwelt on the shores of the ocean."

body.translated_text: "In former times, O <s>Maitreya</s>, in a previous birth

children.text: nāgatā vaṇijaḥ ke cit tasya durdaivayogataḥ /
children.translated_text: "No merchants came, due to his ill fortune;

children.text: tasmād duḥkhī mahākaṣṭī tarapaṇyaṃ grahaṇaṃ na hi // Dak_6.12 //
children.translated_text: therefore, greatly suffering and distressed, there was no obtaining of ferry-toll."

children.text: atha sa cintayām āsa hā hā karma mamādhunā /
children.translated_text: "Then he thought: 'Alas, alas, what is my fate now?

children.text: kiṃ kartavyam idānīṃ me na prāptam annam ādikam // Dak_6.13 //
children.translated_text: What shall I do now? I have not obtained even food and the like.'"

children.text: kasyāpi īdṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ mā bhavatu kadā cana /
children.translated_text: "'May such suffering never befall anyone!'

children.text: ity evaṃ manasā cintya jinaṃ smaran sa tiṣṭhati // Dak_6.14 //
children.translated_text: Thus thinking in his mind, remembering the <s>Jina</s> (the Victor), he remained."

children.text: tataḥ sa nāvikas tatra sthātuṃ na ramate manaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Then that boatman's mind did not delight in remaining there;

children.text: tasmāt samudratīrād anucaṅkramyamāne kasmiṃś cit sthāne
children.translated_text: so, wandering from that seashore, at a certain place
he beheld a single <s>caitya</s> (shrine) — a ruined and not very large <s>stūpa</s> containing relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>."

body.text: taṃ caityaṃ gopālakāḥ krīḍayā pāṣāṇeṣṭakācarcitabhagnitā

children.translated_text: seeing the interior of the <s>caitya</s>, he reflected and said:"

body.translated_text: "That <s>caitya</s>, [damaged by] cowherds who in their play had pelted it with stones and bricks, broken —

children.text: kena pāpātmanā yena caityabhaṅgaṃ ca yat kṛtam /
children.translated_text: "'By what sinful soul was this breaking of the <s>caitya</s> done?

children.text: aśobhanam idaṃ caityaṃ saṃskāraṃ kriyate mayā // Dak_6.15 //
children.translated_text: This <s>caitya</s> is unsightly; restoration shall be done by me.'"

children.text: tat saṃskāraṃ kṛtaṃ tena yatra bhagnādi tatra ca /
children.translated_text: "That restoration was done by him wherever there was breakage and the like;
in the places that were crumbled and damaged, with stone and brick —

body.text: nāvika iti kṛtvā ca pūrvavac chobhanaṃ kṛtam // Dak_6.16 //
body.translated_text: the boatman, having done this, made it beautiful as before."

children.text: atha buddhaprabhāvena tasmin kāle ca tatra ye /
children.translated_text: "Then, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, at that time and place,
three hundred merchants with their goods came to his presence."
"Accompanied by a caravan leader, for the crossing of the river,

children.text: vaṇijas te tam āhūya cainam ūcur vaṇigjanāḥ // Dak_6.18 //
children.translated_text: those merchants summoned him and the merchant-folk said to him:"

children.text: bho nāvika vayaṃ ratnadvīpaṃ gacchāmaḥ sarvathā /
children.translated_text: "'O boatman, we are going to the jewel-island by all means;

children.text: bhavān netātra saṃvīkṣya samudrāt pālayatv ataḥ // Dak_6.19 //
children.translated_text: you be the guide here; having surveyed the sea, protect [us] henceforth.'"

body.text: ity ākarṇya sa dhīvaro dhīra āyavyayaṃ cābhivīkṣya vahanaṃ teṣāṃ purataḥ samāropyāha //
body.translated_text: Having heard this, that fisherman, being wise, having examined the income and expenditure, loaded their cargo in front and said:

children.translated_text: You should now remain steady on the vessels.

children.text: svadevatāṃ smṛtvā dhairyam ālambya dṛdhaṃ nivāsata // Dak_6.20 //
children.translated_text: Remembering your own deity, take courage and stay firm.

body.text: te tatheti kṛtvā trayaḥśata vāṇijā vahanaṃ praṇamya ca samudraṃ saṃprārthya vahanam āruhya krameṇa saṃtartum ārabdhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Saying 'so be it,' the three hundred merchants, bowing to the vessel and praying to the ocean, boarded the vessel and began to cross gradually.

body.text: tadā pramuditamānasāḥ sarve ca te vaṇijo mahotsāhaṃ pramodavanta

children.translated_text: [thought:] 'Surely our excellent voyage will be successful!'

body.translated_text: Then all those merchants, with delighted hearts, full of great enthusiasm and joy,

body.text: tataḥ krameṇa cāva

children.text: gāhire vividhamīnakulavicaritataraṅgaphenāvalīagāḍhataraṃ samudraṃ nīlaṃ vimalakhaḍgābhinīlam iva vigatameghaṃ sūryāṃśutāpād iva khaṃ vilīnaṃ samantato 'ntarhitatīralekham agādham ambhonidhimadhyaṃ krameṇa prāptāḥ // tadā sāyāhnasamayam abhūt, tīraṃ prāptuṃ sudurlabham /
children.translated_text: entered the deep ocean — teeming with various fish and sea-creatures, its waves crested with lines of foam, deep and unfathomable — dark blue like an unsheathed sword, cloudless as if the sky had dissolved from the heat of the sun's rays, with the shoreline hidden on all sides — and gradually reached the middle of the fathomless waters. Then it became evening time, and reaching shore became extremely difficult.

body.translated_text: Then gradually they

body.text: mṛdukiraṇasavitari kāle, mahotpātaṃ paramabhīṣaṇaṃ garutmadāśīviṣabhīmam ullolam abhūt //
body.translated_text: When the sun had gentle rays, at that time a great portent arose — supremely terrifying, dreadful as <s>Garuḍa</s> and serpents, with turbulent waves.

children.translated_text: The foam was scattered by the splitting waves, the terrible roaring was caused by the lashing of fierce winds,

children.text: utpātavātākalitair mahadbhir yugāntakālam iva saṃkaṭo 'bhūt // Dak_6.21 //
children.translated_text: and with the great [waves] churned up by the storm winds, it became a crisis as if at the end of an age.

body.text: vidyullatodbhāsuralolajihvā nīlā bhujaṃgā iva naikaśīrṣā
body.translated_text: The clouds, with flickering tongues blazing like lightning-streaks, dark like many-headed serpents,

body.text: āvavrur ādityapathaṃ payodāḥ prasaktabhīmastanitānunādāḥ // Dak_6.22 //
body.translated_text: covered the path of the sun, with continuous and terrifying thunder resounding.

body.text: tataḥ sa nāvikaḥ te vāṇijā

children.text: svajīve nirāśino bhayavihvalāṃś cābhivīkṣya dhairyam avalambya tān uvāca // avadhīr
children.translated_text: despairing of their lives and trembling with fear, took courage and said to them: 'Be patient!
