When this was said, that <s>Maitreya</s>, with his hair-pores bristling with joy, spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'I am awakened, O Blessed One! I am awakened, O <s>Sugata</s>! Such [suffering] has been experienced by one who delights in such sin!'

body.text: bhagavān āha // yeṣāṃ manuṣyāṇām ihaiva saṃsāre yataś cyutvā mātuḥ kukṣāv upapanna

children.text: sā mātā daśamāsaparyantaṃ dhṛtvā kaṣṭena prasūtā stanyapānena pratipālayati / īdṛśīmātari apakārakṛte duṣkarakṛtair na ca mucyate //
children.translated_text: That mother, having carried [the child] for ten months, gives birth with difficulty and nourishes [the child] with breast-milk. When harm is done to such a mother, one is not freed even by performing difficult austerities.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'For those human beings, in this very <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), having fallen from wherever, they are conceived in the mother's womb.

body.text: atha punar api bhagavān āha // maitreya ratnavyūho nāma bhūpāla

children.text: paramapuṇyavān sa punar api kasmiṃś cid dine cintayām āsa //
children.translated_text: supremely meritorious, one day again reflected thus:

body.translated_text: Then again the Blessed One said: '<s>Maitreya</s>, the king named <s>Ratnavyūha</s>,

children.text: ahaṃ vṛddho 'tijīrṇāṅgaḥ sthāsyāmy eva kiyac ciram /
children.translated_text: 'I am old, with thoroughly aged limbs — how long shall I remain?

children.text: avaśyaṃ daivayogena yāsyāmi maraṇaṃ dhruvam // Dak_6.44 //
children.translated_text: Surely, by the force of fate, I shall inevitably go to death.'

body.text: sarvam anarthaṃ rājyaṃ viṣayopabhogyaṃ mahāghorabhayakaraṃ mṛtyusarpabhayākulam anityam asārakam iti vicintyāgāra adhyāvasituṃ mano na ramate // tadā sa rājaputraṃ śubhavyūhaṃ ca mantriṇaṃ samāmantryaivam āha //
body.translated_text: 'All this kingdom is purposeless, the enjoyment of sense-objects is terrifyingly fearful, agitated by the fear of the serpent of death, impermanent, and without essence' — having reflected thus, his mind did not delight in dwelling at home. Then, summoning his prince <s>Śubhavyūha</s> and the minister, he spoke thus:

body.text: putra śubhavyūha
body.translated_text: 'Son <s>Śubhavyūha</s>!

children.translated_text: I here am assailed by old age, surely with worn-out faculties.

children.text: tadā rogābhibhūto 'pi vrajeyaṃ maraṇaṃ dhruvam // Dak_6.45 //
children.translated_text: Then, even overcome by disease, I shall certainly go to death.

children.text: tat pravrajitum icchāmi śreyaḥ ślāghyena vartmanā /
children.translated_text: Therefore, I wish to renounce — it is better on the praiseworthy path,

children.text: purā mṛtyū ripuṃ hanti gṛhasaṃraktam eva vā // Dak_6.46 //
children.translated_text: before the enemy death strikes one who is attached to household life.
Therefore, fearful of <s>saṃsāra</s>, with many apprehensions of danger,

children.text: nātra sthātuṃ mano ramya gacchāmi buddham āśrayam // Dak_6.47 //
children.translated_text: my mind does not delight in staying here — I shall go to the refuge of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: bho putra śubhavyūha mama pūrvapuṇyānubhāvena gautamena śauddhodanena mahyaṃ vyākaroti / acireṇa tathāgato bhaviṣyasi tena prabodhitaḥ / aham eva buddho bhaveyamm, paścimāyāṃ campakavarṇāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetram ekam asti

children.translated_text: 'I shall go there.'

body.translated_text: O son <s>Śubhavyūha</s>, by the power of my former merit, <s>Gautama</s> <s>Śauddhodana</s> (son of <s>Śuddhodana</s>) has prophesied for me: 'You will soon become a <s>Tathāgata</s>' — awakened by him. I myself shall become a <s>Buddha</s>. In the western world-system of campaka-color, there is one <s>Buddha</s>-field.',

body.text:
tasmān mayā yathā proktaṃ tathā caritum arhasi /
prajānāṃ pālanaṃ kṛtvā dharmanītyā

children.translated_text: the way of <s>Dharma</s> (righteousness).

body.translated_text: 'Therefore, you should conduct yourself as I have instructed. Having governed the people, practice

children.text: lokān mā khedayet tāpaiḥ kuladharme samācara /
children.translated_text: Do not afflict the people with torments; practice the family <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: pareṣv api dayāyuktair dānaṃ hi śraddhayā kuru // Dak_6.49 //
children.translated_text: With compassion even toward others, give charity with faith.
Do not commit killing, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, and the like.

children.text: mā mṛṣāvādapaiśunyaṃ pāruṣyaṃ bhinnam eva ca // Dak_6.50 //
children.translated_text: Do not commit false speech, slander, harsh speech, or divisive speech.
Abandon the faults of covetousness, malice, and wrong views.

children.text: etāni tāni sarvāni dhāraya dṛḍhacetasā // Dak_6.51 //
children.translated_text: Hold all these firmly with a steadfast mind.

children.text: pāpānāṃ mūla eṣo hi sugateneti deśitaḥ /
children.translated_text: For this is the root of all sins, as taught by the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One).

children.text: itthaṃ kṛte 'pi nṛpater ītir na ca bhaviṣyati // Dak_6.52 //
children.translated_text: If done thus, there shall be no calamity for the king.'
'From today onward, you are the sovereign lord of all the people,
the instructor of all <s>dharmas</s>, and the bearer of the welfare of all beings.'

body.text: tat kasmād dhetoḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason?

body.text: dharmeṇa vardhate rāj

children.translated_text: prospers; by <s>dharma</s>, wealth increases.
By <s>dharma</s>, wealth is accomplished; by <s>dharma</s>, desires are fulfilled.

children.text: kāmasiddhena mokṣaṃ ca prāpyate nātra saṃśayaḥ // Dak_6.54 //
children.translated_text: And through fulfilled desires, liberation is attained — there is no doubt about this.'

body.translated_text: 'By <s>dharma</s>, the kingdom

children.translated_text: With this path of knowledge, the king instructed his son,

children.text: jñānāṅkuśabhayenaiva kuñcitaḥ sa gajo yathā // Dak_6.55 //
children.translated_text: who was curbed like an elephant by the goad-like fear of knowledge.

children.text: nanāma pitaraṃ tena śrutvā vākyaṃ vaco'mṛtam /
children.translated_text: He bowed to his father, having heard the nectar-like words.

children.text: dhṛtvājñāte yathā tāta prajānāṃ pratipālane // Dak_6.56 //
children.translated_text: 'I shall uphold your command, O father, in the governance of the people.'

children.text: iti praśāsya tato bhūpo ratnavyūho mahāmatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, having instructed, the king <s>Ratnavyūha</s>, the greatly wise,

children.text: prabodhya putrapatnyādīn buddhakṣetraṃ yayau mudā // Dak_6.57 //
children.translated_text: having awakened his son, wives, and others, joyfully went to the <s>Buddha</s>-field.

body.text:
śṛṇu maitreya punar bhūpamārgāṇāṃ gamanakathām /
dadarśa bhūpatir jīrṇapraṇālī

children.translated_text: water-channel.

body.translated_text: Listen, <s>Maitreya</s>, again to the story of the king's journey along the roads. The king, travelling along the road, saw a decayed

children.translated_text: Water was not flowing [before], but upon his seeing it, it flowed.

children.text: prāk na pravāhitaṃ kena, idānīṃ tu pravāhitam // Dak_6.59 //
children.translated_text: 'Previously it was not flowing — by whom? But now it flows!'

children.text: āścaryeti sthite bhūpa ākāśād enam ūcivān /
children.translated_text: While the king stood amazed, a voice from the sky spoke to him:

children.text: puṇyavāṃs tvaṃ mahārāja tvatprabhāvāt pravāhitam // Dak_6.60 //
children.translated_text: 'You are meritorious, O great king! By your influence, it has begun to flow.
This water-channel was broken, surely from within.

children.text: tvaṃ tu dharmatanur evaṃ jānīhi kila bhūpate // Dak_6.61 //
children.translated_text: But you are an embodiment of <s>dharma</s> — know this, O king!'

body.text: rājovāca // na jñāto 'ham eva ca //
body.translated_text: The king said: 'I did not know this at all.'

children.translated_text: Then the king proceeded to a great forest tract.
There he arrived and saw trees bearing fruits and flowers.

body.text: tadanyavṛkṣa eka

children.translated_text: stood with its root uprooted.
Merely by the king's seeing it, it rose up and came back as before.

body.translated_text: Among them, one tree

children.translated_text: Then a voice from the sky said to him: 'You are praiseworthy, O king!

children.text: pādapo 'yam acaitanya utthitaḥ san hi cāgataḥ // Dak_6.64 //
children.translated_text: This tree, though unconscious, has risen and come [back to life].'

body.text: rājovāca // na jñāto 'ham eva tu //
body.translated_text: The king said: 'I did not know this at all.'

children.translated_text: Then, on the roads, three <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> came.
Afflicted with leprosy, blind, always of unhealthy bodies.

children.text: tān dṛṣṭvā sa ca bhūpālo vicāryainān apṛcchata /
children.translated_text: Seeing them, the king, having reflected, asked them:

children.text: brāhmaṇāḥ kutra gantāraḥ katamabhūmyā ihāgatāḥ // Dak_6.66 //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, where are you going? From which land have you come here?'

body.text: brāhmaṇā ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> said:

children.translated_text: 'Is it well with you, O great king renowned as <s>Ratnavyūha</s>?

children.text: nānyat tu kāryam asmākaṃ gacchāmas tatra rājani // Dak_6.67 //
children.translated_text: We have no other business — we are going there, O king.'
Merely by the king seeing them, the blind ones obtained eyes,

children.text: śubhāṅgā bhavanti puṣṭāṅgā muñcanti pāparāśayaḥ // Dak_6.68 //
children.translated_text: they became beautiful-limbed and well-nourished, freed from the mass of sins.

body.text: tataḥ sakhā brāhmaṇa uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then a companion <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> said:

children.translated_text: 'Ah, what a wonder I have experienced! O friend, by what cause?

children.text: cakṣurvihīnena punaś cakṣuḥ prāptaṃ tvayādhunā // Dak_6.69 //
children.translated_text: You, who were without eyes, have now again obtained sight.
You, who were afflicted with leprosy in every limb, have again become beautiful-limbed.
Merely by being seen by this man, [your afflictions] are released.

children.text: sakhe tathā vikārāṅgaḥ śubhāṅgo bhūyate 'dya hi // Dak_6.70 //
children.translated_text: O friend, you who had deformed limbs have today become beautiful-limbed indeed.
Now let us approach and ask him, O friend.

children.text: hetubhūtam ayaṃ sa tvaṃ na ca prādeśikaḥ pumān // Dak_6.71 //
children.translated_text: You are the cause of this — you are no ordinary man.

children.text: kasmād āgatas tvaṃ bho bhavan kiṃ puruṣarṣabhaḥ /
children.translated_text: From where have you come, O sir? What kind of excellent man are you?
You are one whose self is enriched by merit, brilliant with splendors.'

body.text: rājovāca //
body.translated_text: The king said:

body.text: brāhmaṇā

children.translated_text: do you not know the one renowned as <s>Ratnavyūha</s>?

children.text: katham itthām ahaṃ bhadra tatra gacchāmi sāṃpratam // Dak_6.73 //
children.translated_text: How shall I, O good sirs, go there now?'

body.translated_text: 'O <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,

body.text: tadā brāhmaṇāḥ prītipramodyasaumanasyajātās tasmai rājñe āśīrvāṇīm abruvan //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, filled with joy, delight, and gladness, spoke a blessing to that king:

children.text: jayo bhavatu bhūpendra tvayā yan manasepsitam /
children.translated_text: 'May you be victorious, O lord of kings! Whatever is desired in your mind,

children.text: tat sarvaṃ prāptam astv īti puṇyaśriyāsuśobhana // Dak_6.74 //
children.translated_text: may all that be attained — O one beautiful with the splendor of merit!'

body.text: brāhmaṇās tathāstu me, ity uktvā sa satkāraviśeṣaiḥ pūjayitvā visarjayati sma // tato brāhmaṇāḥ prasādapratilabdhāḥ svam āśramaṃ prakrāntā abhūvan // maitreya āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> [said] 'so be it to me' — having said this, he honored them with special hospitality and dismissed them. Then the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, having obtained [his] grace, departed to their own hermitage. <s>Maitreya</s> said:

children.text: kena pāpair bhavet kāṇaḥ kuṣṭhāviṣṭaḥ kathaṃ bhavet /
children.translated_text: 'By what sins does one become one-eyed? How does one become afflicted with leprosy?

children.text: itthaṃbhūtadvijāpyaiva, aho kaṣṭaṃ narasya ca // Dak_6.75 //
children.translated_text: Even a twice-born one can become such — alas, how terrible for a man!'

body.text: maitreyeṇa tathā pṛṣṭo bhagavān āha taṃ punaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus asked by <s>Maitreya</s>, the Blessed One again said to him:

children.text: dṛṣṭam adṛṣṭam uktaṃ te mithyayā śapathaṃ kṛtam /
children.translated_text: 'Having seen the unseen and declared it [falsely], taking a false oath —

children.text: cakṣuhīno 'bhavat tena svārthī na parakāryakṛt // Dak_6.76 //
children.translated_text: by that, he became devoid of eyes; selfish, not acting for others' benefit.
Having stolen wealth in the king's service, the twice-born was made a treasurer.

children.text: kiṃ cid dattvā parasyaiva svagṛhe nīyate punaḥ // Dak_6.77 //
children.translated_text: Having given something [small] to another, he would take [it back] to his own house.
By the ripening of that <s>karma</s>, the twice-born became a leper in body.

children.text: yat kṛtaṃ karma pākena tatphalam aśnute tathā // Dak_6.78 //
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>karma</s> is done, its fruit is experienced through ripening accordingly.'

body.text: maitreya uvāca // prabuddho 'haṃ bhagavan prabuddho 'haṃ sugata //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'I am awakened, O Blessed One! I am awakened, O <s>Sugata</s>!'

body.text: atha sa rājā campakavarṇāyāṃ lokadhātau buddhakṣetraṃ prāptavān / tatra buddhakṣetre vimalaprabhā nāma caitya

children.text: manoramadarśanīyaprāsādikaṃ dṛṣṭvā paramaprītamanās tasyāśramam upāśritavān // paryaṅkam ābhu
children.translated_text: charming and delightful to behold, with his mind supremely pleased, he took shelter in that hermitage. Having assumed

children.text: ya, ṛjukāyaṃ praṇidhāya dhyānārāme sthitaḥ / tatas tatkṣaṇaṃ pañcābhijñatvaṃ prāptah, krameṇa ratnākaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan prāpto 'bhūt //
children.translated_text: the cross-legged posture, having straightened his body, established in the garden of meditation — then, at that very moment, he attained the five <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and in due course became the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Come One), the <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One) named <s>Ratnākara</s> (Jewel-Mine).

body.translated_text: Then that king reached the <s>Buddha</s>-field in the world-system of campaka-color. There, in that <s>Buddha</s>-field, having seen a <s>caitya</s> (shrine) named <s>Vimalaprabhā</s> (Pure Radiance),

body.text: maitreya uvāca // bhagavamṣ tathāgatadhātustūpajīrṇoddhāraṇānāṃ kīdṛśaṃ phalam //
body.translated_text: <s>Maitreya</s> said: 'O Blessed One, what is the fruit of restoring decayed <s>stūpas</s> (reliquary mounds) containing the relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>?'

body.text: tathāgatastūpabiṃbānāṃ sthāpanānāṃ yataḥ katham
body.translated_text: 'The establishment of <s>stūpas</s> and images of the <s>Tathāgata</s> —

body.text: kīdṛśaṃ syāt phalaṃ teṣāṃ tat sarvaṃ deśaya prabho // Dak_6.79 //
body.translated_text: what fruit would there be for those? Teach all that, O Lord!'

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

body.text: āḍhyo nirnaṣṭaśokaḥ kṣatasakalakali

children.translated_text: destroyed, a vessel of delight for the eyes,
a treasury of good fortune and splendor, with accumulated strength, with a beautiful body, renowned,
radiant, of beautiful form, skilled in discourse, with all faculties and limbs subdued,

children.text: 'vyagro dhīmān pradātā bhavati bhagavato buddhabimbaṃ vidhāya // Dak_6.80 //
children.translated_text: undistracted, wise, generous — one becomes [all this] by fashioning an image of the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>.

body.translated_text: 'Wealthy, free from sorrow, with all afflictions

children.text: yāvantaḥ paramāṇavo bhagavataḥ stūpeṣu bimbeṣu vā
children.translated_text: As many atoms as there are in the <s>stūpas</s> or images of the Blessed One,

children.text: tatkartur divi bhūtale ca niyataṃ tāvanti rājyāny api /
children.translated_text: that many kingdoms, certainly, in heaven and on earth, does the maker [enjoy].

children.text: rūpārūpyasamādhisaṃpad akhilaṃ bhuktvā ca sarvaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the complete attainment of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption) of the form and formless [realms], and all happiness,

children.text: ante janmajarāvipattirahitaṃ prāpnoti bauddhaṃ padam // Dak_6.81 //
children.translated_text: in the end one attains the state of the <s>Buddha</s>, free from birth, old age, and calamity.

body.text:
dvātriṃśatā bhūṣitacārugātraḥ sallakṣaṇair lakṣitacakravartī /
bhavej jino

children.text: nte jitadoṣaśatrus tāthāgatīṃ yaḥ pratimāṃ vidhatte // Dak_6.82 //
children.translated_text: at the end, having conquered the enemy of faults — one who establishes an image of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.translated_text: With a beautiful body adorned with the thirty-two [marks], marked as a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign) with the excellent marks, one becomes a <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)

children.translated_text: Completeness of the sense-organs, distance from the states of womanhood and misfortune,

children.text: janma mānuṣyakaṃ vaṃśa uccair ādeyavākyatā // Dak_6.83 //
children.translated_text: human birth, high lineage, words that are heeded,

body.text: jāti

children.translated_text: learning, memory, firmness, desired prosperity,

children.text: sthāneṣv abhiniveśaś ca rāgādibhir abādhanā // Dak_6.84 //
children.translated_text: devotion to [holy] places, and non-affliction by passion and the like —

body.translated_text: birth

children.translated_text: these excellent qualities, approved by the virtuous, arise

children.text: vidhāya buddhapratimāṃ stūpaṃ vā prāṇināṃ mudā // Dak_6.85 //
children.translated_text: from establishing a <s>Buddha</s>-image or a <s>stūpa</s> for the joy of beings.

children.text: na yāti dāsyaṃ na daridrabhāvaṃ na preṣyatāṃ nāpi ca hīnajanma /
children.translated_text: One does not go to servitude, nor to the state of poverty, nor to the state of a servant, nor to a low birth,

children.text: na cāpi vaikalyam ihendriyāṇāṃ yo lokanāthapratimāṃ karoti // Dak_6.86 //
children.translated_text: nor to deficiency of the sense-organs here — one who makes an image of the Lord of the World.
This merit, briefly, should be known regarding <s>caitya</s>-work.

children.text: na śakyate jinaiḥ sarvair vaktuṃ sarvaṃ mayā katham // Dak_6.87 //
children.translated_text: It cannot be fully spoken by all the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors) — how then by me?'

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ jīrṇoddhāraṇabimbakathā ṣaṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story of restoring [decayed stūpas] and [making] images — the sixth chapter.

body.text: VII. snānakathā
body.translated_text: VII. The Story of Bathing

children.translated_text: Then <s>Maitreya</s> spoke to the Blessed One:

children.text: caityānāṃ buddhabimbānāṃ snānānāṃ kathyatāṃ phalam // Dak_7.1 //
children.translated_text: Tell the fruit of bathing <s>caityas</s> (shrines) and <s>Buddha</s> images.

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) spoke:

children.text: ajita śṛṇu maitreya snānasya phalam uttamam /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Ajita</s>, O <s>Maitreya</s>, hear the supreme fruit of bathing
<s>caityas</s> and <s>Buddha</s> images — I shall declare it for the benefit of the world.
He who bathes the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One) with various fragrant perfumes, and performs worship with flowers, incense, body-ointments,

children.text: yo vā pūjaṃ karoti pramuditamanasā śravyavāditraśabdaiḥ /
children.translated_text: with a delighted mind, with pleasing musical sounds —
in the <s>Mandākinī</s> (celestial river), swelling with pollen-dust of golden lotuses,

children.text: vyāptāyāṃ snāti so 'nte sakalakalimalakṣālito yānti mokṣam // Dak_7.3 //
children.translated_text: pervaded [by fragrance] — he bathes at the end, cleansed of all the stains of the <s>Kali</s> age, and attains liberation.
In [that <s>Mandākinī</s>], agitated by the striking of the full, high breasts and buttocks of divine women,
exhaling the fragrant nectar dripping from swelling golden lotuses,

children.text: mandākinyāṃ suraughāḥ pratidinam udakakrīḍayā yad ramante
children.translated_text: in that <s>Mandākinī</s>, the hosts of gods daily sport in water-play —
this is the fruit of bathing the Lord <s>Buddha</s> with waters of various fragrances.

body.text: evaṃ maitreya mahānuśaṃsā tathāgateṣu kṛtapuṇyāni svalpam api bahu phalam //
body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Maitreya</s>, the merits performed toward the <s>Tathāgatas</s> (Thus-Gone Ones) have great benefits — even a small [merit] yields great fruit."

body.text: atha tasmin samaye bhagavān sarvasabhāśritalokānāṃ kāṅkṣācchedanārtham ūrṇākośād bhrūvivarāntarād divyāṃ prabhām utsasarja / tayā prabhayā trisāhasralokadhātum avabhāsya yāvad bhavāgraparyantam avabhāsayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then at that time, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, for the purpose of cutting the doubts of the people present in the entire assembly, emitted a divine radiance from the <s>ūrṇākośa</s> (tuft of hair between the brows). By that radiance, having illuminated the trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasralokadhātu</s>), he illuminated up to the summit of existence (<s>bhavāgra</s>).

body.text: tatraikapradeśe dharmakośavatīmahānagaryāṃ dharmamatir nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati sma // sa ca mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaparivāro dhanadhānyasaṃpanno gṛhakṣetra-udyānadāsadāsīpreṣakajanasaṃpannaḥ / tatas tayā prabhayā sarvāvantaṃ gṛhaṃ bāhyābhyantaram avabhāsitam / tatas tayā prabhayā tasya śarīraṃ spṛṣṭvā, prahlāditamanā

children.translated_text: he spoke:

body.translated_text: In a certain place, in the great city called <s>Dharmakośavatī</s>, there dwelt a merchant named <s>Dharmamati</s>. He was of great wealth, great enjoyment, with an extensive retinue, endowed with riches and grain, furnished with houses, fields, gardens, male and female servants, and attendants. Then, by that radiance, his entire house, inside and out, was illuminated. Then, when that radiance touched his body, with a gladdened mind,

body.text: aho kasya prabhāva eṣa na bhūto na bhaviṣyati, hetubhūtaṃ kaṃ pṛccheyam // ity uktvā tūṣṇīm abhūt //
body.translated_text: "Ah, whose is this splendor? — such has never been nor shall be! Whom, who is the cause, should I ask?" Having said this, he fell silent.

body.text: tato bhagavato raśmijālaprabhayā gāthām abhāṣata //
body.translated_text: Then, by the radiance of the net of rays of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, a verse was spoken:

children.text: prabhāvaviṣaye hy eṣa buddhasya ca jagadguroḥ /
children.translated_text: "This is within the domain of the splendor of the <s>Buddha</s>, the teacher of the world;

children.text: tasmāt sarvaprayatnena buddhe bhaktikriyāṃ kuru // Dak_7.5 //
children.translated_text: therefore, with all effort, perform acts of devotion to the <s>Buddha</s>.
Know the <s>Buddha</s> as the granter of liberation to beings,
the liberator from the net of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) of those submerged in the ocean of existence.
The refuge of the destitute, the destroyer of disease and sorrow,
the deliverer of all beings from the ocean of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)."

body.text: ity uktvāntarhito 'bhūt // atha sa dharmamatiḥ śreṣṭhī buddhe bhagavati prasannapramodyajātena pūjāpuraḥsareṇa puṣpadhūpādinā pūjārghaṃ dattvā puṣpāñjaliṃ bhagavate prakṣiptavān // tato buddhānubhāvena sarvapuṣpāṇi puṣpamaṇḍapa iva tasthuḥ / dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavat saṃsthitaḥ sitanīlapītaharitāruṇacitra iva śirasi samalaṃkṛto 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, [the voice] disappeared. Then that merchant <s>Dharmamati</s>, with faith and joy arisen toward the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, preceded by worship, having offered worship-offerings with flowers, incense, and the like, cast a handful of flowers toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, all the flowers stood like a flower-pavilion. The incense remained like a mass of clouds — adorned upon [the Buddha's] head, appearing as if white, blue, yellow, green, and red.

body.text: atha sa śreṣṭhī buddhe bhagavati cittaṃ prasādya namaskāraṃ kṛtvā buddham anusmaran sukhena tiṣṭhati // tatas tasya śreṣṭhina alpāyutvāt kālaṃ gatvā tasya puṇyaprabhāvena trāyatriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ // tato divyastrībhiḥ saha mandākinyāṃ snātvā sukhalīlayā tiṣṭhati // tataḥ svapuṇyavipākena ratnakūṭāgāre niṣadya svargaṃ svargād bhramati ramitvā krīḍitvā kramataś ca sa ratnamatīti khyātavān // tataś ca śakro devānām indraḥ sudharmāyāṃ devasabhāyāṃ buddhasya varṇaṃ bhāsantaṃ taṃ dadarśa //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant, having generated faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, making obeisance, recollecting the <s>Buddha</s>, dwelt in happiness. Then, that merchant, being of short lifespan, upon dying, by the power of his merit was reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods. Then, having bathed in the <s>Mandākinī</s> together with divine women, he lived in blissful play. Then, by the ripening of his own merit, sitting in a jeweled mansion, he roamed from heaven to heaven, having enjoyed and played — and he became known as <s>Ratnamati</s> (Jewel-minded). Then <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Indra</s> lord of the gods, in the <s>Sudharmā</s> divine assembly-hall, saw him radiating the splendor of the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: atha śakro devendras taṃ devaputraṃ kūṭāgāra

children.text: sutaptaṃ kuśalamūlaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca gāthayā pratyabhāṣat //
children.translated_text: and seeing his well-ripened root of merit, replied with a verse:

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, [seeing] that <s>devaputra</s> (son of the gods) in the mansion,

children.translated_text: "By what [merit] is your body like polished gold, resembling a lotus and water-lily?

children.text: gātraśrīr atulā kṛteyam iha te dehāt prabhā niḥsṛtā /
children.translated_text: This incomparable bodily beauty of yours — radiance has issued from your body!
By what [merit] is your face like a fully opened lotus, resembling fine gold?

children.text: brūhi tvaṃ mama devate phalam idaṃ yat karmajaṃ bhujyate // Dak_7.8 //
children.translated_text: Tell me, O divine one — what is this fruit born of <s>karma</s> that is being enjoyed?"

body.text: ratnamatidevaputra uvāca //
body.translated_text: The <s>devaputra</s> <s>Ratnamati</s> spoke:

body.text:
saśrāvako narāditya ākīrṇo varalakṣaṇaiḥ /
tat karma kuśalaṃ kṛtvā rājate 'bhyadhikaṃ mama /
jalajenduviśuddhābha

children.translated_text: is lovely to behold."

body.translated_text: "The Sun of men (the <s>Buddha</s>), accompanied by <s>śrāvakas</s> (disciples), adorned with excellent marks — having performed that meritorious <s>karma</s>, [my splendor] shines forth exceedingly. My face, pure like the moon born from water,

body.text: śakraḥ prāha //
body.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> said:

children.translated_text: "Ah, [what] a field full of virtues, free from all defects,

children.text: yatra nyastaṃ tvayā bījam iṣṭaṃ svargopapattaye // Dak_7.10 //
children.translated_text: in which you planted a seed, desired for attaining heaven!
Who would not worship the <s>Buddha</s>, radiant as a heap of finest gold,
with beautiful wide eyes like pure lotuses?
For him, the pleasures born of [that] meritorious action among the immortals

children.text: rejuḥ sukhāni gagaṇeṣv iva pūrṇacandram // Dak_7.11 //
children.translated_text: shone like the full moon in the skies."

body.text: dharmatā khalu devaputrasya aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante // kutaś cyutaḥ kutropapannaḥ kena karmaṇeti // sa paśyati manuṣyebhyaś cyutaḥ praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyatriṃseṣūpapannaḥ bhagavato 'ntike cittaṃ prasādyeti //
body.translated_text: It is the natural law that for a <s>devaputra</s> recently reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where have I fallen? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' He sees: 'I have fallen from among humans and been reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods, having generated faith in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

body.text: atha tasya devaputrasya cetasy etad abhavat // na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ paryuṣitaparivāso bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāmayeyam / iti sa devaputra

children.text: sarvāṅgavirājitagātro ratnacūḍasugandhādisaṃsṛṣṭadeha anekadevaputrasahasraparivṛtas tenaiva ratnakūṭāgāreṇa saha bhagavataḥ sakāśam upasaṃkrāntaḥ / tato bhagavantaṃ divyapuṣpair avakīrya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya //
children.translated_text: with body adorned in all limbs, his form imbued with jeweled crest, fine fragrance, and the like, surrounded by many thousands of <s>devaputras</s>, together with that very jeweled mansion, approached the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then, having scattered divine flowers upon the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat down before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.translated_text: Then this thought arose in the mind of that <s>devaputra</s>: 'It would not be proper for me to approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience while wearing yesterday's garments.' So that <s>devaputra</s>,

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān sa devaputrasyāśayānuśaya

children.translated_text: elemental constitution,
and nature, delivered a <s>Dharma</s>-teaching conducive to the penetration of the Four Noble Truths (<s>caturāryasatya</s>).

children.text: kṛtavān // yāṃ śrutvā tasya devaputrasya viṃśatiśikharasamudgata
children.translated_text: Having heard it, that <s>devaputra</s>, having shattered with the vajra of knowledge the mountain of the view of the perishable aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) rising in twenty peaks,

children.text: satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā śrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam, sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati //
children.translated_text: directly realized the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotāpattiphala</s>). He, having seen the truth, uttered the solemn utterance (<s>udāna</s>) three times:

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing that <s>devaputra</s>'s disposition, latent tendencies,

body.text: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā na devatābhir na rājñā neṣṭajanabandhuvargeṇa kṛtam / yad bhagavatā

children.translated_text: the oceans of blood and tears have been dried up,
the mountains of bones have been crossed over,
the gates of miserable destinies have been shut,
the gates of heaven have been opened,
and we have been established among gods and humans." And he said:

body.translated_text: "This was not done for us, O Venerable One, by our mother, nor by the gods, nor by a king, nor by the group of dear relatives and kin — that which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "By your power, the terrible path of miserable destinies, fraught with many faults, has been shut;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdaḥ // Dak_7.12 //
children.translated_text: the heavenly destination, rich in merit, has been opened, and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been obtained by me.

children.text: tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ mayādya śuddhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: By reliance on you, I have today obtained the pure, faultless, supremely purified vision;

children.text: prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ tīrṇaś ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmi // Dak_7.13 //
children.translated_text: and I have attained the peaceful state beloved of the noble ones, and I have crossed to the far shore of the ocean of suffering.

body.text:
naravarendra narāmarapūjita vigatajanmajarāmaraṇāmaya /
bhavasahasrasudurlabhadarśana

children.text: phalam adya mune tava darśanam // Dak_7.14 //
children.translated_text: O sage, your vision, difficult to obtain in a thousand existences, is fruitful today."

body.translated_text: O best of men, worshipped by men and gods, free from birth, old age, death, and disease,

body.text: atha sa devaputro bhagavataś caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya saṃjātaharsaḥ suralokābhimukhaṃ divaṃ jagāma //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>devaputra</s>, having bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, with joy arisen, went to the heavenly realm.

body.text: atha sa devaputro vaṇig iva labdhalābhaḥ sasyasaṃpanna iva karṣakaḥ śūra iva jitasaṃgrāmaḥ sarvarogaparimukta ivāturo yayā vibhūtyā bhagavatsakāśam āgatas tayaiva vibhūtyā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>devaputra</s>, like a merchant who has gained profit, like a farmer whose crops have ripened, like a hero who has won a battle, like a sick person freed from all diseases — with the very same splendor with which he had come to the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he returned to his own abode.

body.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā saṃdigdhamanaso bhikṣavo bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / kāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni sā devaputrasyedṛśī vibhūtir āsit // avarakeṇa kuśalamūlena samanvāgataḥ sa devaputra iti //
body.translated_text: Seeing him, the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), with doubtful minds, asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'What <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated, that such was the splendor of that <s>devaputra</s>? By what modest root of merit was that <s>devaputra</s> endowed?'

body.text: atha bhagavān kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīm āsthāya sarvāvantaṃ bhikṣugaṇam āmantryaivam āha // bhikṣavo vaḥ kim āścaryabhūtaṃ taddhetuṃ pravakṣyāmi śṛṇuta //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, having remained silent for a moment, addressed the entire assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> thus: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, what seems wondrous to you — I shall declare the cause of that; listen!'

children.text: upte bīj[e] aṅkuraḥ syāt pṛthivyāṃ tasmād vallī suprajātā supuṣpā /
children.translated_text: "When a seed is planted in the earth, a sprout arises; from that, a creeper well-born, well-flowered,

children.text: bahvī śākhā bahupattrā phalādyā loke tadvaj jñeyam evaṃ prakārāḥ // Dak_7.15 //
children.translated_text: with many branches, many leaves, bearing fruits and the like — so in the world, such kinds of [fruits] should be known.

body.text: bīja upte hi varo bījāṅkuro hi mahān, yathā bījāṅkuro pṛthivyāḥ, dharaṇītalāl laṭā prajātānyaśeṣān mahāprajātānāṃ, bahuśākhāpattrā sapuṣpajātātrāntare phalaprasiddhā subahuprakārāt //
body.translated_text: For when a noble seed is planted, the seedling is great, just as the seedling [grows] from the earth, from the surface of the ground a vine is born with all the remaining great offspring, with many branches and leaves, with flowers born therein, and abundant fruits of many kinds.

children.translated_text: So too, humans plant the best, excellent seed in a worthy field;

children.text: tadubhavo vṛkṣa na nīca kaś cit kṣayaṃ na yānti satataṃ phalanti // Dak_7.16 //
children.translated_text: the tree born from it is no lowly one — they never perish and perpetually bear fruit.

children.text: tasmāt kasya cid bhikṣo bījāṅkuraṃ mahattaram /
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>bhikṣu</s>, the seedling of someone's [merit] is the greatest;

children.text: sarveṣāṃ caiva bījānāṃ puṇyabījaṃ subījakam // Dak_7.17 //
children.translated_text: among all seeds, the seed of merit is the best seed.

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason?

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte

children.text: dhvany asaṃkhyeya kalpair mallā nāma janapade kuśinagarapattanavane bhagavataḥ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasya dhātustūpam ekam asti / tasmin nagare vibhavavihīnamahādīnaparamadaridraḥ śāntamatir nāma śreṣṭhī prativasati sma // tasyānujo vigatamatir nāma, tayor militvā tābhyām anekayatnena dhanārjanaṃ kṛtaṃ tathāpi na saphalam abhūt / tat kasmād dhetoḥ pūrvakuśaladānahīnatvāt //
children.translated_text: in immeasurable <s>kalpas</s> (cosmic ages) ago, in the country called <s>Malla</s>, in the grove of the city of <s>Kuśinagara</s>, there was a single <s>stūpa</s> (reliquary mound) containing relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s> (Abundant Jewels). In that city there dwelt a merchant named <s>Śāntamati</s> (Peaceful-minded), who was devoid of prosperity, extremely poor, and utterly destitute. His younger brother was named <s>Vigatamati</s> (Gone-minded); the two of them together, with much effort, earned wealth — yet it bore no fruit. Why? Because of the deficiency of previous merit and generosity.

body.translated_text: O <s>bhikṣus</s>, formerly, in the past,

body.text: tataḥ prabhūtaratnatathāgatasya śāsane samutpannaḥ prakṛtipariśuddhir nāmopāsakaḥ prativasti sma // sa dharmacittakaḥ karuṇācittam upasthāpya sarvasattvebhyo nityaṃ dharmaṃ deśayati //
body.translated_text: Then, in the dispensation of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Prabhūtaratna</s>, there was born a lay devotee (<s>upāsaka</s>) named <s>Prakṛtipariśuddhi</s> (Naturally Pure), who dwelt [there]. He, with a mind of <s>Dharma</s>, having established a mind of compassion, constantly taught the <s>Dharma</s> to all beings.

body.text: tadyathā //
body.translated_text: Namely:

body.text: ye ke cit paścime kāle sarṣapaphalamātraṃ tathāgatasya śarīradhātuṃ pūjayiṣya

children.translated_text: shall worship the <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relics,

children.text: ti / teṣāṃ sarvakarmabhayo 'ntaśaḥ paiśunyapāpakā akuśalān duḥkhadharmān na kramiṣya
children.translated_text: for them, [from] all fear of <s>karma</s>, even the sinful [karmas] of slander — the unwholesome, painful <s>dharmas</s> — shall not proceed further.

children.text: ti // ye ye mānavās tathāgatadhātustūpaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ kurvanti pūjayanti svadoṣaparihārārtham, te pramādād gamyāgamya prāṇivadhādidoṣavilayaṃ bhaveyuḥ //
children.translated_text: Those people who circumambulate and worship the <s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relics for the removal of their own faults — even if through negligence they have committed faults such as killing of living beings through careless going — those faults would dissolve."

body.translated_text: "Whoever in the future time shall worship even a mustard-seed's measure of the bodily relics of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: śubhāni dharmaḥ pariśuddhadharmaḥ pūrvāṇi pāpāni viśuddhadharmaḥ /
children.translated_text: "Virtuous is the <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> of complete purity; [it purifies] former sins — the <s>Dharma</s> of purification!

children.text: aho hi dharmaḥ paramāryadharmaḥ pavitradharmaḥ śubhakāridharmaḥ // Dak_7.18
children.translated_text: Ah, the <s>Dharma</s> is the supreme noble <s>Dharma</s>, the holy <s>Dharma</s>, the <s>Dharma</s> that produces good!"

body.text: atha sa daridrapuruṣo buddhasya dharmaṃ śrutvā prasādajāto nityam eva dharma

children.text: śrotuṃ gacchatīti // tadānujo vigatamaitr bhrātaraṃ uvāca / bhrāta ā kiṃ tava maryādaṃ vyapahāya kāryaṃ dharmaśrutena kim, tvayā saha vartanaṃ na sukaraṃ kartum
children.translated_text: Then his younger brother, <s>Vigatamati</s>, spoke to his brother: 'Brother, why, abandoning your proper conduct, [do you go]? What use is listening to the <s>Dharma</s>? Living together with you is not easy to manage.

children.text: parapreṣako bhūtvā vartayāmīty uktvā svagṛhān niṣkramya svacchandena, anyasya preṣako 'bhūt // atha sa daridro bhrātā viyoge sati cittavyākulībhūtvā tathāpi svayam eva mana
children.translated_text: I shall become another's servant and live thus.' Having said this, he left his own house and, at his own will, became another's servant. Then that poor brother, when the separation occurred, became mentally distressed; yet he himself, calming his mind,

children.text: praśāntya dharmeṣu cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ // athaikasmin dine raktakāṣāyavastrapātradhārī bhikṣur eko dvāramūleṣv athiṣṭhat piṇḍapātraṃ yācitum // taṃ dṛṣṭvā śīghram eva gṛhaṃ praviśyādrākṣīt kiṃ cin na vidyate / ātmanāhārāya parit
children.translated_text: remained absorbed in reflection on the <s>Dharma</s>. Then one day, a <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) wearing red-brown robes and carrying a bowl stood at the entrance to beg for alms. Seeing him, [<s>Śāntamati</s>] quickly entered the house and saw that there was nothing [to give]. The only rice grains that remained were those set aside for his own food; he immediately took them and offered them to that [<s>bhikṣu</s>].

children.text: āni taṇḍulāny eva santi, sa sahasā gṛhītvā tasmai prāyacchat //

body.translated_text: Then that poor man, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Buddha</s>, with faith arisen, continually went to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.

body.text: bhikṣur api tena yathā datta

children.translated_text: as it was, spoke to him:

body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣu</s> too, having accepted what was given

body.text:
daridre 'pi ca puṇyātmā daridre tyāgadurlabhaḥ /
tasmāt puṇyānubhāvena dāridr

children.translated_text: therefore, by the power of merit, may your poverty be destroyed!

body.translated_text: Even among the poor, a meritorious soul is rare, and among the poor, generosity is hard to find;

children.text: bhadraṃ bhavatu te bhadra nāśayatu abhadrakam /
children.translated_text: May auspiciousness be yours, O good one, and may it destroy all that is inauspicious;
may there be devotion and faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, and thereby attainment of heaven.

body.text: ity uktvāntarhito 'bhūt // atha tasya daridrasyaitad abhavat /
body.translated_text: Having said this, he vanished. Then this thought occurred to that poor man:

children.text: kiṃ kartavyam idānīṃ me hā dhig janma ca jīvitam /
children.translated_text: "What am I to do now? Alas, shame upon this birth and life!

children.translated_text: For one bereft of wealth, death would be preferable."
