children.translated_text: Whoever in the final age will worship even a mustard-seed-sized bodily relic of the <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One), whoever will worship the relic-<s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—their obstructions from former <s>karma</s> (actions) will be exhausted

children.text: pariśudhyate, cittapariśuddhatvād dharma pariśudhyate, dharmapariśuddhatvāt tenaiva phalaṃ labhyate // tathā śrutaṃ me pariśuddhadharmeti //
children.translated_text: and purified; through purification of mind, the <s>Dharma</s> is purified; through purification of <s>Dharma</s>, the fruit is thereby obtained." Thus I have heard: "<s>Pariśuddhadharma</s> (Pure Dharma)."

body.translated_text: Again this thought occurred to him: "From the lay devotee named <s>Prakṛtipariśuddhi</s>, I have heard the <s>Dharma</s>:

body.text: atha tasyaitad abhavat / tathā tathāgataṃ pūjayeyam iti so

children.text: pi nirvāṇaṃ gataḥ / tathāpy asya dhātustūpam asti tam ahaṃ pūjayeyam iti // punas tasyaitad abhavat //
children.translated_text: has attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>; nevertheless, his relic-<s>stūpa</s> exists—I should worship that." Again this thought occurred to him:

body.translated_text: Then this thought occurred to him: "I should worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> in that manner." He too

children.translated_text: "Being destitute of means, with what manner of offerings should one worship?

children.text: puṣpaṃ dhūpas tathā gandhaṃ dīpanaivedyam eva ca /
children.translated_text: Flowers, incense, fragrance, lamps, and food offerings—

children.text: etair vidhiṃ vinā pūjā kiṃ pūjāphalam āpyate // Dak_7.22 //
children.translated_text: without these prescribed items, what fruit of worship can be obtained?"

body.text: iti daridraḥ samanuśocya tiṣṭhati dīnamānasaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus the poor man stood lamenting, with a dejected mind.

body.text: atha tasya dharmaśrutasya puṇyānukūla pratodeneva pracodayati sma // tasya manasi etad abhavat // na mama pratirūpaṃ syād yad ahaṃ tathāgatadhātustūpa upāsitavya

children.text: pānīyamātreṇa snānaṃ kartavyam / iti matvā mṛnmayaghataṃ gṛhītvā nadyāṃ tīre snātvā pariśuddhamānaso jalam ādāya tasmin stūpe snāpayati sma // tato dinamāsātyāyād ekasmin dine caityabimbasnānāya jalam ādātuṃ gacchati //
children.translated_text: a bathing with water alone should be performed." Having decided thus, taking an earthen pot, having bathed at the bank of the river, with purified mind, taking water, he bathed that <s>stūpa</s>. Then—

body.translated_text: Then the merit of having heard the <s>Dharma</s> goaded him on, as if with a favorable goad of <s>puṇya</s> (merit). This thought arose in his mind: "It would not be fitting for me if I did not [worship]; at the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s relic-<s>stūpa</s>,

children.text: jalam ādāya tadā gatvā snānaṃ cāpi prakalpitam /
children.translated_text: having taken water and gone there, and having performed the bathing,

children.text: tadā ghaṭāt patitāni ratnāni vividhāni ca // Dak_7.23 //
children.translated_text: then from the pot fell various jewels.

body.text: tataḥ sa śāntamatis tāni dṛṣṭvā prasādajāto manasīty abhūt //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>Śāntamati</s>, seeing those, with faith arisen, thought in his mind:

children.translated_text: "I bow to the <s>stūpa</s>, to the <s>caitya</s> (shrine), to the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (realm of truth);
I offer these jewels to the <s>caitya</s> with a pure mind."

children.text: tataḥ sa pratinivṛtya nadyās tīre pragacchati /
children.translated_text: Then he turned back and proceeded to the bank of the river;

children.text: dadarśa sa daridreṇa ratnāni ca samākulā // Dak_7.25 //
children.translated_text: and that poor man saw jewels in abundance.
An abundance of diamonds, <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), coral, pearls, and rubies,
<s>karketana</s> (chrysoberyl), sapphires, topazes, and others—

children.text: nadyāḥ pravāhaṃ kṣobhitvā sasāra sikatāsthale // Dak_7.26 //
children.translated_text: having churned up the river's current, they had settled on the sandy bank.
By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>'s merit, even a poor man in a short time
obtains such acquisition of jewels, as if in a dream.

body.text: tataḥ sa daridras tāni svecchayā gṛhya punar api / svaṃ bhavanaṃ pratinivṛtya cintayann uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then that poor man, having taken those at his own pleasure, returned again to his own dwelling and, reflecting, said:

children.translated_text: "Oh, what a field rich in virtues, free from all faults!

children.text: sevayā svalpamātreṇa prāpto 'haṃ saphalaṃ padam // Dak_7.28 //
children.translated_text: By service of even the slightest measure, I have attained a fruitful state."

body.text: tataḥ sa mahādhano 'bhūt suṣkahrado nīragāsaritsamūhair itas tataḥ praveśita iva pūrṇo 'bhūt // tataḥ prabhṛti rājñā rājāmātyair brāhmaṇaiḥ saṃmānitaḥ sādhubhir lokasaṃmato 'bhūt // sādhu satpuruṣa eṣa loke prakhyātaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then he became very wealthy—like a dried-up lake filled from streams flowing in from all sides. From then on, he was honored by the king, royal ministers, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (priests).

body.text: atha sa śreṣṭhī ullāsitamanā harṣasaumanasyajāto buddhe cittaṃ prasādayām āsa //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant, with an elated mind, filled with joy and delight, placed his faith in the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: tato dinamāsātyayāt tasyaitad abhavat //
body.translated_text: Then, after the passing of days and months, this thought occurred to him:

children.translated_text: "Ah, the power of the <s>Buddha</s> is indeed the bestower of inconceivable prosperity!

children.text: bhikṣā rāśiṣaḥ saṃprāptā dāridryaṃ duḥkhitaṃ gatam // Dak_7.29 //
children.translated_text: From mere alms-seeking, wealth has been attained, and poverty and suffering have departed."

body.text: atha sa śreṣṭhī mahatā satkāreṇa stūpeṣu ratnamaya

children.translated_text: multi-storied pavilion,

children.text: ṃ kṛtam abhūt / nānāgandhodakena snāpanaṃ kṛtaṃ tridhā pradakṣiṇīkṛtya mūrdhnā praṇipatya sāñjaliṃ ca praṇidhānaṃ cakāra / bhagavan me janmāntare tathāvidhena tathāgateṣu manaḥprasādaḥ san ratnamayakūṭāgāreṇa saha svarge trāyatriṃśeṣv upapattir bhaveyam // ity uktvā nityam eva tasmin stūpe paryupāsitaḥ //
children.translated_text: and performed bathing with various fragrant waters, circumambulated thrice, bowed with his head, and with joined palms made this aspiration: "O <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), in my future birth, may I be a <s>Tathāgata</s>—"

body.translated_text: Then that merchant, with great reverence, at the <s>stūpas</s>, made a jeweled

body.text:
atha sa śreṣṭhī saṃsārike kṛtakaraṇīyo buddhe bhagavati cittaṃ prasādya kālagataḥ // kālaṃ gatvā dharmakośavatinagare dharmamatiśreṣṭhijanma babhūva /
mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇadhanadhānyasaṃpanna ihaiva janmani mayi prasādya bhaktitaḥ pūjāṃ kṛtavān / tat sarvaṃ mamāgre vahanti /
body.translated_text: Then that merchant, having fulfilled his duties in worldly life, having placed his faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), passed away. After death, he was born in the city of <s>Dharmakośavatī</s> as the son of the merchant <s>Dharmamati</s>.

children.translated_text: At his birth, waters appeared first, adorned like a string of pearls;

children.text: puṣpaṃ ca puṣpakūṭeva dhūpo 'bhrakūṭavat sthitaḥ // Dak_7.30 //
children.translated_text: flowers like a heap of blossoms, and incense stood like a mass of clouds.

body.text: tatas tasya śreṣṭhina alpāyutvād bauddhe prasādya kālagataḥ praṇīteṣu trāyatriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannaḥ svapuṇyaphalavipākena ratnakūṭāgāre niṣadyādyarātrau tatrāgacchati / mayā dharmo deśitaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then, due to that merchant's short lifespan, having placed faith in the Buddhist [teaching], he passed away and was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods, and by the ripening of his own merit, seated in a jeweled pavilion—

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena sanayena sa dāridro 'yaṃ ratnamatir nāma devaputro mayi dharmaṃ śrutvā svabhavanaṃ gataḥ // bhutapūrvaṃ prabhūtaratnasya tathāgatasya dhātustūpe snānakṛtamātreṇa mahadthno 'bhūt / tena paścād ratnamaya

children.translated_text: a pavilion

children.text: k rtaṃ tenaiva praṇidhānavaśās ratnakūṭāgāreṇa saha svargeṣūpapannaḥ //
children.translated_text: was made [by him]; by the power of that very aspiration, together with the jeweled pavilion, he was reborn in the heavens."

body.translated_text: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks)? He who was at that time, in that era, that poor man—he is this son of the gods named <s>Ratnamati</s>, who, having heard the <s>Dharma</s> from me, went to his own abode. In the past,

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ snānakathāparivarto nāma saptamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the chapter called the story of bathing, the seventh chapter.

body.text: VIII. kuṅkumādidānakathā
body.translated_text: VIII. The Story of the Gift of Saffron and Other Substances

body.text: atha kadā cid buddho bhagavān satkṛto gurukṛto mānitaḥ pūjito rājabhī rājāmātyair dhanibhiḥ sārthavāhair devair nāgair yakṣāsuragaruḍakinnaramahoragair abhyarcito buddho bhagavān jñāto mahāpuṇyalābhī cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglānapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārāṇāṃ saśrāvakasaṃgho mahatā satkāreṇa pūjito dharmaśravanārtham / tadā buddho bhagavān svaṃ prabhāvaṃ pradarśayan yeṣām unnatacittānāṃ mānamadadarpaprahāṇārthaṃ parṣadbhyo dharmaṃ deśitavān / tac chrutvā sabhāśritajanāḥ saṃmodavantaḥ //
body.translated_text: Once, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), honored, revered, respected, and worshipped by kings, royal ministers, the wealthy, caravan leaders, <s>devas</s> (gods), <s>nāgas</s> (serpents), <s>yakṣas</s> (nature spirits), <s>asuras</s> (demons), <s>garuḍas</s> (eagle-beings), <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), and <s>mahoragas</s> (great serpents)—

body.text:
tasminn avasare tadā tatra rājagṛhe 'nyatamaḥ sautīrṇo nāma vaṇig āsīt /
mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaparivāraprāptaḥ / tadātmasadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam / tayā saha sukhena tiṣṭhati // sa cintayati / tathā na yuktam, kiṃ tu pitā cāsmākaṃ kiṃkarmaphalopajīvī āsīt / aham api tathā kariṣyāmīti // yady okkarika āsīd okkarika

children.text: ṃ kariṣyāmi / mahāsamudravaṇig āsīt tat tathā kariṣyāmīti //
children.translated_text: "I shall do this. He was an ocean-going merchant; I shall do likewise."

body.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, there was a certain merchant named <s>Sautīrṇa</s>, very wealthy, possessed of great fortune, with an extensive retinue. He had taken a wife from a family equal to his own,

body.text: tadā kenāpi kathyamānena śrutam / jānāmi pitā cāsmākaṃ samudravaṇig āsīt / iti cintayitvā svapatnīm uvāca // kānte matkarmaṇā eva vaṇikkule jātas tenāhaṃ ratnākara

children.text: mahāsamudraṃ gantum icchāmi / tvayā gṛhācāraṃ kṛtvā tiṣṭha ma bhītāsi / acireṇāgamiṣyāmi mamārthe devatāṃ smṛtvā dhairyam ālambya mā sāhasaṃ kuru //
children.translated_text: I wish to go to the great ocean. You should maintain the household and remain; do not be afraid. I shall return before long. For my sake, remember the deities, take courage, and do not act rashly."

body.translated_text: Then, having heard from someone speaking, [he thought]: "I know that our father too was an ocean-going merchant." Having reflected thus, he said to his wife: "Beloved, born as I am in a merchant family by my own <s>karma</s>, therefore

body.text: tac chrutvā patny uvāca //
body.translated_text: Having heard that, his wife said:

children.text: mā brūhi nātha bhartas tvaṃ kathaṃ tiṣṭhāmy ahaṃ nanu /
children.translated_text: "Do not say this, O lord and husband! How shall I remain, tell me?

children.text: viśeṣair abalājātiḥ ko rakṣati gṛhe tava // Dak_8.1 //
children.translated_text: Especially for one of the weaker sex, who will protect your household?

children.text: kasmai sādhayate dravyaṃ putro vā te na vidyate /
children.translated_text: For whose sake would you earn wealth? You have no son.

children.text: yad asti pūrvadravyaṃ te tena śānto bhava prabho // Dak_8.2 //
children.translated_text: Whatever ancestral wealth you have—with that, be at peace, O lord.

children.text: kim eva bahubhir dravyaiḥ kleśa eva yad udbhavet /
children.translated_text: What use are many riches, if only affliction would arise from them?

children.text: kleśināṃ hi sadā duḥkhaṃ saṃsāre sukhatā kutaḥ // Dak_8.3 //
children.translated_text: For those who are afflicted, there is always suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence)—whence happiness?
For those who possess much wealth, there is always the great fear of the suffering of affliction;

children.text: tan nirarthaṃ bahudravyaṃ sādhane mā kurūdyamam // Dak_8.4 //
children.translated_text: therefore, much wealth is purposeless—do not make effort in its acquisition."

body.text: bhartā uvāca //
body.translated_text: The husband said:

children.text: itthaṃ mā vadasi kānte kuladharmaiṣa me yataḥ /
children.translated_text: "Do not speak thus, beloved; this is my family duty,

children.text: nīcena mahatā cāpi kuladharmaṃ na varjayet // Dak_8.5 //
children.translated_text: whether lowly or great, one should not abandon the family tradition.

body.text: viśeṣeṇa gṛhasthānāṃ dhana

children.translated_text: is indeed the root for embodied beings;

children.text: dhanenāpi vihīnasya kuto mitraṃ kutaḥ sukham // Dak_8.6 //
children.translated_text: for one who is deprived of wealth, whence friends? Whence happiness?

body.translated_text: Especially for householders, wealth

children.text: dravyenaiva vaśāḥ sarve pumān api dhanena ca /
children.translated_text: All are subject to wealth, and even a man [depends] on riches;

children.text: dhanena lokasatkāraṃ yāty ataḥ sādhayed dhanam // Dak_8.7 //
children.translated_text: through wealth one attains the respect of the world; therefore one should earn wealth."

body.text: patny uvāca //
body.translated_text: The wife said:

body.text:
svāmin vinā kathaṃ nāthaṃ tiṣṭhāmi cāham ekikā /
candreṇa rahitā rātrir andhakāra

children.translated_text: darkness in the house.

body.translated_text: "O lord, how shall I, without a protector, remain alone? Like a night without the moon,

body.text: punaś ca //
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

children.text: yasmāt striyo vinā bhartrā tarkayante parair api /
children.translated_text: Because women without a husband are preyed upon by others,

children.text: bhūmau patitamāṃsāni piṇḍāni śakunair iva // Dak_8.9 //
children.translated_text: like pieces of meat fallen on the ground [are seized] by birds.

body.text:
bhaveṣu lobhavastūni nārīpuṣpaphalāni ca /
kasyāsti nāgame cittaṃ dṛṣṭvā strīṣu vimohitā

children.translated_text: upon seeing women?

body.translated_text: In worldly existence, objects of desire and the flowers and fruits of women— whose mind is not deluded

body.text:
adāntaś cittamātaṅgaḥ satpathena kathaṃ vrajet /
kupathena yadā gacchet prapaten nārake hi sa
body.translated_text: The untamed elephant of the mind—how would it go on the right path? When it goes on the wrong path, it would fall into hell.

body.text: viśeṣeṇa striyā dharma

children.translated_text: obtains is exceedingly rare;

children.text: tasmāt saṃtrasitāṃ svāmin mā māṃ tyajya vraja svayam // Dak_8.12 //
children.translated_text: therefore, O lord, do not abandon me, frightened as I am, and go by yourself."

body.translated_text: Especially, the <s>Dharma</s> that a woman

body.text: tat kasya hetoḥ //
body.translated_text: For what reason?

children.text: śṛṇuṣvaikakathāṃ bhartaḥ śrutaṃ me mātari kva cit /
children.translated_text: "Listen, O husband, to one story; I heard it once from my mother:

children.text: manasā cintitāt pāpād veśyā bhavati brāhmaṇī // Dak_8.13 //
children.translated_text: Through sin merely conceived in the mind, a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman) becomes a courtesan."

body.text: bhartā uvāca //
body.translated_text: The husband said:

children.text: kathaṃ veśyā bhavet kānte brāhmaṇī sukulodbhavā /
children.translated_text: "How could a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman) of good birth become a courtesan, beloved?

children.text: manasā cintitāmātrair idam āścaryam adbhutam // Dak_8.14 //
children.translated_text: By mere thoughts conceived in the mind? This is a wonder most astonishing!"

body.text: patny uvāca //
body.translated_text: The wife said:

children.translated_text: "There was a city called <s>Kośalā</s>, spacious and splendid,
teeming with learned people, adorned by virtuous persons.
In that city, there was a very wealthy <s>brāhmaṇa</s> (priest), learned in the <s>Vedas</s>;

children.text: sa patnīsahitaś cāsau vasate sukhalīlayā // Dak_8.16 //
children.translated_text: he, together with his wife, lived in happy sport.
Then, by the decree of fate, that best of twice-born died,
leaving behind the love of his dear one, helplessly, along with all his prosperity.

body.text:
tatpatnī brāhmaṇī sā vai aprasūtā sayauvanī /
bhartu

children.translated_text: virtues remembering, became distressed in mind.

body.translated_text: His wife, that <s>brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman), childless and still young, her husband's

children.text: dineṣu gacchatsu nitānta-āturā bhartur viyogād virahāc ca premṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: As the days passed, she became exceedingly afflicted by the separation from her husband and the anguish of love;

children.text: śītopacāraiś ca kṛte 'pi gātre dāheva yasyā jvalitogravahninā // Dak_8.19 //
children.translated_text: even though cool treatments were applied to her body, she burned as if with a blazing, fierce fire.
Filthy in tattered garments on her bed, like a she-monkey's resting place—

children.text: tasyās tathāvidhair anyair upacāraiś ca ko vidhiḥ // Dak_8.20 //
children.translated_text: for her in such a condition, what use were any other treatments?

children.text: upacāriṇī tatas tasyā vaidyam āhūya darśitā /
children.translated_text: Her attendant then summoned a physician and showed her to him;

children.text: vaidyena hastaṃ saṃgṛhya dhamanī vīkṣyate punaḥ // Dak_8.21 //
children.translated_text: the physician, taking her hand, examined her pulse again.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā uktaṃ tadā tena, praśrabdhā na cikitsayā /
children.translated_text: Having examined her, he then said: "She cannot be cured by medicine;

children.text: yasyā viraharoge na vaidyauṣadhir lagiṣyati // Dak_8.22 //
children.translated_text: for one whose disease is the pain of separation, no physician's remedy will take effect."

children.text: iti vicārya vaidyo 'sau pratyāgataḥ svakaṃ gṛham /
children.translated_text: Having thus deliberated, the physician returned to his own house,

children.text: dhamanīdṛṣṭam anyaṃ ca gṛhītvā hi yathā matam // Dak_8.23 //
children.translated_text: having noted what was observed through the pulse and other [signs], according to his judgment.
Because the unconscious, ailing woman — by the man's hand not touching [her],

children.text: sparśamātreṇa tasyā vai hṛdaye śītalaṃ tv abhūt // Dak_8.24 //
children.translated_text: by the mere touch alone, coolness arose in her heart.

body.text:
hṛdaye svasthabhūtena parivṛtopacārikā /
paśyantī cakṣuṣā sarvā

children.translated_text: she spoke slowly and gently:

body.translated_text: With her heart restored to health, surrounded by attendants, seeing all [of them] with her eyes,

children.text: kena pṛṣṭādya me haste kena spṛṣṭā ca me tanau /
children.translated_text: "By whom was my hand touched today? By whom was my body touched?

children.text: kīdṛśī sukhasvasthāni ucyatāṃ mayi he sakhi // Dak_8.26 //
children.translated_text: What kind of healthy comfort [is this]? Tell me, O friend."

body.text: upacārikā ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: The attendants said:

body.text: svāmini te vinā svasthaiḥ vaidyaḥ prajñapta

children.translated_text: for [your] sake;

children.text: glānānām akṣaṇā kiṃ ca dṛṣṭvā auṣadham ācaret // Dak_8.27 //
children.translated_text: for the ailing, what delay? Having examined [you], he administered medicine."

body.translated_text: "O mistress, without those who are well, a physician was appointed

body.text: brāhmaṇī uvāca //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> (Brahmin woman) said:

children.text: striyo vā puruṣo vāpi, svastho jātaś ca me hṛdi /
children.translated_text: "Was it a woman or a man? Health has arisen in my heart;

children.text: īdṛśaḥ sukhajāto me glānaṃ śāntam abhūt kṣaṇāt // Dak_8.28 //
children.translated_text: such comfort has arisen in me — the illness was pacified in an instant."

body.text: upacārikā ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: The attendants said:

body.text: na striyaḥ svāmini vaidyaḥ pumāṃl lokacikitsakaḥ /

children.text: dhamanīmātram ālakṣya gatavān svagṛhe sa ca // Dak_8.29 /
children.translated_text: having merely examined the pulse, he has gone to his own home."

body.translated_text: "Not a woman, O mistress; the physician is a man, a healer of people;

body.text: brāhmaṇī uvāca //
body.translated_text: The <s>Brāhmaṇī</s> said:

children.translated_text: "Ah! By the mere touch of a man's hand on my back, in my heart

children.text: upajātam īdṛśaṃ saukhyaṃ krīḍākṛte kathaṃ sukham // Dak_8.30 //
children.translated_text: such happiness has arisen — what happiness would there be from amorous play?"
By this mere thought, that vow-observer became sinful;

children.text: ihajanma tatas tyaktvā karmavāyubhir īritā // Dak_8.31 //
children.translated_text: having abandoned this birth, impelled by the winds of <s>karma</s>,
she was reborn in the delightful city of <s>Pātarī</s> as a courtesan;
she was named <s>Kāmaratī</s>, adorned with beauty and charm.
Gradually she became a young woman, intoxicated with the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love);

children.text: tasyā mātā ratīlolā putrīṃ vadati tatra ca // Dak_8.33 //
children.translated_text: her mother, fond of pleasure, spoke to her daughter there:

body.text:
asmākaṃ kuladharmeṣu veśyāvṛttiṃ kuruṣva tat /
viśeṣai rūpalāvaṇya

children.translated_text: especially your beauty and charm please great people;

children.text: krīḍaṃ kuruṣva putri tvaṃ bahuśo dhanadaiḥ saha // Dak_8.34 //
children.translated_text: engage in amorous play, O daughter, frequently with those who give wealth."

body.translated_text: "In the customs of our family, practice the profession of a courtesan;

body.text: tataḥ prabhṛti sā kāmaratī asakṛt svakulavyavahāraṃ kṛtavatī // tataḥ kāmaratī pañcatvam upagatā narake patitā //
body.translated_text: From then on, <s>Kāmaratī</s> repeatedly carried out the livelihood of her family. Then <s>Kāmaratī</s>, having died, fell into hell.

body.text: svāminn aham api tathā bhaviṣyatīti tvām ahaṃ vakṣyāmi //
body.translated_text: "O lord, I too will become like that" — thus I shall tell you.

children.text: mā bhaiṣī he priye kānte sādhu sādhu subhāṣitam /
children.translated_text: "Do not fear, O dear beloved one; well said, well said!

children.text: na bhaviṣyet tathā tvaṃ hi saṃtiṣṭha dṛḍhacetasā // Dak_8.35 //
children.translated_text: You shall not become like that; stand firm with a resolute mind."

body.text: atha satīrṇavaṇijaḥ patnīvacanam akṛtvā paṇyam ādāya bahubhir vāṇijair mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ // tasya patnī nātiyauvanavatī madhyavayasī aprasūtā

children.text: tataḥ kaścidvarṣāntare gate sā putrārthe ca svāmino 'rthe utkaṇṭhitā paritasya
children.translated_text: Then, when some years had passed, she, longing for a son and for her husband, suffered

children.text: na cāsyā bhartā āgacchati // // sā uvāca //
children.translated_text: and her husband did not return. She said:

body.translated_text: Then the ocean-crossing merchant, disregarding his wife's words, took his merchandise and descended into the great ocean with many merchants. His wife was not very youthful, of middle age, and without children.

children.text: bhartā naivāgataḥ kasmāt dīrghakālaṃ gato vaṇik /
children.translated_text: "Why has my husband, the merchant, not come, having gone for a long time?

children.text: tadā vinā ca saṅgena kutaḥ putrodayaṃ mama /
children.translated_text: And without his company, whence the arising of a son for me?

children.text: vayasi gate viśeṣais tu vaṃśacchedo na saṃśayaḥ // Dak_8.36 //
children.translated_text: With my youth gone, especially, the cutting off of the lineage is certain."

children.text: tasyā bhartā sautīrṇo 'sau nāgataḥ sucireṇa ca /
children.translated_text: Her husband, the ocean-crossing [merchant], did not return even after a very long time;
with the thorn of grief in her heart, she remained with a dejected mind.

body.text: atha sautīrṇavaṇijo mahatā satkāreṇa

children.translated_text: some merchants returned,

children.text: sugandhadravyāṇi tathāgatāya niryātaye tyaktvā pattralekhaṃ cānyavaṇijasya haste dattvā preṣayati //
children.translated_text: and having set aside fragrant substances as an offering to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, he sent a letter, placing it in the hand of another merchant.

body.translated_text: Then, with great honor toward the ocean-crossing merchant,

body.text: tataḥ sa vaṇijas tasya patnyai haste pattraṃ samarpayati //
body.translated_text: Then that merchant delivered the letter into the hands of his wife.

body.text: tadā tasya patny āgṛhītvā lekham, kuśalavārttāṃ papraccha //
body.translated_text: Then his wife, having received the letter, asked about his welfare:

children.text: kuśalī bhadra me bhartā kuśalaṃ sarvavastukam /
children.translated_text: "Is my husband well, O good one? Is all his property well?

children.text: siddhāni sarvakāryāṇi mā kaś cid rujayā vapuḥ // Dak_8.38 //
children.translated_text: Are all his affairs accomplished? May no illness [afflict] his body."

body.text: so 'vocat sarvaṃ kuśalaṃ mā bhaiṣīty uktvā svagṛhaṃ gataḥ // atha sā tasya patnī bhartā āgamiṣyatīti cintyāśayā utkaṇṭhitamanās tiṣṭhati //
body.translated_text: He said: "All is well; do not fear." Having said this, he went to his own home. Then his wife remained with a longing mind, thinking 'my husband will return.'

body.text: pratyāgate tataś cāsmiṃ

children.translated_text: due to his ill fortune,

children.text: tadā ca taraṇe naukā babhūva pralayāmbudhau // Dak_8.39 //
children.translated_text: at that time, during the crossing, the boat [was lost] in the ocean of destruction.

body.translated_text: But when he was returning,

children.translated_text: Then, remembering, he uttered the name of the <s>Buddha</s>;

children.text: kṣaṇāt prāṇaṃ yayau tatra tenāsau sugatiṃ gataḥ // Dak_8.40 //
children.translated_text: in an instant his life departed there, and by that he attained a good destination.

body.text: naśyanti sarvavastūni jīvaś cāpi praṇaśyati / vārttāpi nāgatas tasya mṛto 'pi jīvito 'tha vā //
body.translated_text: All possessions perished, and the living being also perished; no news of him came — whether he was dead or alive.

body.text: agaman viṃśaty abdāni kālaṃ gata abhūd asau // Dak_8.41 //
body.translated_text: Twenty years passed; he had departed [from this world].

children.text: dineṣu gacchatsu kramataś ca vṛddhā dhammillaśuklā kubjā ca sābhūt /
children.translated_text: As days passed, gradually she aged, her hair-knot turned white, and she became bent;

children.text: tathāpi tasyāḥ sneho na naśyati cānekadevasmaraṇena tiṣṭhati // Dak_8.42 //
children.translated_text: yet her love did not perish, and she remained with constant remembrance of the gods.

children.text: atha sā cintayām āsa svāminā prahitāni ca /
children.translated_text: Then she thought: "The fragrant substances sent by my husband
to the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One) —
how shall I worship here the lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the ocean of virtues,
when King <s>Ajātaśatru</s> has prohibited the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>?"

children.text: atha sā cintayām āsa pūjayāmi tathāgatam /
children.translated_text: Then she thought: "I shall worship the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
standing on the pinnacle of my mansion, with sandalwood and unguents."
Then, with joy and a mind filled with devotion,

children.text: arcitaṃ candanenaiva kusumaiḥ saha maṇḍalam // Dak_8.46 //
children.translated_text: she worshipped with sandalwood and flowers in a <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle).

children.text: tataḥ sā prāñjaliṃ kṛtvā natvāha sādaraiḥ punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Then, having joined her palms and bowed, she said again with reverence:

children.text: bhartā me 'pi mṛto vāpi jīvito vātha vā punaḥ // Dak_8.47 //
children.translated_text: "Is my husband dead, or is he alive, or what?

children.text: vārttāpi nāgatā tasya kathaṃ he bhagavan mune /
children.translated_text: No news of him has come; how [can this be], O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O sage?

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sarvadarśī tvaṃ nāsti kiṃ cid aveditam // Dak_8.48 //
children.translated_text: You are omniscient, all-seeing; nothing is unknown [to you].

children.text: svapnaṃ dāsyasi me nātha, asti nāsty atha vā mune /
children.translated_text: Grant me a dream, O lord — is [he] or is [he] not, O sage?

children.text: darśanam autsukaṃ jātaṃ bhartur vadanapaṅkajam // Dak_8.49 //
children.translated_text: An eager longing has arisen to see the lotus-face of my husband."

children.text: iti sā yācanaṃ kṛtvā tad dināni nināya ca /
children.translated_text: Having thus made her supplication, she passed those days;

children.text: saṃveśāya niśāyāṃ vai svāgāranilayaṃ yayau // Dak_8.50 //
children.translated_text: at night, for sleeping, she went to the quarters of her own home.

body.text: atha bhagavān sarvajñas tasyā āśayaṃ jñātvā svaṃ prabhāvaṃ pradarśayan

children.translated_text: spoke to <s>Sautīrṇa</s> through supernatural power with the voice of <s>Brahmā</s>:

body.translated_text: Then the omniscient <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing her intention, displaying his own power,

body.text: sautīrṇa tava patnyā tvām eva kālagataṃ na jānāti / tasmād divyarūpaṃ dhṛtvā svargād avatīrya divyadehaṃ svapnaṃ darśayatu // iti sahacittotpādād bhagavataḥ sautīrṇavaṇijo divyaśarīram abhivīkṣya,
body.translated_text: "O <s>Sautīrṇa</s>, your wife does not know that you have passed away. Therefore, assuming a divine form, descend from heaven and show [her] your divine body in a dream." Thus, simultaneously with the arising of this thought from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the ocean-crossing merchant, beholding his divine body,

body.text: dharmatā khalu aciropapannasya trīṇi cittāny utpadyante // kutaś cyutvā, ihopapannaḥ, kena karmaṇeti / sa paśyati manuṣyebhaś cyutas trāyatriṃśeṣūpapanno bhagavataḥ kuṅkumādidānād iti //
body.translated_text: [reflected:] it is indeed the nature of one who has recently been reborn that three thoughts arise: 'From where did I pass away? Where have I been reborn? By what deed?' He sees: having passed away from among humans, I have been reborn among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods, due to the offering of saffron and the like to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: tatas sugandhamukho devaputraś calavimalakuṇḍalahārārdhahāravibhūṣitagātro ratnacūḍaḥ kuṅkumatamālapattrādyalaṃkṛtagātras tām eva rātriṃ sugandhagandhena catuḥkrośaṃ sphuritvā yatra yatra gataḥ svargalokād avatīrya bhāryāyāḥ koṣṭhāgāre pratyasthāt // tataḥ sā imaṃ svapnam apaśyat // bhartā uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then the divine son <s>Sugandhamukha</s> (Fragrant-faced), his body adorned with sparkling, pure earrings, necklaces, and half-necklaces, with a jewel-crest, his body decorated with saffron, <s>tamāla</s>-leaf, and the like, that very night, having pervaded four <s>krośas</s> with the fragrance of sweet scent, wherever he went, descending from the heavenly world, he appeared in his wife's storehouse. Then she saw this dream. The husband said:

children.text: kānte jānīhi tvadbhartā mamaiva maraṇaṃ dhruvam /
children.translated_text: "O beloved, know that your husband — my death is certain.

children.text: tvaṃ na jānīṣi mā bhītā svargalokād ihāgataḥ // Dak_8.51 //
children.translated_text: You do not know; do not be afraid — I have come here from the heavenly world."
"By the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, not by any other [means], through the offering of saffron and the like,
having enjoyed the happiness of the divine world, I dwell in blissful ease."

body.text: kāśmīra

children.translated_text: <s>gośīrṣa</s>
sandalwood — those who give [these] to the best of <s>Sugatas</s> (Well-gone Ones),

children.text: te prāpnuvanti hy amarālayeṣu sugandhadehāḥ khalu ye manuṣyāḥ // Dak_8.53 //
children.translated_text: they indeed obtain fragrant bodies in the abodes of the immortals — those humans."

body.translated_text: "Saffron,

body.text:
buddheṣu dharmeṣu tathā ca saṃghe prasannacittā bhava cāpramattā /
tathā bhavethā

children.translated_text: thus may you become as I am, and quickly attain the path of well-being.

body.translated_text: "Be of serene mind toward the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Dharma</s>, and also the <s>Saṅgha</s>, and be vigilant;

body.text: iti jinānubhāvena svapatnīṃ dharmam upadeśya svabhavanaṃ gataḥ // tataḥ sā tathāvidhaṃ svapnaṃ dṛṣṭvā prabudhyati mahādbhūtaṃ ca saṃprāptā śokākulitamānasā //
body.translated_text: Thus, by the power of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor), having instructed his own wife in the <s>dharma</s>, he departed to his own abode. Then she, having seen such a dream, awoke, and having attained a great wonder, was overwhelmed with grief in her mind.

body.text:
tatotthāyāsanāt sā ca vimṛśya manasā punaḥ /
satyasvapnam imaṃ jñātvā duḥkho

children.translated_text: trembling seized her body, and tears

children.text: tanur nūnam aśru sravati locanāt // Dak_8.55 //
children.translated_text: indeed flowed from her eyes.

body.translated_text: Then, rising from her seat, reflecting again in her mind, knowing this to be a true dream, with body-hair standing on end from sorrow,

children.text: tataḥ kṛtvā samādhānaṃ nanāma sugatāya vai /
children.translated_text: Then, having composed herself, she bowed to the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-gone One):

children.text: rakṣa māṃ bhagavañ chāstaḥ kuru nātha anugraham // Dak_8.56 //
children.translated_text: "Protect me, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O Teacher; bestow your grace, O Lord."
Having spoken thus, with great serenity, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the best of <s>Sugatas</s>,

children.text: pūrvavad maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā aṣṭau dināni pūjitaḥ // Dak_8.57 //
children.translated_text: having prepared a <s>maṇḍala</s> as before, was worshipped for eight days.
Then, by the force of time, she too passed away,
and was reborn as a divine maiden among the exalted <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods.
She became a divine maiden named <s>Sugandhagandhinī</s> (Sweet-scented One);

children.text: bhartrā saha sukhenaiva svarge tiṣṭhati sā ciram // Dak_8.59 //
children.translated_text: together with her husband, she dwells happily in heaven for a long time.

body.text: tatas tau saṃbhāṣitau bhagavataḥ kuṅkumādidānād devalokeṣūpapannau // tasmād bhagavataḥ sakāśaṃ gacchāvaḥ paryupāsanāya vadanāyeti //
body.translated_text: Then those two conversed [and reflected]: 'Through offering saffron and the like to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, we have been reborn in the divine worlds. Therefore let us go to the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s> for attendance and [hearing] his discourse.'

body.text: tadā sugandhamukhadevaputrastrīpuruṣau sugandhagandhena catuḥkrośaṃ sphuritvā tām eva rātriṃ sarvaṃ jetavanamahāvihāram udāreṇāvabhāsya bhagavantaṃ candanādisugandhavarṣaiḥ pūrayitvā bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇau dharmaśravaṇāya //
body.translated_text: Then the divine son <s>Sugandhamukha</s> and his wife, having pervaded four <s>krośas</s> with their sweet fragrance, that very night, illuminating the entire <s>Jetavana</s> great monastery with splendor, having showered the <s>Bhagavān</s> with rains of sandalwood and other sweet fragrances, they sat before the <s>Bhagavān</s> to hear the <s>dharma</s>.

body.text: atha bhagavān sugandhamukhadevaputrayor āśayaṃ prakṛtiṃ ca jñātvā tādṛśī

children.translated_text: a <s>dharma</s>-discourse penetrating the Four Noble Truths,
hearing which, for those
two, man and woman,

children.text: viṃśatiśikharasamudgataṃ satkāyadṛṣṭiśailaṃ jñānavajreṇa bhittvā śrotāpattiphalaṃ sākṣātkṛtam // sa dṛṣṭasatyas trir udānam udānayati sma //
children.translated_text: the mountain of the view of the perishable aggregate (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), risen to twenty peaks, was split by the thunderbolt of knowledge, and the fruit of stream-entry (<s>śrotāpattiphala</s>) was directly realized. He, having seen the truth, uttered this inspired utterance (<s>udāna</s>) three times:

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, knowing the dispositions and natures of the divine son <s>Sugandhamukha</s> [and his wife], gave such

body.text: idam asmākaṃ bhadanta na mātrā kṛtaṃ na pitrā kṛtaṃ na rājñā na devatābhir neṣṭasvajanabandhuvargeṇa na pūrvapretair na śramaṇabrāhmaṇair yad bhagavatāsmākaṃ kṛtam

children.translated_text: the doors to the lower realms have been closed, and the doors to heaven have been established."

body.translated_text: "This, venerable one, was not done for us by our mother, not done by our father, not by a king, not by deities, not by beloved kinsmen and relatives, not by departed ancestors, not by ascetics and <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> — that which the <s>Bhagavān</s> has done for us:

children.text: tavānubhāvāt pihitaḥ sughoro hy apāyamārgo bahudoṣayuktaḥ /
children.translated_text: "By your power, the greatly terrible path to the lower realms, fraught with many faults, has been closed;

children.text: apāvṛtā svargagatiḥ supuṇyā nirvāṇamārgaś ca mayopalabdhaḥ // Dak_8.60 //
children.translated_text: the path to heaven, greatly meritorious, has been opened, and the path to <s>nirvāṇa</s> has been attained by me."

body.text: tvadāśrayāc cāptam apetadoṣaṃ nāv adya labdhaṃ suviśuddhacakṣuḥ / prāptaṃ ca śāntaṃ padam āryakāntaṃ tīrṇaṃ ca duḥkhārṇavapāram asmin //
body.translated_text: "By relying on you, the flawless [vision] has been obtained; today the thoroughly purified eye [of dharma] has been gained; the peaceful, noble, beloved state has been reached, and the far shore of the ocean of suffering has been crossed in this [life]."

children.translated_text: "O best of men, worshipped by men and gods, free from birth, old age, death, and disease,

children.text: bhavaśahasrasudurlabhadarśana saphalam adya mune tava darśanam // Dak_8.62 //
children.translated_text: O sage, whose sight is difficult to obtain in a thousand existences — fruitful indeed is your sight today."

body.text: avanamya bhagavataś caraṇau dvāv abhivandya jātasaṃharṣau gamiṣyāva ity ārocya suralokābhimukhaṃ divaṃ jagatuḥ //
body.translated_text: Bowing down and saluting the two feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, filled with joy, announcing 'we shall depart,' they went to the sky, facing toward the world of the gods.

body.text: atheha bhikṣavaḥ pūrvarātriṃ jāgarikāyogam anuyuktā viharanti / tair dṛṣṭo bhagavato 'ntike

children.translated_text: a magnificent radiance. Having seen it,

children.text: saṃdigdhā bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ // kiṃ bhagavann asyāṃ rātrau bhagavantaṃ darśanāya brahmā sahāpatiḥ śakro devendra uta catvāro lokapālā upasaṃkrāntāḥ //
children.translated_text: being doubtful, they asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, in this night, did <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, <s>Śakra</s> the lord of gods, or the four world-protectors come to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>?"

body.translated_text: Now here, the monks, engaged in the practice of wakefulness during the first watch of the night, were abiding. They saw in the vicinity of the <s>Bhagavān</s>

body.text: bhagavān āha // na bhikṣavo brahmā sahāpatir na śakro devendro nāpi catvāro lokapālā māṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrāntāḥ /
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "O monks, neither <s>Brahmā Sahāpati</s>, nor <s>Śakra</s> the lord of gods, nor the four world-protectors came to see me.

body.text: asau sautīrṇavaṇijo mahāsamudram avatīrṇaḥ / tato 'sau sautīrṇavaṇijo mahyaṃ kuṅkumādisugandhadravyāṇi dattvānya

children.text: preṣitaḥ / tataḥ pratyāgate durdaivayogān mahāmbudhau samudramadhye nāvaṃ bhagnībhūtvā samudre patitvā kālaṃ gataḥ // tasya patnī sugandhagandhinī devakanyā, tayā mayi prasannībhūya prāsādaśikhare sthitvā kuṅkumādisugandhair aṣṭau dināni pūjitaḥ, tayā praṇidhānaṃ kṛtam // yatre me svāmina
children.translated_text: was sent. Then, upon returning, by the force of ill fate, in the great ocean, in the middle of the sea, the ship broke apart, and falling into the sea, he died. His wife was <s>Sugandhagandhinī</s>, a divine maiden. She, having become devoted to me, standing on the top of a palace, worshipped [me] for eight days with saffron and other fragrances, and she made a vow: 'To the place where my husband

children.text: sthāne preṣyatāṃ sugata / iti tatpuṇyapraṇidhānavaśāt trāyatriṃśeṣu deveṣūpapannā // tāv imāṃ rātriṃ matsakāśam upasaṃkrāntau, tayor mayā dharma deśitam, dṛṣṭasatyau ca svabhavanaṃ gatau //
children.translated_text: is, may he be sent, O <s>Sugata</s>.' By the power of that meritorious vow, she was reborn among the gods of the Thirty-Three (<s>Trāyatriṃśa</s>). Those two came to my presence this night. To them I taught the <s>Dharma</s>, and having seen the truth, they returned to their own abode.

body.translated_text: That ocean-crossing merchant descended into the great ocean. Then that ocean-crossing merchant, having given to me saffron and other fragrant substances, [was reborn] in another

body.text: tasmāt tarhi bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam / yat triratneṣv upakāraṃ kuryān nāpakāram ity evaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyaṃ mamāntare mama nirvṛte //
body.translated_text: Therefore, O monks, you should train thus: 'One should do service to the Three Jewels, not disservice' — thus, O monks, you should train, in my presence and after my <s>nirvāṇa</s> (passing).

body.text: tato bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātā bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ // bhagavan ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyaya asau sautīrṇaḥ kuṅkumādigāndhikavastūni prahitāni, tvaddarśanam aprāpya samudramadhye kālagata iti //
body.translated_text: Then the monks, having become doubtful, asked the Blessed One: 'O Blessed One, what is the cause, what is the condition? That <s>Sautīrṇa</s> — the saffron and other fragrant goods were sent [by him], yet without attaining your sight, he died in the middle of the ocean.'

children.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'O monks, listen!

body.text:
bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavaḥ pradeśikamaṇḍalino rājaika asti /
tatrājiravatīnāmanadīpāre nātidūre nānāpādapadrumopaśobhite manoramavistāre saritpravāhite dharmarucir nāma ṛṣiḥ prativasati sma / sa nityaṃ dharma śrotuṃ gacchatīti //
body.translated_text: In ancient times, O monks, there was a king who was a regional ruler. There, not far from the bank of a river called <s>Ajiravatī</s>, in a charming expanse adorned with various trees, near a flowing river, a sage named <s>Dharmaruci</s> dwelt. He would always go to hear the <s>Dharma</s>.'

body.text: atha kadā cid ṛṣyāśramamārgāntare duṣṭajantor bhayam utpādita iti lokopavāda

children.text: śrutvā sa rājā sahāyair iṣudhanu sajjīkṛtya ṛṣyāśramaṃ gatavān // tata ṛṣyāśramaṃ prāpya gurupraṇāmaṃ kṛtvā nānāvinodakathālāpena sukhena tiṣṭhati // tataḥ sa munir dhanurbāṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā rājānam uvāca // alam anena rājan dhanurbāṇaṃ sajjīkṛtya
children.translated_text: that king, with his companions, having armed his bow and arrows, went to the sage's hermitage. Then, having reached the sage's hermitage, having bowed to the guru, he sat happily with various entertaining conversations. Then the sage, having seen the bow and arrows, said to the king: 'Enough of this, O king! Having armed your bow and arrows,
you have come.

children.text: ahaṃ duṣṭo na, me dṛṣṭvā rājan bhīto 'si vā punaḥ //
children.translated_text: I am not dangerous — seeing me, O king, are you afraid?'

body.translated_text: Now, once, having heard the rumor that on the path to the sage's hermitage, a dangerous creature had caused fear,

body.text: atha sa rājā karṇa

children.text: mṛṣṭvā praṇāmaṃ kṛtvāha / ma evaṃ brūhi guro tvadbhayaviṣādān na, kiṃ tu mārgānte duṣṭajantor bhayam utpādita iti lokopavādaṃ śrutvāgato 'ham iti //
children.translated_text: [in respect], having bowed, said: 'Do not speak thus, O guru! It is not out of fear or dismay of you, but rather, having heard the rumor that a dangerous creature had caused fear on the roadside, I have come.'

body.translated_text: Then that king, touching his ear

body.text: atha ṛṣir abravīt /
body.translated_text: Then the sage said:

children.text: mā khedaṃ kuru he rājan saṃsāreṣu asārake /
children.translated_text: 'Do not grieve, O king, in this insubstantial <s>saṃsāra</s>!

children.text: helayā cāparādhi syāt kathitaṃ tvayi bhūpate // Dak_8.63 //
children.translated_text: Through carelessness, one may offend — this has been said to you, O king.
In times of reaching peril, even one who sees does not truly see.

children.text: śrutam api na bhāvyaṃ te tasmāc cokto mahīdhara // Dak_8.64 //
children.translated_text: What is heard is also not to be trusted — therefore I have spoken, O lord of the earth.

body.text: śastre bhṛte prahāreyuḥ kasmiṃ

children.translated_text: some living being oneself.

children.text: samādhānaṃ tato bhūtvā krīyase dṛḍhacetasā // Dak_8.65 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, becoming composed, act with a firm mind.

body.translated_text: When weapons are borne, one might strike

children.text: kasmāc chāsitam itthaṃ te śṛṇu tvaṃ bhūpate punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Why have you been thus instructed? Listen again, O king:

children.text: akāraṇe gate prāṇe śastreṇa vidhyate yadi // Dak_8.66 //
children.translated_text: If, without cause, a life is taken by a weapon,

children.text: vyathayā prāṇinā tena pralāpaiḥ kandanena tu /
children.translated_text: by the suffering of that being, with lamentations and crying,

children.text: punaḥ śāpayate nūnaṃ doṣaśalyo hi jāyate // Dak_8.67 //
children.translated_text: it will surely curse — for the thorn of fault is born [from that].

children.text: ahiṃsā paramo dharma ahiṃsā paramaṃ tapaḥ /
children.translated_text: Non-violence is the supreme <s>dharma</s>; non-violence is the supreme austerity.

children.text: ahiṃsā paramaṃ jñānam ahiṃsā paramaṃ padam // Dak_8.68 //
children.translated_text: Non-violence is the supreme knowledge; non-violence is the supreme state.'

body.text: atha sa rājā tatheti satyam eva ity uktvā gurucaraṇau praṇāmaṃ kṛtvā pratinivṛttayati sahāyaiḥ saha pathi nānākathāvinodaiḥ //
body.translated_text: Then that king, saying 'so be it, truly so,' having bowed at the guru's feet, turned back with his companions, [passing the time] with various entertaining stories along the way.

body.text: tato nadīṃ niṣkramya, upā

children.text: dhaṃ prāptavān dṛṣṭaḥ / madhyāhne ravikiraṇair ātaptaiḥ pānīyaṃ pītvā tarucchāyāyām āśṛtāṃ mṛgapatnīṃ dadarśa //
children.translated_text: the uplands. At midday, having drunk water heated by the sun's rays, he saw a female deer resting in the shade of a tree.

body.translated_text: Then, crossing a river, he reached

body.text: atha sahasaiva sa rājā guror vacanaṃ vismāritas tāṃ mṛgapatnīṃ śareṇa bhinnaḥ / udare śaraṃ bhidyati // tato mṛgapatnī mānuṣyagirā rājānam evam āha //
body.translated_text: Then suddenly, the king, having forgotten the guru's words, pierced that female deer with an arrow. The arrow struck her belly. Then the female deer, with a human voice, spoke thus to the king:

body.text:
sādhu sādhu mahārāja kṛtas tvam uttamaṃ vratam /
tvaṃ ca rājarṣabha

children.translated_text: You, the best of royal bulls, born among the gods,
most righteous!

body.translated_text: 'Well done, well done, O great king! You have performed a supreme vow!

children.text: na mānuṣā cāsmi manuṣyavarya mṛgy apy ahaṃ tvadviṣayāntavāsā /
children.translated_text: I am not a human, O best of men — I am a deer, dwelling within your domain.

children.text: vṛddhā tvadīyena tṛṇodakena kathaṃ hi rājan tvayi khedayatnaḥ // Dak_8.70 //
children.translated_text: Nourished by your grass and water — how then, O king, is there this effort to harm me?
Having attained by the shelter of fortune the kingship desired by the world,

children.text: trātāsi loke vyasane bhayeṣu kathaṃ nu rājan śareṇa bhinno me // Dak_8.71 //
children.translated_text: you are the protector of the world in adversity and danger — how then, O king, have you pierced me with an arrow?
I am of animal birth, wretched, ignorant, and weak.

children.text: āhāro maithunaṃ nidrā paśuvṛttis tathā nṛpa // Dak_8.72 //
children.translated_text: Food, mating, and sleep — such is the conduct of animals, O king.
You are the authority over many <s>dharmas</s>, the discriminator of right and wrong,

children.text: bhūpāla iti vikhyātaḥ sarvalokaiḥ praśaṃsitaḥ // Dak_8.73 //
children.translated_text: renowned as 'king,' praised by all people.
Mighty to the weak, lord and refuge of the wretched —

children.text: īdṛśas tvaṃ mahārāja kathaṃ me jīva hāritaḥ // Dak_8.74 //
children.translated_text: such as you are, O great king, how have you taken my life?

children.text: viśeṣair gurviṇī cāham udarasthasya kā gatiḥ /
children.translated_text: Moreover, I am pregnant — what fate [awaits] the one in my womb?

children.text: asya mukhaṃ na paśyeyaṃ tenāsyaṃ paśyate na me // Dak_8.75 //
children.translated_text: I shall not see its face, nor shall it see mine.

body.text: punaś ca //
body.translated_text: And further:

children.text: na siṃhajātir na ca vyāghrajātir na ṛkṣajātir na ca sūkarī hy aham /
children.translated_text: I am not of lion birth, nor of tiger birth, nor of bear birth, nor a boar.

children.text: vṛkā na jātir na ca krūrajātis tvayā kimarthaṃ svaśareṇa bhinnā // Dak_8.76 //
children.translated_text: I am not of wolf birth, nor of any cruel birth — why have you pierced me with your arrow?
This is the conduct of cruel, fierce hunters,

children.text: asatyānāṃ ca duṣṭānām evācāravidho nṛpa // Dak_8.77 //
children.translated_text: of the shameless and likewise of the untruthful and wicked, O king.'

body.text: tato rājā idaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā śalyam iva gadgadakaṇṭhena pratyuttaraṃ dātuṃ na śaknoti // tatra kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīm āsthāya sa rājā mṛgapatnīm uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then the king, hearing these words, like a thorn [in his heart], with a choked throat, was unable to give a reply. Having remained silent there for a moment, the king spoke to the female deer:

body.text: kiṃ many

children.translated_text: think, O doe? Even when one has gone out hunting,

children.text: aparādhena lipto 'haṃ guror vacanaṃ nānyathā // Dak_8.78 //
children.translated_text: I am stained by this offense — the guru's words were not otherwise [i.e., were true].

body.translated_text: 'What do you

children.translated_text: Just as [when something is obtained] by chance, like a crow and a palm-fruit, [it is] created by delight —

children.text: na kiṃ cit krūracittena na ca te dveṣabhāvataḥ // Dak_8.79 //
children.translated_text: it was not with any cruel intent, nor from hatred toward you.'

body.text: mṛgapatny uvāca //
body.translated_text: The female deer said:

children.translated_text: 'What do you think, O great king? By grace toward oneself and others —

children.text: svakānāṃ ca parāṇāṃ ca śarīraṃ tulyam eva ca // Dak_8.80 //
children.translated_text: the bodies of one's own and of others are equal indeed.

children.text: sukhaduḥkhaṃ ca sarveṣāṃ kathaṃ na jñāyase nṛpa /
children.translated_text: The happiness and suffering of all — how do you not know this, O king?

children.text: mama prāṇaharas tvaṃ hi kiṃ vaktavyam ataḥ param // Dak_8.81 //
children.translated_text: You are the taker of my life — what more is there to say beyond this?'

body.text: ity uktvā sā mṛgī kālagatā //
body.translated_text: Having said this, that doe died.

body.text: tatas tasya bhartā mṛgaḥ samāyātaḥ ghrāṇo nocchvāsam āghrāya paśyati tāṃ mṛtaśarīrāṃ dṛṣṭvā ucchedakarīram iva sahasā bhūmau papāta / krameṇa smṛtim upasthāpya karuṇakaruṇair nānāvilāpaṃ cakāra //
body.translated_text: Then her mate, the male deer, came. Sniffing, not sensing breath, he saw her dead body, and like a tree uprooted, he suddenly fell to the ground. Gradually regaining consciousness, he made various lamentations, most piteous:

children.translated_text: 'Alas! O beloved, the delight of my life! How do you go alone?

children.text: māṃ vihāyādhunā tatra kathaṃ kena prahāritā // Dak_8.82 //
children.translated_text: Having now abandoned me, by whom have you been struck there?
Equal in uprightness, equal in knowledge, equal to me in valor —

children.text: tvadguṇaṃ kathaṃ vismṛtya manye kāntārabhīṣaṇam // Dak_8.83 //
children.translated_text: how can I forget your virtues? I consider [this world] a fearful wilderness.
No other friends exist — you alone are my beloved.

children.text: idānīṃ sneham utsṛjya kathaṃ te jīva hāritaḥ // Dak_8.84 //
children.translated_text: Now, having abandoned [your] love, how has your life been taken?'

body.text: tataḥ sa rājānam uvāca //
body.translated_text: Then he spoke to the king:

children.text: mama prāṇasameyaṃ strī patnī me jīvahāritā /
children.translated_text: 'This woman was equal to my very life — my wife's life has been taken!

children.text: atisnehatarā strī me kathaṃ te prāṇahāritā // Dak_8.85 //
children.translated_text: A woman of exceeding love for me — how has her life been taken by you?'

body.text: atha sa mṛgas tasmai śāpitaḥ // yathā me patnī nadīmadhye sthitvā prahāritena vyāpāditā / tathā tvaṃ samudramadhye pañcatvam upagacchatu // caturvarṇānāṃ hīnavarṇo bhavatv iti śanaiḥ svam āśramaṃ gato mṛgaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then that deer cursed him: 'Just as my wife, standing in the middle of the river, was killed by a blow — so may you die in the middle of the ocean! May you become the lowest of the four castes!' — and slowly the deer went to his own hermitage.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavas tena kālena tena samayena ṛṣir āsīd ahaṃ saḥ / yo 'sau sautīrṇaḥ sa rājābhūt // mṛgaśāpena śreṣṭhī bhūtvā samudramadhye kālagataḥ / kiṃ tu bauddhanāmānusmṛtya pramodya kuṅkumādidānato deveṣūpapannaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O monks? At that time, at that occasion, I was that sage. The one who was <s>Sautīrṇa</s> — he was that king. By the deer's curse, having become a merchant, he died in the middle of the ocean. But by recollecting the name of the <s>Buddha</s> and with joy, and by the gift of saffron and the like, he was reborn among the gods.'

body.text: mahānuśaṃsā bhikṣavaḥ kuṅkumādigandhadānasya tathāgateṣu mahānuśaṃsā //
body.translated_text: 'Of great benefit, O monks, is the gift of saffron and other fragrances to the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — of great benefit!'

body.text: punaś ca śṛṇu //
body.translated_text: And listen again:

children.translated_text: 'The celestial river <s>Mandākinī</s>, displaying the splendor of the breasts, hips, and thighs of playful women at the bathing-gates,
with abundant, blooming lotuses — when <s>Indra</s>, the lord of gods, bathes in it,
with beautiful women trembling with passion, repeatedly, out of respect for the best in the world —
such is the fruit of the gift of fragrant water, water for the feet, incense, flowers, garlands, and fragrances [to the Buddha].

children.text: yad rājā cakravartī viyati gataghanaiḥ kuṅkumāmbhaḥpravāhaiḥ
children.translated_text: When a <s>Cakravartin</s> king [bathes] in the Ganges with streams of saffron-water flowing through the sky from dispersed clouds,
fragrant with camphor, combined with the cool, sweet-smelling touch of sandalwood,

children.text: gaṅgāyām aṅgasaukhyaṃ paramam anubhavan modate sundarībhis
children.translated_text: experiencing supreme bodily bliss, and delighting with beautiful women —

children.text: tat tyāgāt kuṅkumāder guṇagaṇanidhaye buddhabhaṭṭārakāya // Dak_8.87 //
children.translated_text: such [is the fruit] of the gift of saffron and the like to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Lord, the treasury of hosts of virtues.
Having performed worship of the best of <s>Sugatas</s> with the sounds of <s>mṛdaṅga</s> (drums), <s>vīṇā</s> (lutes), and kettle-drums,

children.text: śṛṇoti śabdān suramānuṣāṇāṃ śrotraṃ ca divvaṃ labhate viśiṣṭam // Dak_8.88 //
children.translated_text: one hears the sounds of gods and humans, and obtains the excellent divine ear.'

body.text: iti śrīdvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ kuṅkumādidānakathāparivarto nāmāṣṭamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the chapter called 'The Story of the Gift of Saffron and the Like' — the eighth chapter.

body.text: IX. chattradānakathā
body.translated_text: IX. The Story of the Gift of a Parasol

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantam evam āha // bhagavan
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One: 'O Blessed One,

children.text: buddheṣu stūpabimbeṣu chattram udāraṃ pradiśanti ye /
children.translated_text: those who offer a magnificent parasol to <s>Buddhas</s>, <s>stūpas</s>, and images —

children.text: teṣāṃ phalaṃ kīdṛśaṃ syād bhāṣasva sugata prabho // Dak_9.1 //
children.translated_text: what fruit would there be for them? Speak, O <s>Sugata</s>, O Lord!'

body.text: evam ukte 'tha bhagavān kṣaṇam eva tūṣṇīm āsthāya, idaṃ mahānimittaṃ prādurbhāvam akarot svaṃ prabhāvasaṃdarśanārthaṃ buddhapūjāsaṃvartanārthaṃ buddhe 'prasannānāṃ cittānāṃ manaḥprasannasaṃjananārtham //
body.translated_text: When this was said, the Blessed One, having remained silent for a moment, manifested this great sign — for the purpose of displaying his own power, for the purpose of promoting the worship of the <s>Buddha</s>, and for the purpose of generating mental joy in the minds of those who were not devoted to the <s>Buddha</s>.

body.text: athānantaraṃ mahāpṛthivī ṣaḍvikāra

children.text: prakampitā, ā rasātalaṃ yāvat sumerum api / evaṃrūpāṇy adbhutāni bhavanty anyāni ca // tadyathā // saṃkṣiptāni viśālībhava
children.translated_text: down to the nethermost regions, up to [Mount] <s>Sumeru</s>. And wonders of such a kind occurred, and others too. Namely: what was contracted became expanded. Elephants trumpeted. Horses neighed. Various musical instruments in the houses sounded by themselves. The blind obtained sight. The deaf obtained hearing. The mute became capable of speech. Those with impaired faculties obtained complete faculties. The mad became free from madness. Those afflicted by poison became free from poison. Mutual enemies obtained friendliness. Pregnant women gave birth safely. Those bound in chains were freed from bondage. The poor obtained wealth. The hungry became full-bellied. The sick were freed from disease. And the gods in the sky released a rain of divine flowers.

children.text:
ti / hastinaḥ krośanti / aśvā hreṣante / gṛhagatāni vividhavādyabhāṇḍāni svayaṃ nadanti / andhāś cakṣuḥ pratilabhante / badhirāḥ
śrotraṃ labhante / mūkaḥ pravyāhārasamartho bhavati / indriyavikalā indriyāṇi pūrṇāni labhante / unmattā vigatamadā bhavanti, viṣapīḍitā nirviṣā bhavanti /
anyonyavairiṇo maitrīṃ pratilabhante / gurviṇyaḥ svastinā prajāyante /
bandhanabaddhā bandhanād vimucyante / adhanā dhanāni pratilabhante /
bubhukṣitāḥ pūrṇodarā bhavanti / rogārttā rogair vimuktā bhavanti / antarikṣāś ca devā divyapuṣpavarṣam utsṛjanti //

body.translated_text: Then immediately, the great earth shook with six kinds of tremors,

body.text: atha śakro devānām indra adhastāj jñānadarśanaṃ pravartya tatkṣanam eva svargalokāt prasarati / bhagavataḥ pūjārthaṃ svayam eva mahāpramāṇadivyasuvarṇaratnamayacchattraṃ dhṛtvā devagaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ tatra gṛddhakūṭaparvate samāyāti koṭipramāṇadundubhayaḥ pranādayan //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, directing his knowledge-vision downward, at that very moment descended from the heavenly world. For the purpose of worshipping the Blessed One, he himself, holding a great, divine parasol made of gold and jewels of vast proportions, together with the hosts of gods, came to <s>Gṛddhakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) Mountain, causing millions of kettledrums to resound.

body.text: atha śakro devānām indro bhagavantaṃ dadarśa

children.text: dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgataṃ kāñcanaparvatam iva śriyā jvalantaṃ bhagavantaṃ suvarṇaratnamayaiś chattraiḥ saṃchādita abhūt / tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavataḥ purastān niṣaṇṇaḥ //
children.translated_text: — endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, blazing with splendor like a golden mountain — [and] covered the Blessed One with parasols made of gold and jewels. Having circumambulated three times, having saluted the feet of the Blessed One with his head, he sat down before the Blessed One.

body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, saw the Blessed One

body.text: atha bhagavān dharmaṃ kathayā saṃdarśya samuttejayati saṃharṣayati //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, through the teaching of <s>Dharma</s>, instructed, inspired, and delighted [them].

body.text: ⟨anitya saṃsāram anitya koṣam anitya sauhṛdi saputradārā / anitya rājo vividhopabhogya

children.translated_text: In <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), everything is indeed impermanent.

body.translated_text: 'Impermanent is <s>saṃsāra</s>, impermanent is the treasury, impermanent are friendships, sons, and wives. Impermanent is the kingdom with its various enjoyments

body.text: dānaṃ vibhūṣaṇaṃ loke dānaṃ durgatinivāraṇam / dānaṃ svargasya sopāṇaṃ dānaṃ śāntikara

children.translated_text: and is auspicious.

body.translated_text: Giving is an ornament in the world; giving prevents an evil rebirth; giving is the staircase to heaven; giving brings peace

body.text: atha śakro devānām indraḥ saparivāro dharmaṃ śrutvā punar api divaṃ jagmuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, together with his retinue, having heard the <s>dharma</s>, departed again to heaven.

body.text: tadanantaraṃ parṣajjanās taddhetukaṃ cāveditamanasaḥ, teṣām āśayaṃ jñātvā bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ //
body.translated_text: Thereupon, the assembly members, their minds stirred by that [teaching], knowing their dispositions — the <s>bhikṣus</s>, in whom doubt had arisen, asked the Blessed <s>Buddha</s>, the cutter of all doubts:

body.text: kutremāni bhagavan kuśalamūlāni kṛtāni yato bhagavata evaṃvidhā pūjā bhikṣusaṃghasya ceti // bhagavān āha // tathāgatenaiva tāni bhikṣavaḥ pūrvam anyāsu jātiṣu karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavatpratyupasthitāny avaśyabhāvīni / mayaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni, ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati / na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāni pṛthivīdhātau nāpavāyvagniṣu vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca //
body.translated_text: 'Where were these wholesome roots (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) created, Blessed One, such that the Blessed One receives worship of this kind, and the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> as well?' The Blessed One said: 'It is the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, who formerly in other births performed and accumulated those actions, whose provisions have been gathered, whose conditions have ripened, which stand ready like a flood, and which are inevitable. These actions were performed and accumulated by me — who else would experience their fruits? O <s>bhikṣus</s>, actions that have been performed do not ripen in the earth element, nor in water, wind, or fire — whether wholesome or unwholesome.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte

children.text: dhvani kṣamāvatyāṃ mahānagaryām utpāditaḥ kṣemaṃkaro nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasarathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān etarhi tiṣṭhati saśiṣyaḥ // tena khalu punaḥ samayena anyatamajanapade rājadhānī āsīt / manoramā ṛddhisphītā subhikṣā cākīrṇabahujanaparivṛtā vidvajjanasampannā

At that time, in another land, there was a royal capital — delightful, prosperous, well-provisioned, thronging with many people,
and endowed with learned persons. In that royal capital, a great <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head,

body.translated_text: 'In a former time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past

body.translated_text: Then that great <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, on the fourth day, having prepared flowers, incense, fragrances, parasols, banners, and flags, cast a handful of flowers.

body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> asked the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>: 'From where, venerable Blessed One, has this invitation come?'

mahākṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣikto nimantraṇaṃ kṛtam /

children.translated_text: Thus [he spoke].

body.translated_text: 'The great <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head has made an invitation. We must go there — make ready, O <s>bhikṣus</s>!'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, on the fourth day, surrounded by the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s> — the Blessed <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, tamed, with a tamed retinue; calm, with a calm retinue; liberated, with a liberated retinue; wondrous, with a wondrous retinue; disciplined, with a disciplined retinue; an <s>Arhat</s>, with an <s>Arhat</s> retinue; free from passion, with a retinue free from passion; inspiring faith, with a faith-inspiring retinue — like a bull surrounded by a herd of cows; like an elephant surrounded by a herd of young elephants; like a lion surrounded by a group of fanged beasts; like a royal swan surrounded by a flock of geese; like a <s>Suparṇī</s> (great bird) surrounded by a flock of birds; like a learned one surrounded by a group of students; like the horse <s>Bālāha</s> surrounded by a herd of horses; like a guide surrounded by a group of travel

body.text: aśrauṣīd rājā mahākṣatriyo mūrdhnābhiṣiktaḥ kṣemaṃkarasamyaksaṃbuddhaś cāsmākaṃ rājadhānīm anuprāpta iti śrutvā ca mahatyā rājarddhyā mahatā rājānubhāvena samanvāgato yena bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya kṣemaṃkarasya samyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ //
body.translated_text: The king, the great <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, heard that the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> had arrived at their royal capital. Having heard, endowed with great royal splendor and great royal majesty, he approached the Blessed <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One; having approached, having bowed his head at the feet of the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, he sat down to one side.

body.text: atha rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ mūrdhnābhiṣiktaṃ kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati // athā sa rājā labdhaprasādajātaḥ kṣemaṃkaraṃ samyaksaṃbuddhaṃ rājakule nimantrya śatarasena bhojanena pratipāditaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> instructed the king, the <s>Kṣatriya</s> anointed on the head, with teachings conducive to awakening. Then that king, having gained faith, having invited the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s> to the royal palace, served him with a meal of a hundred flavors.

body.text: śatasahasramūlyena suvarṇacchattreṇa saṃchādayām āsa //
body.translated_text: He covered [the Buddha] with a golden parasol worth a hundred thousand [coins].

body.text: atha sa bhagavān kṣemaṃkaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddho dharmavarsaṃ pravarṣitum ārabdhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, began to rain down the <s>dharma</s>-shower:

children.translated_text: 'Well done, well done, O great king! Most excellent is the great meritorious vow!

children.text: chattrāvarohaṇaṃ yena, īdṛśaṃ phalam āpyate // Dak_9.3 //
children.translated_text: By the offering of the parasol, such fruit is obtained.'

with a parasol that blocks the sun like the halo of the moon —

children.text: tad api phalam udāraṃ chattradānāt prasūtam // Dak_9.4 //
children.translated_text: even that noble fruit is born from the gift of a parasol.'

body.text: hemacchattratiraskṛtārkakiraṇā

children.translated_text: seated on the shoulders of splendid, well-trained elephants,
adorned with many jewels, rivaling the majesty of <s>Śakra</s>,
kings who are <s>Cakravartins</s> of the four continents travel through the sky playfully —
that fruit comes from the gift of flower-parasols at <s>caityas</s> containing <s>Tathāgata</s> relics.'

body.translated_text: 'With the radiance of the sun eclipsed by golden parasols,

body.text: punas ca vistareṇa śṛṇu / tathāgatebhyaś chattrapradānato rājā bhavati cakravartī caturaṅgo vijitavān dhārmiko dharmarājaḥ saptaratnasamanvāgataḥI // tadyathā //
body.translated_text: 'Listen further in detail. From the gift of a parasol to <s>Tathāgatas</s>, one becomes a king, a <s>Cakravartin</s>, possessing four divisions [of an army], victorious, righteous, a king of <s>dharma</s>, endowed with the seven jewels. Namely:'

so with supernatural power, by the path of the sky, he returned to his own monastery.

body.translated_text: 'The wheel-jewel, the elephant-jewel, the horse-jewel, the woman-jewel, the gem-jewel, the householder-jewel, and the general-jewel. body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who was the king at that time, in that era — I was he. Because I, with faith, placed a parasol on the <s>stūpas</s> of the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Kṣemaṃkara</s>,

body.translated_text: Then <s>Dhātustejas</s> arrived at a supremely extensive, level, and flat terrain not very far from there. Then in the king's mind arose an eagerness to sport at the speed of a horse. The king rested his companions there. Then the king rode at horse-speed twice, three times. Then, carried away by the exceedingly swift horse, he went far. In a very distant place, the horse abandoned him, and the king fainted. When the faint passed, the king regained consciousness in a moment. The horse had gone out of sight. Then all the companion-people, having lost sight of the king, became disheartened and turned back.

children.translated_text: As he went on the southern path, thus from this path — going again by the southern path, he saw a great expanse of burning hot sand, and then he approached the banks. He saw sand ablaze like burning fire. Seeing that, with a mind distraught, he thought: 'How can one proceed? Where should I go?' While he stood thus, a fearsome creature appeared — neither horse, nor donkey, nor camel, nor cow — its facial form was unrecognizable. A single creature, having approached, spoke to him: 'O man, mount upon my back! How can one proceed on this sand-expanse? If you walk, your soft feet, like wheat-grain, will be shattered as if by pestle-blows. Therefore mount upon my back — I shall carry you to the other bank.' He mounted, and then it carried him swiftly. At that very moment, having reached the bank, that creature disappeared.
