body.translated_text: Then the beings of <s>Magadha</s>, at that time, were coming to <s>Gṛddhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak). <s>Dhātustejas</s> saw them and asked: 'Where are you going?' They said: 'We are going to <s>Gṛddhrakūṭa</s> to see the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>.' <s>Dhātustejas</s>, hearing the name '<s>Buddha</s>' — never heard before — all the pores of his body thrilled, and the greatest curiosity arose.

body.text: tataḥ sa dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samanvāgatam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyomaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajāto bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā purato niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya //
body.translated_text: Then he beheld the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), endowed with the thirty-two marks of a great being, his body adorned with eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with a halo of light, [radiant] like a thousand suns.

body.text: atha bhagavān āśayaṃ jñātvā caturāryasatyaprativedhikī dharmadeśanā kṛtā // yāṃ śrutvā prasādajāto bhagavantam etad avocat // bhagavan vyākarotu

children.translated_text: a prophecy of supreme, perfect awakening!"

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), knowing his disposition, gave a <s>Dharma</s> discourse penetrating the Four Noble Truths. Having heard it, with faith arisen, he said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, please give me a prophecy—

body.text: atha bhagavān āha // bhaviṣyasi tvaṃ kulaputra dhātuśikharanāmalokadhāto

children.text: dhātustejo nāma tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān iti
children.translated_text: shall become a <s>Tathāgata</s> (Thus-Gone One) named <s>Dhātustejas</s>, an <s>Arhat</s> (Worthy One), perfectly and fully awakened, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, a <s>Buddha</s>—"

children.text: vyākaraṇaṃ śrutvā pravrajyāgrahaṇaṃ cakāra // tatkṣaṇe sākṣād arhattvaṃ prāptam //
children.translated_text: Having heard the prophecy, he took ordination as a renunciant. At that very moment, he directly attained <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat).

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "You, O son of good family, in the world-realm named <s>Dhātuśikhara</s>,

body.text: tato bhikṣavas taṃ dṛṣṭvāścaryajātā bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ / ko 'sau bhagavan tvayā samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛta iti //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), seeing him, were filled with wonder and asked the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "Who is he, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, whom you have prophesied for perfect awakening?"

body.text: bhagavān āha // dakṣiṇāpathi dharmakalpo nāma rājā mahāpratāpavān dharmiṣṭhaḥ / tasya rājñaḥ suto 'sau //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "In the southern region, there was a king named <s>Dharmakalpa</s>, of great majesty, righteous. He is the son of that king."

body.text: bhikṣava ūcuḥ // kāni bhadanta tena karmāṇi kṛtāni yenābhirūpo darśanīya

children.text: prāsādikas tejaḥ pravrajyārhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti // bhagavān āha //
children.translated_text: inspiring of faith, radiant, and has directly realized <s>arhattva</s> through renunciation?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said:

body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) said: "What deeds, O Venerable One, did he perform, that he is handsome, pleasing to behold,

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte

children.text: dhvani ekanavatikalpe vipaśvī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuśyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān bandhumatīṃ mahārājadhānīṃ nagarīm upaniśritya viharati sma // atha sa bhagavān sakalabuddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayāgnir iva nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinivṛtaḥ / tasmā
children.translated_text: era, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), a perfectly and fully awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśvin</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans—

children.text: rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanastūpaṃ kāritaṃ krośam uccatvena //
children.translated_text: King <s>Bandhumant</s>, having performed worship of his bodily relics, had a <s>stūpa</s> built, a <s>yojana</s> (league) in extent on every side, a <s>krośa</s> (quarter-league) in height.

body.translated_text: "Long ago, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past

body.text: tena samayena anyatamaśreṣṭhiputreṇa taṃ dṛṣṭvā prasādajātena pitrā sādhitā

children.text: nānādhātumahārajatarūpyaratnakūṭāni gṛhītvā tasmin vipaśvinaḥ stūpagarbhe dhātur āropitaḥ // tena praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ
children.translated_text: and taking various great gold, silver, and jeweled pinnacles, he placed a relic in the reliquary chamber of <s>Vipaśvin</s>'s <s>stūpa</s>. He made this aspiration:

children.text: anenāhaṃ kuśalena paścime samaye paścime kāle paścimake tathāgate 'nuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhau vyākaraṇaṃ pratilabheyam iti //
children.translated_text: "By this merit, in the final time, in the final age, in the presence of the last <s>Tathāgata</s>, may I receive a prophecy of supreme, perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: At that time, a certain merchant's son, seeing it and having faith arisen, [requested] from his father the means,

body.text: tena putreṇa kṛtakuśalamūlena tasya pitā dakṣiṇapathi dharmakalpo nāma rājā babhūva, tasya putro dhātustejaḥ pūrvajanmany api pitāputrau //
body.translated_text: By the roots of merit planted by that son, his father became King <s>Dharmakalpa</s> of the southern region—in their previous births too they were father and son.

body.text: bhagavān āha // kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhiputra āsīd ayaṃ sa dhātustejarājā

children.text: vipaśvinaḥ stūpe dhātum āropitaṃ / tena hetunā abhirūpaḥ prāsādiko darśanīyataraḥ
children.translated_text: He placed a relic in the <s>stūpa</s> of <s>Vipaśvin</s>. By that cause, he became handsome, inspiring of faith, and most pleasing to behold.

children.text: arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti // mayāpi samyaksaṃbodhau vyākṛtaḥ //
children.translated_text: He directly realized <s>arhattva</s> (the state of an Arhat). And by me too he has been prophesied for perfect awakening."

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who was at that time, in that era, the merchant's son—he is this King <s>Dhātustejas</s>.

body.text: bhagavān punar uvāca // mahānuśaṃsā maitreya mahānuśaṃsā bhikṣavas tathāgatasya stūpabimbeṣu dhātvavaropaṇānāṃ naikaphalānuśaṃsā // tac chṛṇuta //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) further said: "Of great benefit, O <s>Maitreya</s>, of great benefit, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, is the installation of relics in <s>stūpas</s> and images of the <s>Tathāgata</s>—of manifold fruits and benefits. Listen to this:

children.translated_text: He who is well-established on the path of the <s>Sugata</s>'s (Well-Gone One's) perfections on earth,
becomes one of celebrated fame, a refuge for all beings;
endowed with the prosperity of an exceedingly lofty and firm nature—

children.text: jinapratikṛtau janena yadi dhātur āropyate // Dak_10.4 //
children.translated_text: when a relic is installed by a person in an image of the <s>Jina</s> (Victor).

children.text: śakrīṃ samantād adhigamya lakṣmīṃ dvīpāṃś ca bhuktvā caturo narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings, having attained the glory of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) on every side and having enjoyed the four continents,

children.text: ante viśuddhaṃ padam āpnuvanti dhātoḥ samāropaṇato jinasya // Dak_10.5 //
children.translated_text: in the end attain the pure state, from the installation of a relic of the <s>Jina</s>.
That mortals are seen in the mortal world as beautiful, with moon-like faces, fine brows, and long eyes,
resembling the finest gold, endowed with patience and gentleness—

children.text: pṛthvīṃ yac cāpi rājā jalanidhivasanāṃ pālayaṃś cakravartī
children.translated_text: and that a king rules the earth girdled by oceans as a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch)—

children.text: tat sarvaṃ buddhabimbe bhavati tanubhṛtāṃ dhātum āropya bhaktyā // Dak_10.6 //
children.translated_text: all that arises for embodied beings from devotedly installing a relic in a <s>Buddha</s> image.

children.text: tasmād bhikṣavo mamāntare mama nirvṛte 'nāyake loke idaṃ sūtraṃ deśayitavyam /
children.translated_text: "Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in my absence, when I have attained <s>nirvṛti</s> (final peace) and the world is without a guide, this <s>sūtra</s> should be taught.

children.text: śrutvā ca prasādo bhavati prasādajāte tathā kariṣyati tathā ca kṛtvā tatphalaṃ prāpyate dhruvam //
children.translated_text: Having heard it, faith arises; when faith has arisen, one will act accordingly; and having acted thus, that fruit is certainly obtained."

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ dhātvavaropaṇakathā daśamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story of relic installation, the tenth chapter.

body.text: XI. maṇḍalakathā
body.translated_text: XI. The Story of the <s>Maṇḍala</s> (Sacred Circle)

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo dhātvavaropaṇaphalānuśaṃsāṃ śrutvā bhagavantaṃ punar evam āha //
body.translated_text: Then indeed, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, having heard the benefits and fruits of relic installation, again spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: bhagavañ śrotum icchāmi, maṇḍalaṃ sugatasya ca /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I wish to hear: regarding the <s>maṇḍala</s> (sacred circle) of the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One),

children.text: kriyate yena pūjārtham, phalaṃ teṣāṃ kathaṃ vibho // Dak_11.1 //
children.translated_text: which is made for the purpose of worship—what is the fruit thereof, O Powerful One?"

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said:

children.translated_text: "One becomes golden-complexioned, freed from all diseases,
distinguished among gods and humans, with radiant beauty like the moon;
prosperous with wealth and gold, one is born in a royal lineage—
he who makes a <s>maṇḍala</s> in this excellent abode of the <s>Sugata</s>."

body.text: iti bhāṣitvā bhagavān tūṣṇībhūtaḥ sthitaḥ / tathānuṣṭhite bhagavān saṃcintayati //
body.translated_text: Having spoken thus, the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) remained silent. When it was thus established, the <s>Bhagavān</s> reflected:

body.text: candraprabho bodhisattva ihāgacchatv iti sahacittotpādād bhagavataś candraprabho bodhisattvaś candrāvabhāsalokadhātor antarhitaḥ / tatkṣaṇam eva ṛddhyā vihāyasā āgatya gṛddhakūṭe bhagavataḥ purato niṣaṇṇaḥ // sa bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivanditvā, ekānte niṣīdati

children.text: sa ca sākṣāc candra iva rūpasaundaryaś candra iva prabhāvirājitaśītaraśmiḥ
children.translated_text: He indeed, like the moon itself in beauty of form, with cool rays shining with the radiance of the moon—
a <s>yojana</s> (league) in every direction was illuminated by his splendor.

body.translated_text: "Let the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s> (Moonlight) come here." With that very arising of thought from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s> vanished from the world-realm <s>Candrāvabhāsa</s> and at that very moment, by miraculous power—

body.text: atha sa bodhisattva utthāyāsanād bhagavantaṃ tridhā pradakṣinīkṛtya uttarāsaṅgaṃ kṛtvā dakṣiṇajānumaṇḍalaṃ pṛthivyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpyā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇamya bhagavantam etad avocat // bhagavan kasmin sati bhavapratyayo jāyate / kasya nirodho nirodhāt punar bhavet / kiṃ bhavo nirudhyate //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>bodhisattva</s>, rising from his seat, having circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, having arranged his upper robe, having placed his right knee on the ground, facing the <s>Bhagavān</s> with joined palms—

body.text: bhagavān āha // sādhu sādhu candraprabha / bhikṣavaḥ paśya

children.text: yūyam api tathā śṛṇotha / idaṃ sūtraṃ saṃprakāśayiṣye daśabalasamanvāgato
children.translated_text: you too, listen thus. I shall illuminate this <s>sūtra</s>. Endowed with the ten powers,

children.text: haṃ caturvaiśāradyaviśārada udārām ārṣabhaṃ parṣadi siṃhanādaṃ nadāmi / yad utāsmin satīdaṃ bhavaty asyotpād
children.translated_text: skilled in the four kinds of fearlessness, I roar the noble, bull-like lion's roar in the assembly: When this exists, that comes to be; from the arising of this,
that arises. That is: from the condition of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance)

children.text: saṃskāraḥ, saṃskārapratyayād vijñānaṃ vijñānapratyayān nāmarūpaṃ nāmarūpapratyayāt ṣaḍāyatanaṃ saḍāyatanapratyayāt sparśaḥ sparśapratyayāt tṛṣṇā tṛṣṇāpratyayād upādānam upādānapratyayād bhavo bhavapratyayāj jātir jātipratyayāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā
children.translated_text: arise <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from the condition of formations, <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from the condition of consciousness, <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form); from the condition of name-and-form, the six <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases); from the condition of the sense-bases, <s>sparśa</s> (contact); from the condition of contact, <s>tṛṣṇā</s> (craving); from craving—

children.text: saṃbhavanti / evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya samudayo bhavati / yad utāsmin na satīdaṃ na (
children.translated_text: they arise. Thus is the origination of this entire great mass of suffering. When this does not exist, that does not

children.text: ) satīdaṃ na bhavati / asya nirodhād idaṃ nirudhyate / yad utāvidyānirodhāt saṃskāranirodhaḥ saṃskāranirodhād vijñānanirodho vijñānanirodhān nāmarūpanirodho nāmarūpanirodhāt ṣaḍāyatananirodhaḥ ṣaḍāyatananirodhāt sparśanirodhaḥ sparśanirodhād vedanānirodho vedanānirodhāt tṛṣṇānirodhas tṛṣṇānirodhād upādānanirodha upādānanirodhād bhavanirodho bhavanirodhāj jātinirodho jātinirodhāj jarāmaraṇaśokaparidevaduḥkhadaurmanasyopāyāsā nirudhyante / evam asya kevalasya mahato duḥkhaskandhasya nirodho bhavati / svākhyāto me bhikṣavo dharma uttāno vivṛtaś chinnaplotiko yāvad devamanuṣyebhyaḥ samyak saṃprakāśitaḥ //
children.translated_text: come to be; from the cessation of this, that ceases. That is: from the cessation of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), the cessation of <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations); from the cessation of formations, the cessation of <s>vijñāna</s> (consciousness); from the cessation of consciousness, the cessation of <s>nāmarūpa</s> (name-and-form)—

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "Well done, well done, <s>Candraprabha</s>! O <s>bhikṣus</s>, behold—

body.text: asmin khalu dharmaparyāye bhāṣyamāṇe candraprabheṇa bodhisattvena aṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmāḥ pratilabdhā

children.translated_text: and attained the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections)
as well.

body.translated_text: When this <s>Dharma</s> discourse was being spoken, the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s> attained the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>,

body.text: atha khalu bhagavāṃs tasyaiva vyākaraṇam anuprayacchati //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) bestowed upon him this very prophecy:

body.text: sādhu sādhu kulaputra, asmiṃs tava lokadhātau candraprabho nāma tathāgato 'rhan bhaviṣyatīti //
body.translated_text: "Well done, well done, O son of good family! In this world-realm of yours, there shall be a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, named <s>Candraprabha</s>."

children.translated_text: "Endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed,

children.text: devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ śāstā loke bhaviṣyati // Dak_11.3 //
children.translated_text: he shall be a teacher of gods and humans in the world."

body.text: atha sa bodhisattvo bhagavatas tathāgatasya vyākaraṇam anuprāpya prasādajātena bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā svabhavanaṃ prakrāntaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then that <s>bodhisattva</s>, having received the prophecy from the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with faith arisen, circumambulated the <s>Bhagavān</s> three times, bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with his head, and departed to his own abode.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavas tasya bodhisattvasya abhirūpa

children.text: darśanīyaṃ prāsādikaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā bhagavantam eva ūcuḥ // kāni bhadanta candraprabheṇa bodhisattvena karmāṇi kṛtāni, abhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādikaḥ // bhagavān āha //
children.translated_text: pleasing, and faith-inspiring [appearance] of that <s>bodhisattva</s>, said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "What deeds, O Venerable One, were performed by the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>, that he is handsome, pleasing, and faith-inspiring?" The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.translated_text: Then indeed, the <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having seen the handsome,

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavatikalpe vipaśvī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ sastā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaśritya viharati sma // tena khalu punaḥ samayena bhagavān vipaśvī samyaksaṃbudhha ihaiva vihārān niṣkramya trāyatriṃśeṣu bhavaneṣu viharati //
body.translated_text: "Long ago, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past era, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a perfectly and fully awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśvin</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed—

body.text: atha te janakāyā bhagavantaṃ vinā sthātumano notsahante // tatas te janakāyā bhagavato vipaśvinaḥ śrāvakottama

children.text: sunandabhikṣus tam ūcuḥ // kva gacchati bhagavān vipaśvī ciraṃ divasam adṛṣṭvā sarve janakāyā bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum ākāṅkṣamāṇāḥ sthitāḥ //
children.translated_text: the <s>bhikṣu</s> (monk) <s>Sunanda</s>, said to him: "Where has <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vipaśvin</s> gone? Not having seen him for many days, all the people stand here longing to see the <s>Bhagavān</s>."

body.translated_text: Then those people could not bear to remain without the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Then those people, [seeking] the foremost disciple of <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vipaśvin</s>,

body.text: sunandabhikṣur āha // ihaiva vihāre 'ham ekas tiṣṭhāmi, sa mayāpi darśanaṃ na prāpto bhagavān //
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Sunanda</s> said: "I alone remain here in the monastery; even I have not obtained a sight of the <s>Bhagavān</s>."

body.text:
tena khalu punaḥ samayenānyatamaḥ śreṣṭhī mahārddho dharmakāmaḥ śuddhāśayo bhagavantam arcanārthaṃ puṣpadhūpādīni gṛhītvā vipaśyinaḥ
samyaksaṃbuddhasya vihāre praviśati // tatas tena bhagavantam adṛṣṭvā pṛṣṭaḥ /
bhagavān kva gacchati / kutra viharati / aho mandabhāgyasya bhagavān na prāpta iti //

Thereafter, that merchant, having had it constructed, descended to the street and summoned all the townspeople, saying: "All those who desire to worship the <s>Tathāgata</s> should worship at that <s>maṇḍala</s>, until the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Vipaśvī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened One, arrives." Having heard that, from then on all the people of <s>Bandhumatī</s>, having seen it and being filled with faith, performed worship for the sake of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: Then, at another time, the merchant, having worshipped at the <s>maṇḍala</s>, made an aspiration: "By this root of merit, may I become a forest-dwelling <s>Bodhisattva</s>; and at the coming of the final teaching, may I obtain the prophecy of enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhivyākaraṇa</s>)." Thus the aspiration was made. Then, having generated faith in the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>, having died, he was conceived in the womb of the queen of King <s>Kauravya</s>. After the passage of nine months, a son was born — handsome, pleasing, and beautiful to behold. When, at the very moment of his birth, the entire city was illuminated by his radiance (

children.translated_text: hunchbacked, deaf, deficient in their faculties, afflicted by diseases — he saw them. Some were proud with the intoxication of beautiful form and youth, thundering — he saw them. Having seen them, this thought arose in him: "In this <s>saṃsāra</s> (cycle of existence), everything is indeed calamity; this body is filled with impurity and sin,
a place of disease and grief,
filled with fear,

There is no means of preventing old age and death. Therefore I should seek the means of crossing the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>." Having thus reflected, he entered the royal palace and became

children.translated_text: "From desire arises greed; from greed arises grief;

children.translated_text: by grief the body withers; death is reached therein."

body.text:
tasmāt sukhaṃ na paśyāmi mānuṣāṇāṃ kadā cana /

body.translated_text: "In such an essenceless [existence], who would seize the essence?"

body.text: tataḥ sa candraprabhaḥ pitaraṃ rājānaṃ vijñāpitavān // tāta śṛṇu me vāñchā

body.translated_text: Then <s>Candraprabha</s> informed his father the king: "Father, hear my wish

children.translated_text: "Giving (<s>dāna</s>) is a great treasure, a companion [that follows one], not shared by thieves and the like;
giving is the washing of the mind from the dust of the faults of avarice and greed;
giving is a vehicle of happiness that removes the fatigue of the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>;
giving is a true, eternal friend, fair-faced, that bestows manifold happiness."
"Whether one desires the arising of wealth, or splendor, or the virtue of authority,
or dwelling in the city of the gods, or the virtue of beauty and charm —

children.text: yad abhilaṣati sarvaṃ tat samāpnoti dānād
children.translated_text: whatever one desires, all that is obtained through giving;

body.translated_text: "Therefore I request [your permission]."

body.text: tato janakaḥ prahasan tam uvāca // aho śuddhaceto durāsada, bālo 'pi dānam eva rocate // punar āha // putra candraprabha kiin bhāṣase

children.translated_text: Indeed, in your domain, the food-house and drink-house,
filled with gold, silver, gems, and pearls — all that is under your control.
Give gifts as you wish, according to your intention."

body.translated_text: Then the father, laughing, said to him: "O one of pure mind, hard to approach — even as a boy, giving alone delights [you]!" He said again: "Son <s>Candraprabha</s>, what do you say?

body.text: sa āha // tāta sādhu bhadraṃ bhavatu // ity uktvā pitur vācaḥ śirasā nidhāya, śramaṇabrāhmaṇavaṇīpakebhyo dānāni dadāti puṇyāni karoti //
body.translated_text: He said: "Father, excellent! May it be auspicious!" Having said this and receiving his father's words on his head [with respect], he gave gifts to ascetics, <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, and traders, and performed meritorious deeds.

body.text: atha tasya dārakasya candraprabhasya saṃsāranairguṇyaṃ bahudoṣayuktaṃ matvā agāramadhyā vasituṃ mano na ramate / vanaprasthaṃ gantumana iti cintitavān //
body.translated_text: Then the boy <s>Candraprabha</s>, having understood that <s>saṃsāra</s> is devoid of qualities and full of many faults, his mind did not delight in dwelling in a household. He thought of going to the forest as a hermit.

body.text: tasyaitad abhavat //
body.translated_text: This thought arose in him:

body.text: ayuktam etan mātāpitarāv anivedya kathaṃ gaccheyam / ata eva mātāpitarāv agre nivedya vanaprasthaṃ gaccheyam ity ārocya yena pitā tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya pitarau cāha // tātānujānīhi me gṛhāvāse bahudoṣajālaṃ matvāhaṃ vānaprastho bhaveyaṃ tat tavājñāṃ dehīti //
body.translated_text: "It is improper — how can I go without informing my parents? Therefore, I should first inform my parents and then go to the forest as a hermit." Having thus announced, he approached his father and said to his parents: "Father, permit me; having understood the net of many faults in household life, I would become a forest hermit — give me your permission for that."

body.text: evam uktau pitarau sāśruvadanau gadgadakaṇṭham ucchvāsya tam ūcatuḥ // nārhaty atrātmaja nau hṛdaye śokaśalyavraṇam asaṃrūḍham eva udghaṭayituṃ parameṇa duḥkheneti //
body.translated_text: Thus addressed, the parents, with tear-filled faces, sighing with choked throats, said to him: "O son, it is not proper for you to tear open the wound of the grief-thorn in our hearts that has not yet healed, with supreme suffering."

children.text: tathā kṣamaṃ vetsi gṛhānurāgaṃ śreyaḥpathaṃ vā vanavāsasaukhyam /
children.translated_text: "You know well the attachment to home, and [also] the path to the highest good and the happiness of forest-dwelling;

body.text: tac chrutvā sa āha // paśyatu deva //
body.translated_text: Having heard that, he said: "May the king observe:"

children.translated_text: "In a home that is the abode of heedlessness, intoxication, lust, greed, and hatred,
what scope is there for <s>dharma</s>, which is opposed to all that?"
"Dragged about by many evil deeds, troubled by the acquisition, earning, and guarding of possessions,

children.translated_text: with an unpeaceful mind, assailed by the onset of calamities — when will a householder attain the path of tranquility?"

body.translated_text: There, having generated immeasurable <s>dhyānas</s> (meditations), he ascended to the heavens.

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena śreṣṭhī āsīt / ayam asau candraprabho bodhisattvo vipaśvinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya vihāre suvarṇamayamaṇḍalaṃ nirmāpitaḥI / tena karmaṇo vipākena kauravyakule rājatvam anubhūya bodhisattvo bhūtvāṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmā

children.translated_text: were obtained [by him]. He was also prophesied by me for supreme enlightenment. As the aspiration was made, so it came to be — not otherwise."

body.translated_text: "What do you think, O monks? He who at that time and occasion was the merchant — he was this <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Candraprabha</s>. He had a golden <s>maṇḍala</s> constructed in the monastery of <s>Vipaśvī</s>, the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddha</s>. As the ripening of that deed, having experienced kingship in the <s>Kauravya</s> lineage, becoming a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, the eighteen unique qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>

) The great fruits and benefits of the <s>maṇḍala</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — [their] fruits and benefits:

distinguished among gods and humans, with radiance brilliant as the moon;

whoever makes a <s>maṇḍala</s> in this excellent abode of the <s>Sugata</s>."
"They attain sovereignty over people at once,
long-lived, freed from the fears of various diseases;

body.text: XII. bhojanakathā
body.translated_text: XII. The Story of the Food Offering

body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva</s> <s>Mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, for the sake of generating wholesome [inclinations] in beings, again said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

At one time, together with the community of listeners (<s>Śrāvakas</s>), I was dwelling in <s>Rājagṛha</s>, in the <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove), at the <s>Kalandakanivāpa</s> (Squirrel-feeding Ground).

body.text: tasminn avasare tatra anyataraḥ śreṣṭhī gṛhapatiḥ prativasati sma / āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī tīrth

He was converted by the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, brought into the teaching, and became exceedingly devoted to the <s>Bhagavān</s>. That householder was of noble disposition, and he said to the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>: 'Be my companion; I wish to make an offering to the <s>Bhagavān</s>.'

children.translated_text: The venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> consented to that householder's [request] by remaining silent.

body.translated_text: "On that occasion, a certain merchant householder resided there — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, of extensive property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, devoted to the

body.text:
athāyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyanas taṃ gṛhapatim ādāya yena bhagavāṃs
tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ /
ekānte niṣaṇṇa āyuṣmān mahāmaudgalyāyano bhagavantam idam avocat // ayaṃ bhadanta gṛhapatir ākāṅkṣati bhagavantaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ bhojayitum iti / tad asya bhagavān adhivāsayann anukampām upādāyeti

children.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s>
consented to that householder's [request] by remaining silent.

body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s>, taking that householder, approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having saluted the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> with his head, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the venerable <s>Mahāmaudgalyāyana</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: "This householder, venerable sir, wishes to feed the <s>Bhagavān</s> together with the community of listeners. May the <s>Bhagavān</s> consent to his [request], out of compassion."

body.text: atha sa gṛhapatir bhagavatas tūṣṇībhāvenādhivāsanāṃ viditvā śatarasam āhāra

"Let preparation be made
for this householder's

children.translated_text: offering." Then, at that very instant, <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, transformed the entire <s>Veṇuvana</s> (Bamboo Grove) into a sandalwood grove.

body.translated_text: Then that householder, having understood the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s consent through his silence, having prepared a meal of a hundred flavors,

body.text: airāvatasupratiṣṭhitasadṛśāni ca nāgasahasrāṇi vālavyajanena vījayanti supriyapañcaśikhatumburuprabhṛtīni cānekāni gandharvasahasrāṇy upacitāni, ye vicitrair vādyaviśeṣair vādyaṃ kurvanti divyasudhābhojanam //
body.translated_text: Thousands of <s>Nāgas</s> (serpent-beings) resembling <s>Airāvata</s> (Indra's elephant), well-positioned, fanned [the assembly] with chowries; and thousands of <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) — <s>Supriya</s>, <s>Pañcaśikha</s>, <s>Tumburu</s>, and many others — were assembled, and they performed music with various special instruments, [accompanying] the divine ambrosia-feast.

body.text: tataḥ sa gṛhapatir divyamānuṣyair upakaraṇair bhagavantam upasthāya sarvāṅgena bhagavataḥ pādayor nipatya praṇidhānaṃ kartum ārabdhaḥ // anena kuśalamūlenāhaṃ cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena cāndhe loke 'nāyake 'pariṇāyake buddho bhūyām iti //
body.translated_text: Then that householder, having attended upon the <s>Bhagavān</s> with divine and human provisions, having prostrated with his entire body at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, began to make his aspiration: "By this root of merit, by this arising of the mind, and by this renunciation of gifts, may I become a <s>Buddha</s> in a blind world without a guide or leader."

body.text: atha bhagavāṃs tasya gṛhapater hetuparaṃparāṃ karmaparaṃparāṃ ca jñātvā smitaṃ prāviṣkaroti // tasmin samaye nīlapītalohitāvadātā arciṣo bhagavato mukhadvārān niścaranti / niścaritvā, adha ūrddhabhavāgraparyantam avabhāsya / atha tā arciṣo bhagavantaṃ tripradakṣiṇīkṛtya bhagavata uṣṇīṣe 'ntarhito 'bhūt //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, having known the sequence of causes and the sequence of <s>karmas</s> of that householder, displayed a smile. At that time, blue, yellow, red, and white rays issued from the mouth of the Blessed One. Having issued forth, illuminating downward and upward to the limits of the highest existence — those rays, having circumambulated the Blessed One three times, disappeared into the <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> (crown-protuberance) of the Blessed One.

body.text: athāyuṣmān ānandaḥ kṛtakarapuṭo bhagavantaṃ papraccha //
body.translated_text: Then the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>, with palms joined, asked the Blessed One:

children.translated_text: 'A cluster of various, thousand-colored rays has been emitted from within your mouth,

children.text: avabhāsitā yena diśaḥ samantād divākareṇodayatā yathaiva // Dak_12.2 //
children.translated_text: by which the directions all around have been illuminated, just as by the rising sun.
The <s>Buddhas</s>, who are free from [worldly] arising, who have abandoned wretchedness and pride, who are the supreme causes in the world —

children.text: nākāraṇaṃ śaṅkhammālagauraṃ smitam upadarśayanti jinā jitārayaḥ // Dak_12.3 //
children.translated_text: the <s>Jinas</s> (Conquerors), who have conquered their enemies, do not display a smile as white as a conch shell without a cause.

body.text:
tatkālaṃ svayam adhigamya vīra buddhyā śrotṝṇāṃ śravaṇa jinendra kāṅkṣatānām
/
dhīrābhir munivṛṣa vāgbhir uttamābhir utpanna

children.translated_text: dispel

body.translated_text: Having understood [the cause] by yourself at this time, O hero, by [your] wisdom — for the listeners who desire to hear, O lord of <s>Jinas</s>,

body.text: saṃśayaṃ śubhābhiḥ // Dak_12.4 //
body.translated_text: the doubt that has arisen, with your steadfast, supreme, and auspicious words, O bull among sages!

body.text: nākasmāl lavaṇajalādrirājadhairyāḥ saṃbuddhāḥ smitam upadarśayanti nāthāḥ / yasyārthe smitam upadarśayanti dhīrās taṃ śrotuṃ samabhilaṣanti te janaughā iti //
body.translated_text: Not without cause do the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, who have the steadfastness of the ocean and the king of mountains, O protectors, display a smile. The multitude of people desire to hear that for whose sake the steadfast ones display a smile.'

body.text: bhagavān āha // evam etad ānandaivam etan nāhetv apratyayam ānanda te tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ smitaṃ prāviṣkurvanti / paśyānandānena gṛhapatinā mamaivaṃvidhaṃ satkāraṃ kṛtam

children.text: evaṃ bhagavata eṣa ānanda gṛhapatir anena kuśalamūlena cittotpādena deyadharmaparityāgena ca trikalpāsaṃkhyeyasamudānītāṃ bodhiṃ samudānīya karuṇāparibhāvitā
children.translated_text: Thus, <s>Ānanda</s>, this householder, by this root of merit, by this generation of the thought [of enlightenment], and by the relinquishing of gifts, having accumulated <s>bodhi</s> (enlightenment) gathered over three incalculable <s>kalpas</s> (aeons), being pervaded by

children.text: ṣaṭ pāramitāḥ paripūrya divyānnado nāma samyaksaṃbuddho bhaviṣyati / ayam asya deyadharmo yo mamāntike cittaprasādaḥ //
children.translated_text: compassion, having perfected the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), shall become a Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Divyānnada</s> (Giver of Divine Food). This is the reward of his gift — his mental devotion in my presence.'

body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'It is so, <s>Ānanda</s>, it is so! Not without cause and condition, <s>Ānanda</s>, do the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Enlightened Ones display a smile. See, <s>Ānanda</s> — by this householder, such honor has been rendered to me.

body.text: etac ca prakaraṇaṃ rājā bimbisāro māgadhāś ca paricārakāc chrutvā paraṃ vismayam āpannāḥ //
body.translated_text: Having heard this chapter, King <s>Bimbisāra</s> and the attendants of <s>Magadha</s> attained supreme wonder.

body.text: bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ //
body.translated_text: The monks, having become doubtful, asked the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, who cuts through all doubts:

body.text: paśya bhagavan yāvad anena gṛhapatinā bhagavān saśrāvakasaṃgho divyamānuṣikābhir ṛddhibhir abhyarcita iti //
body.translated_text: 'See, O Blessed One, how much this householder has worshipped the Blessed One together with the community of disciples with divine and human supernatural powers!'

body.text: bhagavān āha // tathāgatenaivaitāni karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati / na hi bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni / śubhāśubhāni pacyante, kadāpi na praṇaśyanti //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said: 'These <s>karmas</s> were performed and accumulated by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself — who else would experience [their results]? Indeed, O monks, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated, whether wholesome or unwholesome, ripen — they never perish.'

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani pūrṇo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān // atha pūrṇo nāma samyaksaṃbuddho janapadacārikaṃ caran

children.translated_text: arrived at a certain royal capital. A <s>Kṣatriya</s> king heard that the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s>, wandering on a countryside tour, had arrived in his territory. Having heard, with great royal splendor and great royal power, he approached the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s>,

children.text: ) upasaṃkramya pūrṇasamyaksaṃbuddhasya pādau śirasā vanditvaikānte niṣaṇṇaḥ / ekānte niṣaṇṇaṃ rājānaṃ kṣatriyaṃ pūrṇaḥ samyaksaṃbuddho bodhikarair dharmaiḥ samādāpayati //
children.translated_text: and having approached, having saluted the feet of the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s> with his head, he sat down to one side. To the <s>Kṣatriya</s> king seated to one side, the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s> exhorted with teachings conducive to enlightenment.

body.translated_text: In ancient times, O monks, in a past age, a Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Pūrṇa</s> appeared in the world — perfect in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. Then the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside,

body.text: atha rājā kṣatriyo buddhe bhagavati cittaprasādajātaḥ, pūrṇasamyakṣaṃbuddhaṃ saśrāvakasaṃghaṃ traimāsikaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātraśayanāsanaglanapratyayabhaiṣajyapariṣkārair upasthāya bhagavataḥ sasaṃghasya vividhānnapānabhojyāni dadāti, bhagavato ratnamayapratimāṃ kārayitvā buddhaharṣaṃ kāritavān / yatrānekaiḥ prāṇiśatasahasrair mahāprasādo labdhaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Kṣatriya</s> king, having generated mental devotion to the <s>Buddha</s>, the Blessed One, attended the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Pūrṇa</s> together with the community of disciples for three months with robes, alms-food, beds, medicines for illness, and requisites. He gave to the Blessed One together with the <s>Saṃgha</s> various foods, drinks, and eatables. Having had a jeweled image of the <s>Buddha</s> made, he caused delight in the <s>Buddha</s>. Thereby, hundreds of thousands of beings obtained great devotion.

children.translated_text: do you think, O monks? He who was the king at that time, in that era — I was

And by that very cause, such worship has been rendered to this <s>Tathāgata</s> by the merchant, by <s>Śakra</s>, and by the divine worlds. Therefore, O monks, you should train thus: We shall render honor and respect to the Teacher.'

body.translated_text: 'What

children.translated_text: 'Great is the benefit of food-giving and feeding.' And listen further:
'The divine ambrosia, held in the lotus-petal hands of beautiful women, blazing with excellent color and fragrance,
sweet to the touch and pleasurable — in the celestial city, the hosts of gods
eat the divine nectar placed in radiant golden vessels —
that fruit comes from the gift of food bestowed upon the noble <s>Saṃgha</s> headed by the <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: maitryā yaḥ saha kiṃkaraiḥ smararipuṃ nirjitya vajrāsane
children.translated_text: He who, together with compassion and attendants, having conquered the enemy of desire on the <s>vajrāsana</s> (diamond seat),

children.text: kleśārīn api yo durantaviṣayān antaścarān durjanān /
children.translated_text: having [conquered] also the enemies of <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions) — those impassable, internal, evil sense-objects —

children.text: skandhārātim api prasahya sugato mṛtyuṃ ca nītvā vaśaṃ
children.translated_text: and having forcefully [conquered] the enemy of the aggregates, the <s>Sugata</s>, having brought even death under control,
attained mastery over the enjoyment of all supreme flavors — even that, through the arising of food-giving.
Endowed with all limbs complete, with the splendor of happiness and eloquence,

children.text: āyur balaṃ varṇam udārarūpaṃ prāpnoti vidvān aśanapradānāt // Dak_12.8 //
children.translated_text: long life, strength, complexion, and noble form — the wise one obtains [these] from the gift of food.

children.text: nirjitya śatrūn balavīryayuktān lakṣmīṃ samāsādya ca ye narendrāḥ /
children.translated_text: Kings who, having conquered enemies endowed with strength and valor, and having attained prosperity,

children.text: svādūni bhojyāni samāpnuvanti bhojyapradānād dvipadās tad etat // Dak_12.9 //
children.translated_text: obtain delicious foods — that [comes] from the gift of food, O two-footed ones [i.e., humans].

children.text: annadānaṃ varaṃ śreṣṭham annadānāt paraṃ na hi /
children.translated_text: The gift of food is supreme, the best — there is nothing higher than the gift of food.

children.text: kṣudduḥkhārtāt paraṃ nāsti tasmād annaṃ garīyasam // Dak_12.10 //
children.translated_text: There is nothing worse than the suffering of hunger — therefore food is most weighty.

children.text: annena rahito yaś ca balavīryaṃ na cāsya ca /
children.translated_text: One who is deprived of food has neither strength nor vigor;

children.text: kāryakāraṇa utsāhe tasyotsāhaṃ na vidyate // Dak_12.11 //
children.translated_text: in the enterprise of duties, that one has no enthusiasm.
For others [deprived of food], the worship of gods and [performance of] vows perishes, and play and delight are destroyed.

children.text: kāle bhuktaṃ vihīnasya kathājñānaṃ ca hīyate // Dak_12.12 //
children.translated_text: For one who has not eaten at the proper time, knowledge and conversation also decline.
For those deprived of food, all <s>dharma</s> (religious practice) deteriorates.

children.text: tasmāt sarvaṃ prayatnena annadānaṃ tu cīyase // Dak_12.13 //
children.translated_text: Therefore, with all effort, the gift of food should be accumulated.'

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ bhojanakathā dvādaśaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the Story of Food-Giving — the twelfth chapter.

body.text: XIII. pānakathā
body.translated_text: XIII. The Story of the Gift of Drink

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantam etad avocat //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya</s> spoke thus to the Blessed One:

children.text: aparaṃ śrotum icchāmi pānadānasya yat phalam /
children.translated_text: 'I wish to hear further what the fruit of the gift of drink is.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ vada vādīndra sarvalokābhibhodhane // Dak_13.1 //
children.translated_text: Tell all that, O best of speakers, for the awakening of all the worlds!'

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

children.text: śṛṇu maitreya vakṣyāmi pānadānasya yat phalam /
children.translated_text: 'Listen, <s>Maitreya</s>, I shall tell the fruit of the gift of drink.
Having become single-minded, surely out of desire for the welfare of the world.'

body.text: ye saṃghe pratipādayanti muditā

children.translated_text: a thirst-quenching drink, endowed with delightful sweet flavors, sharp, fragrant, and pleasing — having destroyed their craving for existence, [overcoming] the fear of existence, [cutting] the creeper of craving with wisdom,

children.text: pāraṃ yānti bhavārṇavasya niyataṃ dattvā śubhaṃ pānakam // Dak_13.3 //
children.translated_text: they cross to the far shore of the ocean of existence, certainly, by giving auspicious drink.'

body.translated_text: As it is traditionally heard:

body.translated_text: 'In ancient times, O monks, in a past age, in this very auspicious <s>kalpa</s>, when the life-span of people was twenty thousand years, a Perfectly Enlightened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, the Leader of the World, appeared in the world — perfect in knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, tamer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, <s>Buddha</s>, Blessed One. He was dwelling near the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> (the Sages' Abode) in the Deer Park. There, a certain

body.text: tatas tasyā mātsaryam utpannam / sāgṛhītapariṣkārā bhikṣūn uvāca // bhikṣavo yadi mriyedhvaṃ tathāpi na yuṣmabhyaṃ dadāmy api pānīyam / ghaṭo me ūno bhaviṣyatīti // tato 'mī bhikṣavas tṛṣārtā nirāśayā prakrāntāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then miserliness arose in her. She, holding her possessions, said to the monks: 'O monks, even if you die, I shall not give you even water! My pot will become depleted.' Then those monks, thirsty and hopeless, departed.

body.text: tato magadhaviṣaye mahāḍhyaḥ siṃhaketur nāma sārthavāhas tasya putrī pānīyaghaṭam ādāya pānīyaṃ gṛhītuṃ gṛhadvārād bahir niḥsṛtā // tatas te ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: Then in the territory of <s>Magadha</s>, a very wealthy caravan-leader named <s>Siṃhaketu</s> — his daughter, taking a water-pot, came out from the house-door to fetch water. Then they said:

children.translated_text: us water to drink!'

body.translated_text: 'Dear girl, we are extremely thirsty — please give

Having come at this time, exhausted and suffering from thirst — please give them sugar, raw sugar, and pepper and the like in appropriate proportions. I shall prepare a drink and give it.'

body.translated_text: Then those eight monks, at <s>Ṛṣipatana</s> in the Deer Park, approached the Blessed One. Having approached, having saluted the feet of the Blessed One with their heads, they sat down to one side.

body.text: anena kuśalamūlenāhaṃ yatra yatropapadyate tatra tatra jātau jātau jātismarā bhaveyam / tad anusmṛtya buddhe bhagavati pūjite prasannā bhavāmi / tathāgataṃ pūjāsatkāraṃ karisyāmīti // tataḥ sā dārikā buddheṣv abhiprasādya kālagatā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyatriṃśeṣūpapannā // pañcaśataparivārāparivṛtā sābhūd divyaprāsāde sukhopaviṣṭe nānāsaṃgītivādyapravādite niṣpuṃsake / aciropapannasya striyā vā puruṣasya vā trīṇi cittāny utpadyante / kutaś cyutā kutropapannā kena karmaṇeti // sā paśyati, mānuṣyebhyaś cyutā ihopapannā / api tu kāśyape bhagavati satkārakṛtā tena kuśalamūlena deveṣvūpapannā iti //
body.translated_text: 'By this wholesome root, wherever I am reborn, in each and every birth, may I have memory of past lives. Remembering that, may I have faith in the Blessed <s>Buddha</s> when worshipped. I shall perform worship and honor to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' Then that girl, having gained faith in the <s>Buddhas</s>, died and was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-Three) gods. Surrounded by five hundred attendants, she was comfortably seated in a divine palace, with various music and instruments playing, in a paradise without males. When a woman or man has recently been reborn, three thoughts arise: 'From where did I fall? Where have I been reborn? By what <s>karma</s>?' She saw: 'Having fallen from the human realm, I have been reborn here. Moreover, by the honor rendered to the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, by that wholesome root I have been reborn among the gods.'

body.translated_text: Then in the mind of that drink-offering divine maiden, this thought arose: 'It would not be fitting for me, being of stale [i.e., old] attendants, to approach the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s> for an audience.' Knowledge-and-vision arose [in her mind]. The Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>, having accomplished the work of a <s>Buddha</s>, passed into <s>nirvāṇa</s>. A great relic-<s>stūpa</s> of his stands. Then this thought arose in her: 'Alas, I am of poor fortune! Where shall I see the Blessed <s>Kāśyapa</s>?' Then she remembered: 'I have heard that whoever worships even a mustard-seed-sized bodily relic of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> — by them, the fruit of purification is obtained; for the sinful one, sin is pacified.' children.translated_text: 'His wife had neither son nor daughter. He, placing his cheek on his hand, stood absorbed in worry: "My household is endowed with abundant wealth, but I have neither son nor daughter.',

children.translated_text: 'After my death, certainly all my property will become subject to the king." Thinking thus, he lamented exceedingly and became supremely agitated.'

body.translated_text: 'In that finest of great cities, <s>Kapilavastu</s>, among the <s>Śākyas</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> named <s>Rohiṇa</s> dwelt — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, with vast and extensive property, endowed with wealth equal to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>.'

body.text: athāsya daivayogād acireṇānyatamadevanikāyāc cyutvā tasyāḥ prajāpatyāḥ kukṣim avakrāntā / tatas tayā svāmī niveditaḥ / tataḥ svāminaivaṃ viditaṃ tataḥ svāminocyate // bhadre yadi putraṃ janiṣyasīty evaṃ kuśalam / atha duhitaraṃ tayaiva saha tvāṃ niṣkāsayāmīti //
body.translated_text: 'Then, by divine fortune, before long, [a being] having fallen from a certain divine assembly, entered the womb of his wife. Then she informed her husband. Then, having learned thus, the husband said: "Dear one, if you will bear a son, it is well. But if [you bear] a daughter, together with her I shall expel you!"'

body.text: yāvad aṣṭānāṃ navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā dārikā jātā abhirūpā prāsādikā atikrāntā manuṣyavarṇam asaṃprāptā ca divyavarṇaśuklavastraiḥ prāvṛtā aliptā garbhamalena

children.translated_text: When <s>Rohiṇa</s> heard that his wife had given birth and a girl was born, he entered angrily. Then the girl, wrapped in divine garments, was presented by his wife. Then <s>Rohiṇa</s> the <s>Śākya</s>, seeing the girl, was filled with supreme wonder:

body.translated_text: 'After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth — a girl was born, beautiful, pleasing, surpassing human complexion, though not having attained divine complexion — wrapped in white garments, unsmeared by the impurities of the womb,

body.text: aho āścarya me putrī kīdṛśī rūpaśobhitā
body.translated_text: 'Oh, how wonderful! What kind [of beauty] is my daughter, adorned with such beauty!

body.translated_text: She was born together with garments — by what <s>karma</s> was she born [thus]?'

'And many sons of ministers come day after day.

body.translated_text: "Long ago, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, there was a city named <s>Malayavatī</s>, delightful and unique, filled with various festivities, teeming with many people, furnished with learned persons, crowded with people of great wealth, abundant with women—

body.text: asya cetikā ekāsti

children.text: tayā cetikayā pratidinaṃ tasyodyānapuṣpāṇi nicitvā parinivṛtya kāle mārge tathāgatasya keśanakhastūpe kavalaikāni puṣpāṇy avarohayati sāgatya, ketuvikramasya devārcanāya dadātīti / evaṃ sā cetikā pratidinaṃ tadvyapāre niyojitā / tena udyānacāriṇī bhavati // tadanantare kāle lakṣasaṃkhyāyāṃ gacchanti / tadā caityadevatā prasannībhūya tayā prasādaḥ pratilabdhaḥ // ihaiva phalam āpyate / sā cetikā paramasundarībhūya suśīlasvabhāvābhūt, punar api tasyāḥ koṣṭhāgāre dhanadhānyasamṛddhyā nānālaṃkāraparipūrṇāni bhavanti // tadā sukham anubhūyate // tadā ketuvikramaḥ paramāścaryaprāptaḥ, kathaṃ me cetikāyāḥ kalevaraṃ suṣṭhu bhūtaṃ ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ // tathaivānyalokā api uktāḥ ke cid āhuḥ, bata bho kathaṃ cetikā vividhavastrasaṃpannā bhavati // evam evānyajanās tāṃ dṛṣṭvāścaryaprāptā abhūvan // tatas tasyā
children.translated_text: and that maidservant, daily gathering the flowers of that garden, when [the Buddha] had attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing), on the road would offer single flowers at the <s>stūpa</s> of hair and nails of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

children.text: lpāyuḥ kālaṃ kṛtvā, śrāvastyāṃ mahānagaryām anyatamadharmaśīlo nāma śreṣṭhī, tasya prajāpatyā
children.translated_text: of short lifespan, having died, in the great city of <s>Śrāvastī</s>, a certain merchant named <s>Dharmaśīla</s>, in the womb of his wife,

children.text: kukṣāv upapannā // tato daśamāsātyayā dārikā jātā abhirūpā prāsādikā paramasundarī, kramataḥ sā mahatī pravṛttā //
children.translated_text: she was reborn. Then after ten months, a girl was born—beautiful, faith-inspiring, supremely lovely; gradually she grew up.

body.translated_text: there was a single maidservant of his,

body.text: tadāham eva śrāvakasaṃghaiḥ śrāvastyāṃ viharāmi jetavane 'nāthapiṇḍadasyārāme

children.text: tena khalu punaḥ samayena śrāvastyāṃ sālaprabhañjikā nāma parva pratyupasthitam / tatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi saṃnipātya sālapuṣpāṇy ādāya krīḍanti ramanti paricārayanti // tadā sā śreṣṭhidārikā sālapuṣpāṇy ādāya śrāvastīṃ praviśati / bhagavāṃś ca bhikṣusaṃghaparivṛtaḥ śrāvastīṃ piṇḍāya caritvā nirgacchati // dadarśa buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītya cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakaṃ dṛṣṭvā punaḥ prasādajātayā sālapuṣpair avakīrṇaḥ / tataḥ pradakṣiṇīkṛtya pratinivṛttā / bhūyo 'nyāni gṛhasyārthe āneṣyāmīti // yāvad asau sālavṛkṣam adhirūḍhā patitā bhagavataḥ kṛtopasthānā sā kālagatā praṇīteṣu deveṣu trāyatriṃśeṣūpapannā // yāvad sālapuṣpavimānālaṃkṛtā svargaṃ svargād bhramantī ramantī //
children.translated_text: At that time, in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, the festival called <s>Sālaprabhañjikā</s> (Breaking of the <s>Sāla</s> branches) was at hand. There, many hundreds of thousands of living beings gathered, took <s>sāla</s> flowers, and played, sported, and celebrated. Then that merchant's daughter, taking <s>sāla</s> flowers, entered <s>Śrāvastī</s>. And the <s>Bhagavān</s>, surrounded by the community of <s>bhikṣus</s>, having gone on alms-round in <s>Śrāvastī</s>, was going out. She beheld the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, with body resplendent with the eighty minor marks, adorned with an aura of a fathom's length, with radiance surpassing a thousand suns, like a moving jeweled mountain, auspicious in all directions. Seeing him, with faith arisen, she scattered <s>sāla</s> flowers [upon him]. Then, having circumambulated him, she turned back [thinking]: 'I shall bring other [flowers] again for the purpose of [my] household.' While climbing the <s>sāla</s> tree, she fell, and — having performed worship to the <s>Bhagavān</s> — she died and was reborn among the excellent <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods. There, adorned with a celestial palace of <s>sāla</s> flowers, she roamed from heaven to heaven, sporting.

body.translated_text: "At that time, I myself was dwelling in <s>Śrāvastī</s> with the community of disciples, in the <s>Jetavana</s> (Jeta's Grove), in the park of <s>Anāthapiṇḍada</s>.

body.text: evam eva bhikṣavaḥ sā dārikā, yayā arhan mārge sālapuṣpair avakīrṇaḥ / tasmād bhikṣavas tathāgateṣu kārāpayitavyā

children.translated_text: they should be honored —

children.text: īdṛśaṃ phalam āpyate / atha bhagavato vacanaṃ (
children.translated_text: such fruit is obtained." Then, having accepted the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>,

children.text: ) pratiśrutya prasādajātena ānando bhagavantam etad avocat //
children.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s>, with faith arisen, spoke thus to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.translated_text: "Thus indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that girl, by whom an <s>arhat</s> (worthy one) was scattered with <s>sāla</s> flowers on the path — therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, [offerings] should be made to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>,

body.text:
bhagavan kīdṛśaṃ nātha lakṣapuṣpasya yat phalam /
śrotukāma

children.translated_text: I wish to hear — O Great-armed one, tell us, O Supreme Lord!"

body.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O Protector, what is the fruit of [offering] a hundred thousand flowers?

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.translated_text: "I shall declare in brief, for the benefit of the worlds,

children.text: kramato lakṣapuṣpāṇāṃ śṛṇv ānanda atandritaḥ // Dak.15_6 //
children.translated_text: the [fruits of offering] a hundred thousand flowers, in order — listen, O <s>Ānanda</s>, without sloth!
A hundred sins of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>), committed in a hundred births —

children.text: rohaṇaṃ māghyapuṣpāṇāṃ śamayati na saṃśayaḥ // Dak.15_7 //
children.translated_text: the offering of <s>māghya</s> flowers removes [them], without doubt.

body.text:
kṛṣṇāparājitā yena prarohante narāḥ kva cit /
sarvapāpaharā ghorā

children.translated_text: [they are] removers of all sins, terrible ones, destroyers of all enemies.

body.translated_text: Those persons who anywhere offer <s>kṛṣṇāparājitā</s> (dark-colored <s>Aparājitā</s>) flowers —

children.translated_text: There is destruction of all obstacles, and the fruit of enjoyment and liberation comes;
having attained the happiness of a king, [one attains] the supreme rank of the king of the gods.
Those persons who offer <s>śvetāparājitā</s> (white <s>Aparājitā</s>) flowers —

children.text: śāntabhūtā dhanāḍhyāś ca nānāśāstreṣu pāragāḥ // Dak.15_10 //
children.translated_text: they become peaceful, wealthy, and masters of various <s>śāstras</s>.
Endowed with firmness and valor, possessing various kinds of intelligence,

children.text: bhūpateḥ padaṃ saṃprāpya jāyante svargagāminaḥ // Dak.15_11 //
children.translated_text: having attained the rank of a king, they are born as heaven-goers.
Those persons who offer golden jasmine (<s>suvarṇayūthikā</s>) flowers —

children.text: dhanavān bhogavān bhūtvā vibhavaiḥ dhanadasamāḥ // Dak.15_12 //
children.translated_text: becoming wealthy and full of enjoyments, equal to <s>Dhanada</s> (Kubera) in riches.
The best of men who offer the supreme <s>karavīra</s> (oleander) flowers —
[they] attain mastery over all people, and increase the delight of the gods.
Those persons who offer <s>damana</s> flowers with great faith —
they always have fragrant bodies; an insatiable beauty is obtained.
Those who offer <s>kokilākṣa</s> flowers become possessed of people and wealth,

children.text: yidyāvatāṃ kule jātaḥ sarvalokaiḥ prapūjyate // Dak.15_15 //
children.translated_text: born in a family of the learned, worshipped by all people.

children.text: rohaṇāc campakaṃ puṣpaṃ narā ye śraddhayā kila /
children.translated_text: Those persons who offer <s>campaka</s> flowers with faith —

children.text: kīrtiśabdaś ca lokeṣu sarvasaṃpada labhyate // Dak.15_16 //
children.translated_text: fame and renown in the worlds, and all prosperity is obtained.
They become handsome and beautiful, with bodies equal to <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love),
endowed with fragrant bodies, and royal splendor is obtained.

children.text: jātipuṣpaṃ ca rohante jātiś ca sukule gatā /
children.translated_text: Those who offer <s>jāti</s> (jasmine) flowers — birth in a good family is obtained;
with exceedingly fragrant bodies, equal to <s>Dhanada</s> in wealth.

body.text: padmapuṣpa

children.text:
naraḥ kaś cit prasannena prarohati /
buddhajñāna
children.translated_text: flower — any person who offers [it] with a clear mind
attains the wisdom of a <s>Buddha</s> and is born on a lotus seat.

body.translated_text: A lotus

children.translated_text: <s>Madhu</s> flowers give sweetness; <s>madhurī</s> flowers give garments likewise;

children.text: kauśikair vastradaṃ caiva kiṃśukai raktavastradam // Dak.15_20 //
children.translated_text: <s>kauśika</s> (silk-cotton) [flowers] give garments; <s>kiṃśuka</s> (Flame of the Forest) flowers give red garments.

children.text: kusumaṃ pārijātaṃ ca yaḥ prarohati mānavaḥ /
children.translated_text: He who offers <s>pārijāta</s> flowers —
he attains infinite happiness and becomes one with a fragrant body.

body.text:
bandhūkapuṣpasaṃrohaṃ sarvapāpāpadakṣayam /
rohanaṃ ketakīpuṣpaṃ kīrtivanto bhaven narāḥ /
sugandhasukhasampanna

children.translated_text: auspiciousness obtains everywhere.

body.translated_text: The offering of <s>bandhūka</s> flowers destroys all sins. Those persons who offer <s>ketakī</s> (screw-pine) flowers become famous; endowed with fragrant happiness,

children.translated_text: Those who offer <s>kumuda</s> (white water-lily) flowers — [their] facial disc [becomes] like the moon;
gentle, equal to the splendor of the moon — they are born in the abode of the gods.

body.text: nīlotpalāni puṣpāṇi ye prarohanti śraddhayā / mukhe

children.translated_text: issues the fragrance of lotuses; [they] become kings of great power.

body.translated_text: Those who offer blue lotus (<s>nīlotpala</s>) flowers with faith — from their mouths

children.translated_text: Those who offer <s>aśoka</s> flowers — [their] bodies become incomparable;
freed from all diseases, kingship is obtained.

children.text: kusumaṃ bhṛṅgarājaṃ ca rohaṇaṃ mānavāḥ parāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those foremost persons who offer <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> flowers —
[it is] the destroyer of all terrible diseases, sorrows, and great ailments.

body.text: javākusuma rohante mānavā naranāyakāḥ l

children.text: mohanaṃ sarvalokānāṃ lokānāṃ vaśyam āgatāḥ // Dak.15_27 //
children.translated_text: [they become] enchanters of all people; all people come under [their] control.

body.translated_text: Those persons, leaders of men, who offer <s>javā</s> (hibiscus) flowers —

children.translated_text: Those persons of pure mind who offer <s>arka</s> (Calotropis) flowers —
endowed with a thousand rays [of splendor], they become possessed of people and wealth.
From the offering of <s>kahlāra</s> (white lotus) flowers with a supremely clear mind —

children.text: nāśanaṃ sarvarogāṇāṃ lakṣmīr vahati sarvadā // Dak.15_29 //
children.translated_text: [it is] the destroyer of all diseases; <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity) accompanies [them] always.
By worshipping here with <s>nāga</s> (serpent-flower) flowers, one becomes happy in the next world;
and likewise, with <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) flowers, the great sins are destroyed.
The excellent <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple) leaves — from offering them without sloth,

children.text: śivaṃ sarvatra prāpnoti yajjānāṃ ca sahasrakam // Dak.15_31 //
children.translated_text: one attains auspiciousness everywhere, and [the merit of] a thousand sacrifices.
Those who offer <s>dhūrta</s> (<s>dhattūra</s>) flowers — [they become] fashioned like gold;
endowed with prosperous happiness, the fruit of enjoyment is obtained.
By worshipping with red lotuses, the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> and the like is destroyed.
Those persons of devout mind who offer <s>dūrvā</s> (Bermuda grass) and <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) —

children.text: śatajanmārjitaṃ pāpaṃ mukto bhavati tatkṣaṇāt // Dak.15_33 //
children.translated_text: sins accumulated in a hundred births are freed at that very moment.

body.text: tagaraṃ puṣpa rohanti paraloke sukhāvahā

children.translated_text: the ancestors attain satisfaction
especially through <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral) rites.

body.translated_text: Those who offer <s>tagara</s> (Indian valerian) flowers — [they bring] happiness in the next world;

children.translated_text: Those who offer <s>tatkārī</s> flowers — they are always endowed with prosperity;
abundance of wealth and grain, and the fruit of desired goals is obtained.

children.text: mallikāpuṣpa rohante na māro kṣobhayet punaḥ /
children.translated_text: Those who offer <s>mallikā</s> (Arabian jasmine) flowers — <s>Māra</s> shall not again disturb [them];
by the offering of fragrant flowers, fame of fragrant qualities [is obtained].

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text:
viśeṣaṃ lakṣapuṣpāṇāṃ rohaṇena phalāphalam /
uccanīcādikaṃ sarva

children.translated_text: the high and low and the like — all this I shall declare in brief.

body.translated_text: "The distinction among the hundred thousand flowers, and the fruit and non-fruit of offering,

children.translated_text: The <s>māghya</s> flowers are the most distinguished, especially [when offered to] the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of truth);
{<s>kṛṣṇāparājitā</s> next,} then golden jasmine flowers, then <s>karavīra</s> after that.

children.text: damanapuṣpāṇi tatpaścāt yaṃ ca puṣpāṇi sarvataḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Damana</s> flowers after that, and then all flowers everywhere —

children.text: viśiṣṭaṃ yaṃ ca buddhānāṃ satataṃ jinabhāṣitam // Dak.15_39 //
children.translated_text: distinguished — and these of the <s>Buddhas</s>, as always declared by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victors).
<s>Campaka</s> and <s>jāti</s> flowers, <s>pārijāta</s> likewise,
<s>ketakī</s>, <s>navamālī</s>, and lotus, <s>kumuda</s>, and water-lily.
<s>Aśoka</s> and <s>arka</s> flowers, <s>kahlāra</s> and <s>nāga</s> flowers,

children.text: bilvapattrāṇi dhattūraṃ javāpuṣpani tathaiva ca // Dak.15_41 //
children.translated_text: <s>bilva</s> leaves and <s>dhattūra</s>, and <s>javā</s> flowers likewise.
<s>Bhṛṅgarāja</s> flowers, then <s>lakṣmī</s> flowers, in order;
<s>tamāra</s>, <s>nirgranthī</s>, <s>yūthī</s>, <s>mallikā</s>, and <s>mādhavī</s> likewise.
Forest garland, <s>kunda</s>, <s>bandhūka</s>, unwilted <s>kuvalaka</s> likewise,
<s>saireyaka</s>, <s>roraṇa</s>, and <s>madhurī</s> flowers in abundance.

body.text: evaṃ krama

children.text: viśiṣṭaṃ ca anyeṣāṃ ca pṛthak pṛthak /
children.translated_text: distinguished, and of others separately,
are the various flowers, born of many kinds.

body.translated_text: Thus, in order,

children.text: nānyoktaṃ ca mayā ke cit sāmānyapuṣpakasya ca /
children.translated_text: Some flowers not mentioned by me are of the general [category];

children.text: kathitaṃ jinanāthaiś ca puṣpāṇāṃ sarvataḥ kila // Dak.15_45 //
children.translated_text: all flowers have been spoken of by the Lord of <s>Jinas</s> everywhere.
From offering all flowers and the like to a <s>caitya</s>, the fruit is supreme;

children.text: pṛthak pṛthak phalaṃ tasmāt puṣpāṇāṃ kathitā jināḥ // Dak.15_46 //
children.translated_text: therefore, the separate fruits of flowers have been declared by the <s>Jinas</s>."

body.text: ānanda uvāca //
body.translated_text: <s>Ānanda</s> spoke:

children.translated_text: "O Protector, I have heard the distinction of the hundred thousand flowers for <s>caityas</s>;

children.text: tathāgatānām anyeṣāṃ vada me vādipuṃgava // Dak.15_47 //
children.translated_text: tell me of the others, O best of speakers, for the <s>Tathāgatas</s>."

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: pūrvoktāni ca puṣpāṇāṃ caityānām abhavat tadā /
children.translated_text: "The previously mentioned flowers were for <s>caityas</s>;

children.text: pravakṣyāmi yathānanda sāṃnidhyaṃ śṛṇu sarvataḥ // Dak.15_48 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare, O <s>Ānanda</s>, the presence [of merit] — hear everything.

body.text:
tathāgateṣu aneyeṣu devatāyāṃ viśeṣataḥ /
pūrvoktāni ca puṣpāṇāṃ yathāyogya

children.translated_text: as one wishes —

children.text: devatā varṇabhedena puṣpāṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca // Dak.15_49 //
children.translated_text: the deities, according to the distinction of color, and the flowers likewise.

body.translated_text: For the other <s>Tathāgatas</s> and deities in particular, the previously mentioned flowers, as appropriate,

body.text: evam ānanda jñātavya

children.translated_text: a person should offer flowers;

children.text: pūrvoktaphalam āpnoti nityam eva na saṃśayaḥ // Dak.15_50 //
children.translated_text: he obtains the previously stated fruit, always, without doubt.

body.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Ānanda</s>, it should be known —

children.text: mahānuśaṃsā puṣpāṇām ārohaṇād dhi phalaṃ tathoktam /
children.translated_text: Great are the benefits of offering flowers — the fruit has been thus stated;

children.text: buddheṣu bimbeṣu tathā ca stūpe anyeṣu deveṣu phalaṃ tad eva // Dak.15_51 //
children.translated_text: for <s>Buddhas</s>, images, <s>stūpas</s>, and other deities, the fruit is the same."

body.text: punaśca //
body.translated_text: And furthermore:

body.text: śakrādhikāḥ pravarabhogasamanvitās te padmendukāntivapuṣo varakīrtiyuktāḥ / śakrān vijitya rabhasā satataṃ bhavanti buddhasya ye sukusumaiḥ prakiranti pūjām //
body.translated_text: "Those who scatter worship upon the <s>Buddha</s> with excellent flowers, with single-minded devotion, for the sake of crossing the ocean of existence — they become superior to <s>Śakra</s>, endowed with the finest enjoyments, with bodies radiant as lotus and moon, possessing excellent fame, continually conquering <s>Śakra</s> with their vigor."

"Those who have bodies fragrant as a collection of blue lotuses, with well-known fame, pure, wide, and beautiful eyes, resembling jewels, moving on earth as humans — [such are] those who have offered the finest incense of noble fragrance to the <s>Jina</s>."

children.translated_text: "With limbs adorned with <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, pearls, and gems, with entire bodies covered in silk garments,

children.text: narottamāḥ sarvajanair upetā bhavanti buddhe surabhipradānāt // Dak.15_54 //
children.translated_text: they become the best of men, attended by all people — [such is the fruit] of the gift of fragrance to the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: evaṃ bhikṣavo 'pi īdṛśaphalaṃ sā cetikā prāptā //
body.translated_text: "Thus indeed, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, that female attendant obtained such fruit."

body.text: tasmād bhikṣavas tathāgateṣu stūpabimbeṣu puṣpaiḥ pratipūjanīyāḥ // evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ bhikṣava iti //
body.translated_text: "Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, [their] <s>stūpas</s> and images should be worshipped with flowers. Thus should you train, O <s>bhikṣus</s>."

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ puṣpakathā pañcadaśaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the Flower Narrative, the fifteenth chapter.

body.text: XVI. praṇāmakathā
body.translated_text: XVI. The Narrative of Obeisance (<s>Praṇāmakathā</s>).

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantaṃ praṇamyaitad avocat //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s>, having bowed to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus:

children.text: śrotum icchāmi he nātha bhagavan bhavamocaka /
children.translated_text: "I wish to hear, O Protector, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O Liberator from existence!

children.text: tāthāgate praṇāmasya phalaṃ teṣāṃ vada prabho // Dak_16.1 //
children.translated_text: Tell the fruit of obeisance to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, O Lord!"

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: sādhu sādhu tva maitreya pṛcchitaṃ yan mayi tvayā /
children.translated_text: "Well done, well done, O <s>Maitreya</s>! That which you have asked of me —

children.text: buddhasya ca praṇāmasya phalaṃ vakṣyāmy ahaṃ nu bho // Dak_16.2 //
children.translated_text: I shall declare the fruit of obeisance to the <s>Buddha</s>, O friend!
Great are the benefits of obeisance to the <s>Buddha</s> — they attain handsome kingship and happiness;

children.text: ye caikacittaiḥ praṇamanti bhaktyā bhavārṇavasyottaraṇāya hetum // Dak_16.3 //
