body.text: saced ākāṅkṣasi niṣīdeti // teṣāṃ ca / ehi bhikṣava ity ukte yat kiṃ cit tīrthikaliṅgaṃ sarvam eva tatkṣaṇam evāntaradhāt // tricīvaraṃ pātraṃ ca prādurabhūt // athocchinno keśas tad yathāpi nāmāsaṃkhyeyavarṣaśatopasaṃpannasya bhikṣor īryapathaḥ susaṃvṛto 'bhūt, saiva teṣāṃ pravarjyābhūt sopasaṃpat sabhikṣubhāveṇa //
body.translated_text: "If you wish, sit down." And for them — when 'Come, monks' was spoken, whatever mark of the <s>tīrthikas</s> (heterodox teachers) [they had], all of it vanished at that very instant. The triple robe and the bowl appeared. Their hair was cut, and just as the deportment of a monk who has been ordained for countless hundreds of years is well-restrained, so was their going forth, together with full ordination and the status of monks.

body.text: ekasya tathāgateṣu mātsaryacittasya bhikṣoś cīvaraṃ na prādurbhūtaṃ pātraṃ ca //
body.translated_text: For one [among them], who had an envious mind toward the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the robe did not appear, nor the bowl.

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣavas tasyāṃ velāyāṃ tathāgatasya caraṇayor nipatya vijñāpayanti sma // tathāgatasyāntike śāstṭsaṃjñāprema ca prasādagauravaṃ cotpādayati sma //
body.translated_text: Then, at that time, the monks, having prostrated at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, made their request; and they generated the perception of the Teacher, love, faith, and reverence toward the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: atha sa ekaś cīvaranaprādurbhūtena punar api tayā vrīḍayā tathāgatasya caraṇayor praṇipatya vijñāpayām āsa // katham etad bhagavan mamaikasya cīvaraṃ notpāditam //
body.translated_text: Then that one, for whom the robe had not appeared, again prostrated at the feet of the <s>Tathāgata</s> with that shame and made his request: "How is it, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, that for me alone the robe was not produced?"

children.translated_text: [Page] 169
) The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ tathāgateṣu praṇāmakāle mātsaryadoṣād iti // evam ukte niśvasya kṣamārthanāṃ kṛtvā tathāgataṃ praṇāmitaḥ // tadā bhagavato 'nubhāvena cīvaraṃ prādurbhūtam // tatkṣaṇam eva malinībhūtam // taṃ dṛṣṭvā vrīḍāvarjitamanā bhikṣur bhagavantam evam āha // bhagavan kena karmaṇā mamaikasya cīvaraṃ na prādurbhūtaṃ, prādurbhūte punar malinībhūtam / ko hetuḥ kaḥ pratyayaḥ //
body.translated_text: In a former time, at the time of bowing to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, due to the fault of miserliness... Having said this, he sighed, begged forgiveness, and bowed to the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Then, by the power of the Blessed One, a robe appeared [for him]. But at that very moment it became soiled. Seeing that, the monk, his mind overwhelmed with shame, said to the Blessed One: 'Blessed One, by what <s>karma</s> did a robe not appear for me alone, and having appeared, why did it become soiled? What is the cause? What is the condition?'

body.text: bhagavān āha //
body.translated_text: The Blessed One said:

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣava atīte 'dhvany asaṃkhyeyakalpe dīpaṃkareṇa pūrvaṃ padmottaro nāma samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sa saṃghena saha janapadacārikāṃ carann anyatamamahājanapadaṃ prāptaḥ // tatra mahājanapade vīthimadhye sthitvā dharmaṃ deśitavān // tadā sarvanāgarās tatropasaṃkrāntā dharmakathāṃ śrutavantaḥ // atha somakaumudir nāma brāhmaṇo mahāvidvāñ śiṣyaganaiḥ sārdhaṃ tāṃ vārttāṃ śrutvā yena padmottaraḥ samyaksaṃbuddhas tenopasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavanta

children.text:
praṇamya purataḥ sthitvā dharmaṃ śṛṇvanti // tadā prasādajātāḥ sarve te tathāgataśāsane pravrajyāgrahaṇaṃ cakārayām āsuḥ // te
tathāgatasyāntike śāstṛsaṃjñāpremagauravajātena bhagavataś caraṇayor nipatayanti sma /
children.translated_text: they stood before him and listened to the <s>dharma</s>. Then, having gained faith, all of them took ordination in the <s>Tathāgata's</s> teaching. With a sense of reverence, love, and respect toward the teacher, they prostrated at the Blessed One's feet.'

body.translated_text: 'In a former time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past age, in an incalculable <s>kalpa</s> before <s>Dīpaṃkara</s>, a Perfectly Enlightened One named <s>Padmottara</s>, wandering on a tour of the countryside together with the <s>saṃgha</s>, arrived at a certain great province. There, in the great province, standing in the middle of the street, he taught the <s>dharma</s>. Then all the townspeople came there and heard the <s>dharma</s>-discourse. Then a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Somakaumudī</s>, a great scholar, together with his group of disciples, having heard that news, approached the Perfectly Enlightened <s>Padmottara</s>; having approached, bowing to the Blessed One,

body.text: tena samayena somakaumudibrāhmaṇasya śiṣya

children.text: tvayaikena tathāgatapraṇāmakāle mātsaryacittena iti bhāvitaḥ / śramaṇavandanam akṛte kiṃ bhaviṣyati iti //
children.translated_text: and you alone, at the time of bowing to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, cultivated a mind of miserliness, [thinking:] "What will happen if I do not bow to the ascetic?"'

body.translated_text: 'At that time, [you were] a disciple of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Somakaumudī</s>,

body.text: tena mātsaryakṛtena, anekavarṣaśatasahasralokair nindanīyajanma bhūtvā, mahān āśīviṣa upapannaḥ / adyāpi tavāśīviṣakaṅkālam astīti kālañjaraparvatasya kandarāyāṃ mahocchrayapramāṇaṃ parvata iva tiṣṭhati // tataḥ śatavarṣātyayād daridrakule jātas tatpaścāt tīrthiko jaṭādhārī bhikṣuko 'bhūt // tadā pāṭaliputranagare kena cid gṛhastena tīrthikān bhojanārthaṃ rasarasāgropetair āhāraṃ sajjīkṛtya tīrthikān āhūya svābhiprāyaṃ tīrthikān bhojitaḥ / tvayā dvādaśa prasthāni kṣīrodanaṃ bhuktam

children.text: tathāpi pūrṇodaro nābhūt // tadā sarve janā
children.translated_text: yet your belly was not full. Then all the people

children.text: pretabhaikṣukaṃ manyante // tadanantaraṃ tvayā vrīḍayā niśvasya cintayati // dhik jīvitam iti matvā tasmāt sthānāt prakrāntaḥ / tata ihaiva janmani cyutvā mānuṣyaṃ janma prāptavān // tadāsau brāhmaṇa
children.translated_text: regarded [you as] a begging ghost. Then you, with shame, sighing and thinking "Alas, this life!" departed from that place. Then, having died in that very birth, you obtained a human birth.' 'That <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,

children.text: śiṣyagaṇaiḥ sārdham āgacchantaṃ paśyan te militvā ihāgatāḥ //
children.translated_text: together with his group of disciples, seeing you coming, they all met and came here.'

body.translated_text: 'By that act of miserliness, having been born in contemptible births for many hundreds of thousands of years, he was reborn as a great venomous serpent. Even today, your serpent-skeleton remains — it stands in the cave of <s>Kālañjara</s> mountain, of vast dimensions like a mountain. Then, after the passage of a hundred years, [you were] born in a poor family, and afterward became a <s>tīrthika</s> (non-Buddhist ascetic), a mendicant wearing matted locks. At that time, in the city of <s>Pāṭaliputra</s>, a certain householder, having prepared food endowed with the finest flavors to feed the <s>tīrthikas</s>, having invited the <s>tīrthikas</s>, fed them according to his own wish. You ate twelve <s>prasthas</s> (measures) of milk-rice,

body.text: tathāgatapraṇāmamātsaryakṛtapāpena tādṛśaṃ duḥkhaṃ anubhūya adyāpi tatpāpaśeṣeṇa praṇāmo na kṛtas tenaiva hetunā cīvarādikaṃ na prādurbhūtaṃ malinībhūtaṃ ca //
body.translated_text: 'By the sin committed through miserliness at the time of bowing to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, having experienced such suffering, even today, by the remainder of that sin, the bow was not made. For that very reason, the robe and the like did not appear, and it became soiled.'

body.text: tadā sa bhikṣur evam eva bhagavan mamāparādham atyayaṃ pratigṛhnātu ity uktvā gautamasya pādayoḥ praṇipatya tiṣṭhati // tadā bhagavato 'nubhāvena tasya pāpāt parimukto 'bhūt / cīvaraṃ ca malinaṃ tyajya yathāpūrvavad bhavati // evaṃ bhikṣava mā yūyaṃ tathāgatam āyuṣmantaṃ mānasā ca vādena samudācariṣṭhavyam // he bhikṣava idānīṃ mamāntike cittaprasādajāta anena kuśalamūlena cārhattvaṃ prāpta iti //
body.translated_text: Then that monk said: 'Even so, Blessed One, may you accept my offense and transgression!' — and bowed at the feet of <s>Gautama</s> and remained [prostrate]. Then, by the power of the Blessed One, he was freed from that sin. And the soiled robe was discarded and became as before. 'Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, do not treat the <s>Tathāgata</s> and the venerable ones with [ill] mind and speech. O <s>bhikṣus</s>, now, having gained faith of mind in my presence, by this wholesome root, [you have] attained <s>Arhat</s>-ship.'

body.text: punar api bhikṣūn āmantryaivam āha //
body.translated_text: And again he addressed the monks thus:

body.text: kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo 'sau tena kālena tena samayena somakaumudibrāhmaṇasya śiṣyatvabhūtena padmottaratathāgatapraṇāmakāle mātsaryadoseṇa īdṛśaṃ duḥkham anubhūtam // so 'haṃ somakaumudibrāhmaṇo yūyaṃ mama śiṣyāḥ // idānīm api yūyaṃ mama śiṣyā abhūvan // mayā cānekatathāgateṣūpāsitena kuśalena saṃsāre 'nantasukham anubhūya tathāgatapadaṃ prāptam // tasmād bhikṣavas tathāgate anumodayitavyā

children.translated_text: serve him, proclaim the virtues and benefits of the <s>Tathāgata</s>,
and bow to the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.translated_text: 'What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who at that time, in that era, as a disciple of the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Somakaumudī</s>, experienced such suffering due to the fault of miserliness at the time of bowing to the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Padmottara</s> — I was that <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> <s>Somakaumudī</s>, and you were my disciples. Even now you have been my disciples. And by me, having served many <s>Tathāgatas</s>, by that wholesome [merit], having experienced endless happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>, the state of a <s>Tathāgata</s> has been attained. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should rejoice in the <s>Tathāgata</s>,

body.text: tathāgatānāṃ praṇāmasya mahāphalānuśaṃsā tac chṛṇuta //
body.translated_text: 'Hear the great fruit and benefits of bowing to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>!'

body.text: yac cakravartī kṣitipapradhānaiḥ kṛtāñjali

children.text: kuṇḍālacārugaṇḍaiḥ / bhaktyā sumūrdhnā bahu vandyate tad buddhapraṇāmāt kathayanti tajjñāḥ //
children.translated_text: with earrings and beautiful cheeks, is greatly worshipped with devotion by bowing the head — those who know say that [is the fruit] of bowing to the <s>Buddha</s>.'

body.translated_text: 'That a <s>Cakravartin</s> (universal sovereign), foremost among kings, with joined palms,

children.text: ye jātamātrāḥ prabhutāṃ prayānti śreṣṭhe kule janma sadaiva yeṣām /
children.translated_text: 'Those who from the very moment of birth attain sovereignty, who are always born in the noblest family,

children.text: hastyaśvayānaiś ca paribhramanti kṛtvā tu te śreṣṭhatare praṇāmam // Dak_16.30
children.translated_text: and who travel with elephants, horses, and chariots — they [attain this] having made the most excellent prostration.'

children.text: prathayati yaśo dhatte śreyo vivardhayati dyutiṃ
children.translated_text: 'It spreads fame, bestows welfare, increases splendor,

children.text: harati duritaṃ sarvaṃ sarvaṃ hy arātim apohati /
children.translated_text: removes all evil, repels all enemies,

children.text: sugatiniyatāṃ loke nṛṇāṃ karoti ca saṃtatiṃ
children.translated_text: establishes in the world a lineage of men destined for good rebirth,
and bears fruit in auspiciousness at the end, inevitably — the act of bowing to the lord of sages.'

children.text: cakrī nṛpo yad balakīrtiyukto dvātriṃśatā lakṣaṇabhūṣitāṅgaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That a king who is a <s>Cakravartin</s>, endowed with strength and fame, with limbs adorned by the thirty-two marks,

children.text: saṃjāyate vai kṣitipapradhāno buddhapraṇāmād dhi phalaṃ tad uktam // Dak_16.32
children.translated_text: is born as the foremost among kings — that fruit is said to be from bowing to the <s>Buddha</s>.'

children.text: evaṃ bahuguṇaṃ matvā matvā kāyaṃ ca bhaṅguram /
children.translated_text: 'Knowing thus the many virtues [of bowing], and knowing the body to be perishable,

children.text: buddhapraṇāmāt ko vidvān kāyakarmānyad ācaret // Dak_16.33 //
children.translated_text: what wise person would perform any other bodily action than bowing to the <s>Buddha</s>?'

children.text: kas taṃ na namaḥ kuryād dṛṣṭvā dūrāt punarbhavād bhītaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Who, seeing [the Buddha], even from afar, fearing rebirth, would not bow to him?
For by making a single prostration, one has reached the far shore of existence — for that reason.'

body.text: evaṃ śikṣitavyaṃ kṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya śukleṣv eva svābhogaḥ karaṇīya ity evaṃ bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyaṃ

children.text: idaṃ avocad bhagavān ātmanā ca bhikṣavo bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti //
children.translated_text: This the Blessed One said. And the <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at what was spoken.

body.translated_text: 'Thus one should train: casting off dark <s>karmas</s>, one should apply oneself to bright [karmas] alone — thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, one should train.'

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ praṇāmakathā soḍasamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the prostration story — the sixteenth chapter.

body.text: XVII. ujjvālikādānakathā
body.translated_text: XVII. The Lamp-Offering Story

body.text: atha khalu bhagavān lokānukampako lokajño lokaśāstā sarvajño dhyānasukhe vijahāra // tena samayena vaiśālīnagaryāṃ mahopadravāḥ prādurbhūtāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then the Blessed One, compassionate toward the world, knower of the world, teacher of the world, omniscient, dwelt in the bliss of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). At that time, in the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, great calamities arose.

children.translated_text: 'Then the citizens and all the people, excessively indulging in pleasures,

children.text: yathākāmaṃ rasaṃ bhuktvā prācaran pāpasaṃgatam // Dak_17.1 //
children.translated_text: having enjoyed flavors as they wished, engaged in sinful company.'
'Then even the <s>Kṣatriya</s>, deluded by the enjoyment of pleasures,
attached to groups of women, heedless of righteousness and <s>dharma</s>.'

children.text: dṛṣtvā sa sundarīṃ kāntām agamyām api mohitaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Seeing a beautiful, desirable woman, though she was forbidden, deluded,

children.text: balenāpi samākṛṣya bubhuje svecchayā mudā // Dak_17.3 //
children.translated_text: even by force he seized and enjoyed her as he pleased, with delight.'
'Likewise, all the citizens, all with minds afflicted by defilements,
rejecting the true <s>dharma</s>, pursued the enjoyment of pleasures.'
'Abandoning the boundaries of family <s>dharma</s>, they acted as they wished.

children.text: satyadharmaṃ pratikṣipya cerur mattadvipā iva // Dak_17.5 //
children.translated_text: Rejecting the <s>dharma</s> of truth, they moved about like maddened elephants.'
'Likewise, groups of women too, with minds disturbed by the defilements of desire,
abandoning their family <s>dharma</s>, roamed about as they pleased.'

body.text: tadātra bahavo duṣṭāś caurā dhūrtā

children.translated_text: and brazen ones,
rejecting good people, acted with no regard for <s>dharma</s>.'

body.translated_text: 'Then many wicked ones, thieves, scoundrels,

children.translated_text: 'Then, from the accumulation of sin, <s>Kali</s> (strife) spread everywhere.',

children.text: saddharmo durbalībhūto nīcavad vilayaṃ yayau // Dak_17.8 //
children.translated_text: 'The true <s>dharma</s> became weakened and went to dissolution like a lowly thing.'
'Then, when the course of <s>Kali</s> had become powerful,
all the lords of the world, seeing [this], turned their faces away from the wicked.'
'Likewise, the other gods too turned their faces away from all protection.',

children.text: teṣāṃ saṃdarśanaṃ kartum api naiva vavāñchire // Dak_17.10 //
children.translated_text: 'They did not even desire to grant them an audience.'

children.text: teṣāṃ trātuṃ tadeko 'pi na śasaka kathaṃ cana /
children.translated_text: 'Not even one among them was able to protect them in any way.',

children.text: evam atra mahotpātaṃ prāvartata samantataḥ // Dak_17.11 //
children.translated_text: 'Thus a great calamity arose there on all sides.'
'All with selves afflicted by defilements waged war against each other.',
'Due to the intensity of their sins, calamities arose.'

body.text: tato 'ndhakārāś ca prādurbhūtā meghaiś channāḥ

children.translated_text: and a great untimely storm and thunderbolt

children.text: meghair guḍuguḍāyate / vidyutaś ca niścaranti / daśa diśaś cākulībhūtās tamo'ndhakāraś ca prādurbhūtaḥ / candrasūryau na prabhāsvarau bhavataḥ / vātavṛṣṭiḥ pravāyati / jalākulībhūtā pralayakālam iva pṛthivī na dṛdhā ca kaiś cid bhūtair āviṣṭābhūt // tadā sarvajanakāyā bhītāḥ saṃvignamanasaḥ
children.translated_text: rumbled in the clouds. Lightnings flashed forth. The ten directions became agitated, and a darkness of obscurity appeared. The sun and moon did not shine. Wind and rain blew. The earth, flooded with water, as if at the time of dissolution, was not firm, and was possessed by certain beings. Then all the people were frightened, with agitated minds.

children.text: ye ke cid brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo brahmāṇaṃ namasyanti / ke cin maheśvaraṃ nārāyaṇaṃ śakraṃ māṇibhadraṃ hārītiṃ candrasūryagrahanakṣatrān namasyamānā yācayanti // ke cin nadīhradasarastaḍāgavāpīkūpādīni pariyācayanti / tathāpi na kaś cit paritrāṇaṃ bhavati //
children.translated_text: Some <s>Brāhmaṇas</s> and householders worshipped <s>Brahmā</s>. Some worshipped and entreated <s>Maheśvara</s>, <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Māṇibhadra</s>, <s>Hārītī</s>, the moon, the sun, the planets, and the constellations. Some entreated rivers, lakes, pools, ponds, reservoirs, wells, and the like. Even so, no protection came.

body.translated_text: 'Then darkness appeared, covered by clouds,

children.text: ) atha ke cid buddhadharmasaṃghābhiprasannā buddhadharmasaṃghān namasyanti //
children.translated_text: Then some, having faith in the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>, worshipped the <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṃgha</s>:

body.text: bhagavan sarvadarśī tvaṃ

children.text: katham asmād vayam evaṃrūpād upadravato bhayasthānāt parimucyema /
children.translated_text: How may we be freed from this kind of calamity and danger?

body.translated_text: 'Blessed One, you are all-seeing!

body.text: bhagavan nātha īdṛśād upadravāt trātā bhava //
body.translated_text: Blessed One, protector, be our savior from such a calamity!'

body.text: ity uktvā bauddhāya namaskāraṃ kṛtvā cintāparo vyavasthitaḥ // atrāntare nāsti kiṃ cid buddhānāṃ bhagavatām aviditam avijñātam / dharmatā khalu buddhānāṃ bhagavatāṃ mahākāruṇikānāṃ lokānugrahapravṛttikānām, ekākārarakṣāṇāṃ, śamathavipaśyanāvihāriṇāṃ, tridamathavastukuśalānāṃ, caturoghottīrṇānāṃ caturṛddhipādacaraṇatalasupratiṣṭhitānāṃ caturṣu saṃgrahavastuṣu dīrgharātrakṛtaparicayānāṃ, pañcā

children.translated_text: limbs

children.text: viprahīṇānāṃ pañcagatisamatikrāntānāṃ, ṣaḍaṅgasamanvāgatānāṃ ṣaṭpāramitāparipūrṇānāṃ, saptabodhyaṅgakusumāḍhyānāṃ, aṣṭāṅgamārgadarśānāṃ navānupūrvavihārasamāpattikuśalānāṃ, daśabalabalināṃ daśadiksamāpūrṇayaśasāṃ daśaśatavaśavartiprativiśiṣṭānāṃ trirātres tridivasasya buddhacakṣuṣā lokaṃ vyavalokya jñānadarśanaṃ pravartate / ko hīyate ko vardhate kaḥ kṛcchraprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃkaṭaprāptaḥ kaḥ saṃbādhaprāptaḥ kaḥ kṛcchrasaṃbādhaprāptaḥ kasya duḥkhapaṅkanimagnasya hastoddhāraṃ dadyām uddhārayeyam iti
children.translated_text: [of defilement], who have transcended the five destinies, who possess the six limbs [of virtue], who have fulfilled the six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections), who are adorned with the flowers of the seven limbs of awakening, who show the eightfold path, who are skilled in the nine successive attainments, who have the strength of the ten powers, whose fame fills the ten directions, who excel in rulership over ten hundred [domains] — [it is their nature that] with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye, surveying the world three times nightly and three times daily, knowledge-and-vision arises: 'Who is declining? Who is progressing? Who has reached difficulty? Who has reached distress? Who has reached constraint? Who has reached difficulty and constraint? To whom, sunk in the mire of suffering, shall I extend my hand and lift him out?'

body.translated_text: Having said this, they bowed to the <s>Buddha</s> and stood absorbed in worry. In the meanwhile — there is nothing unknown or unperceived by the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>. For it is the nature of the Blessed <s>Buddhas</s>, who are greatly compassionate, whose activity is the benefitting of the world, who are guardians of one form, who dwell in <s>śamatha</s> (calm) and <s>vipaśyanā</s> (insight), who are skilled in the three means of taming, who have crossed the four floods, who are well-established on the soles of the four bases of supernatural power, who have long cultivated the four means of gathering [disciples], who are free from the five

body.text: atha tatkṣaṇam eva pratisarann abhyutthāya, āyuṣmadānandapramukhān bhikṣusaṃghān āmantrayate sma // bho bhikṣava ānandapramukhā vaiśālīnagarīṃ gatvā mamājñayā mama vacanena vaiśālīnagarīṃ gatvā vīthīmadhye niṣaṇṇā imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣaya

children.translated_text: Then certainly all obstacle-spirits and seizing-spirits
will be pacified, and all calamities and wicked beings
will flee. Namely, these verses:

body.translated_text: Then, at that very moment, turning back and rising, he addressed the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> headed by the venerable <s>Ānanda</s>: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s> headed by <s>Ānanda</s>! Go to the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>! By my command, by my word, having gone to the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s> and seated yourselves in the middle of the street, recite this verse!

body.text: visarata visarata duṣṭasattvā muñcata muñcata mā tiṣṭhantu, īti

children.translated_text: be pacified!'

body.translated_text: 'Scatter! Scatter, O wicked beings! Release! Release! Do not remain! May the calamity

body.text: iti uddiśya bhikṣugaṇān visarjayām āsa //
body.translated_text: Thus instructing, he dispatched the assembly of monks.

body.text: atha te bhikṣavo bhagavataś caraṇayoḥ praṇipatya bhagavataḥ vacanaṃ śirasā nidhāya, imā vighnotsāraṇadhāraṇī hṛdayagatā // tatkṣaṇam evarddhyā ca vaihāyasād ānandapramukhāḥ pañcaśatabhikṣugaṇā lohitapakṣarājahaṃsa iva gagaṇadeśāt taṃ viṣayam anuprāptāḥ // athānandapramukhā bhikṣugaṇā vaiśālīnagarīṃ gatvā vīthīmadhye sthitvā brahmasvareṇa ekamatenaikasvareṇa imāṃ gāthāṃ bhāṣitum ārabdhāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks), having bowed at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s> and placed his words upon their heads, [recited] this <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) for dispelling obstacles, holding it in their hearts. At that very moment, by miraculous power—

children.translated_text: And these verses:

body.text: visarata visarata

children.translated_text: The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate toward the world, commands!

children.text:
muñcata
muñcata ma tiṣṭhantu / ītir vyupaśāmyatu
children.translated_text: Release! Release! Let them not remain! Let the calamity be pacified!
Depart! Depart! The <s>Buddha</s>, the great god, supreme among gods, the teacher, enters!

children.text: sendrāś ca devāḥ sabrahmakāḥ saprajāpatikaś catvāraś ca lokapālā
children.translated_text: The gods with <s>Indra</s> and with <s>Brahmā</s> and with <s>Prajāpati</s>, and the four world-guardians

children.text: praviśanti anekāni ca devatāsahasrāṇi / asurendrāś ca anekāni asuraśatasahasrāṇi prativasanti / bahūni ca bhūtasahasrāṇi bhagavato 'bhiprasannāni prabhaviṣyanti sarvasattvānām arthe / te co mā anarthaṃ kariṣyanti //
children.translated_text: enter, and many thousands of deities! The lords of <s>asuras</s> and many hundreds of thousands of <s>asuras</s> reside here! And many thousands of beings are devoted to the <s>Bhagavān</s>—

body.translated_text: "Disperse! Disperse!

body.text: nirgacchata nirgacchata

children.translated_text: Flee quickly!
If those of evil intent do not depart, they shall be destroyed!

children.text: maitracittā nāparādhakāmā rakṣāṃ cānuvartitukāmās te tiṣṭhantu praviśantu / buddho lokānukampaka evam ājñāpayati sarvasattvahitādhyāśayo maitrīvihārī kāruṇikavihārī muditāviharī upekṣāvihārī //
children.translated_text: Those who are of loving mind, who do not wish to cause harm, and who wish to follow the protection—let them stay, let them enter! The <s>Buddha</s>, compassionate toward the world, thus commands, with an intention for the welfare of all beings, abiding in <s>maitrī</s> (loving-kindness)—"

body.translated_text: Depart! Depart!

children.translated_text: "These mantra-words are accomplished, these verses of power are proclaimed by the <s>Jina</s> (Victor);

children.text: sarveṣāṃ devatānāṃ ca bhūtānāṃ ca hitaiṣiṇām // Dak_17.13 //
children.translated_text: for all deities and beings who wish for welfare."
"By knowledge, by the supreme purpose, and by the nature of <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: jagatām ītayaḥ sarvāḥ śāmyantv ārogyam astu vaḥ // Dak_17.14 //
children.translated_text: may all calamities of the world be pacified! May health be yours!"

body.text: iti bhāṣyamāṇe sarvabhūtagaṇā

children.text: saṃtrastāḥ samvignamanaso daśa diśaḥ palāyitvā vilayaṃ gatā duṣṭasattvā vihethacittā
children.translated_text: terrified, with agitated minds, fled in the ten directions and disappeared—the evil beings with harmful intentions

children.text: kupitacittāḥ pratipraśabdhā abhūvan // tadā ca vihāyasi ghanavidyuvātavṛṣṭijalākulapraśāntābhūt //
children.translated_text: and angry minds became pacified. And then in the sky, the disturbance of dense lightning, wind, and rain-water was calmed.

body.translated_text: When this was spoken, all the hosts of beings,

body.text: phalapuṣpapratimaṇḍitasurasasvādūni cābhūvan //
body.translated_text: Fruits and flowers were adorned, and the juices became delicious.

body.text: evaṃ buddhānubhāvena tasyāṃ nagaryāṃ sarvopadravadurbhikṣaṃ praśāntya, sarva ṛtavo yathābhiprāyaṃ kāle tathā samṛdhyati kāle varṣati kāle vāyavaḥ pravāyanti //
body.translated_text: Thus, by the power of the <s>Buddha</s>, in that city all calamities and famine were pacified; all seasons prospered according to their proper times, rain fell in due season, and winds blew in due season—

body.text: tadā sarvajanakāyāḥ praharṣajātāḥ sarvabhikṣugaṇān vāsena bhaktena nimantritā
body.translated_text: Then all the people, filled with joy, invited all the communities of <s>bhikṣus</s> with lodging and food,

body.text: atha khalu bhikṣava ānandaprabhṛtayo varṣātyayāc charadaḥ śaradātyayāc caturmāsātyayāc chiśiraḥ samāyātaḥ tadā janakāyān evam āha // vayam api māsacatuṣṭayam agamat atrāsthitā guror antikaṃ gacchāmaḥ //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>bhikṣus</s> led by <s>Ānanda</s>, after the passing of the rains, then autumn, then after the four months, winter having arrived—then he said to the people: "We too, after these four months—"

body.text: ity ukte sarvajanakāyā bhikṣugaṇān gamanakālam api jñātvā satkṛtya pūjayitvā mānayitvā visarjayām āsuḥ //
body.translated_text: When this was said, all the people, knowing that the time for the <s>bhikṣus</s> to depart had come, honored, worshipped, and revered them, and bade them farewell.

body.text: atha te bhikṣavo dhīratayā nagaraṃ nagarāc caṃkramyamāṇā anyatamajanapadaviṣayam anuprāptāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bhikṣus</s>, traveling steadily from town to town, arrived in the territory of a certain countryside.

body.text: atha tasmiñ janapade mahāḍhyo dhanakanakasamṛddho mahābhogo vistīrṇaparigraho mahātyāgo mahāparivāraḥ śuddhāśayo dharmātmā paropakārī śramaṇabrāhmaṇavaṇīpakeṣv abhirato duḥkhīnāṃ duḥkhatārako mahākaruṇādṛṣṭaḥ śuddhaceto nāma śreṣṭhī dvātriṃśatābhir vanitābhiḥ parivṛtaḥ sukhalīlayā tiṣṭhati // kāle tyāga

children.text: kāle upābhogaḥ // sa śreṣṭhī tān bhikṣūn samāgatān dṛṣṭvā śītārtenāgatam iti jñātvātikaruṇābhibhūtaḥ sādarair agnimathe nītvā ujjvālikāṃ prajvālya dadāti / tena śreṣṭhinā bahavo 'gnimaṭhāḥ kāritāḥ santi / tasmāt pañcaśatabhikṣugaṇā agnitāpaiḥ saṃtarpitāḥ // tataḥ paścād annāhārāḥ pradattāḥ / te bhikṣavas tad annaṃ na bhuktā
children.translated_text: in due season, supplies were available. That merchant, seeing those <s>bhikṣus</s> arriving, knowing they had come afflicted by cold, overwhelmed with compassion, led them respectfully to a fire-hall, lit a warming fire, and gave—

children.text: / tad dṛṣṭvā sa śreṣṭhī tān uvāca // kena bhikṣavo mayā dattānnaṃ nopabhuktam //
children.translated_text: Seeing that, the merchant said to them: "Why, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, have you not eaten the food given by me?"

body.translated_text: Now in that countryside there was a very wealthy [merchant], prosperous in riches and gold, of great fortune, with extensive possessions, of great generosity, with a large retinue, of pure intention, righteous, devoted to helping others, hospitable to <s>śramaṇas</s> (ascetics) and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>—

body.text: bhikṣava ūcuḥ // buddho bhikṣavo yam akāle na bhoktavyaṃ sūryāstaniśākālam iti //
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> said: "The <s>Buddha</s> [has said] that <s>bhikṣus</s> should not eat at improper times—after sunset and during the night."

body.text: tataḥ sa śreṣṭhī tathety uktvā gṛhaṃ praviśati //
body.translated_text: Then the merchant, saying "So be it," entered his house.

body.text: atha sa rātryatyayāt prātaḥkāle yathāyogyānusāraiḥ piṇḍapātrādi dattvā tān satkārayām āsa //
body.translated_text: Then, after the passing of the night, in the morning, he gave alms-bowls and other things as was appropriate, and honored them.

body.text: atha te bhikṣavas taṃ gṛhītvā tasmai śuddhāśiṣaṃ dattvā gamiṣyāma ity ārocya tasmāt sthānān niṣkrāntāḥ / niṣkramya yena gṛddhakūte bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntā upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā ekānte niṣaṇṇāḥ //
body.translated_text: Then those <s>bhikṣus</s>, having received that and given him pure blessings, announced "We shall depart" and left that place. Having departed, they approached <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s> (Vulture Peak) where the <s>Bhagavān</s> was—

body.text: athānandabhikṣur utthāyāsanād bhagavataḥ prataḥ sthitvaivam āha // bhagavan sarvajña yathā bhavadājñā tathā vaiśālīnagaryāṃ sarvā ītayaḥ praśāntā abhūvan //
body.translated_text: Then the <s>bhikṣu</s> <s>Ānanda</s>, rising from his seat, standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s>, spoke thus: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, O Omniscient One, as per your command, in the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, all calamities were pacified—

body.text: tava prabhāvād iti kṛtvā vayam atrāgatā sma //
body.translated_text: by your power, and therefore we have come here."

body.text: bhagavān āha // sādhu sādhu ānanda sādhu sādhu bhikṣavaḥ / evaṃ parārthakṛte udyogakaraṇīyam //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "Well done, well done, <s>Ānanda</s>! Well done, well done, <s>bhikṣus</s>! Thus should effort be made for the sake of others."

body.text: punar bhagavantam ānanda āha //
body.translated_text: Again <s>Ānanda</s> spoke to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

body.text: bhagavan vaiśālīnagaryāṃ nivṛttakāle 'nyatamajanapadaviṣayam anuprāptāḥ / tāṃ nagarīṃ vayam agamat / anyatamaśreṣṭhī āḍhyo 'smān śītavātapariśramād āgatān dṛṣṭvā sādareṇāhūya, ādāv agnimaṭhe praṇīyāgniṃ prajvālya dadāti / bahavo 'gnimaṭhāḥ santi // śreṣṭhī paramadhārmiko 'sau purusaḥ / ye ye śramaṇabrāhmaṇatīrthikāś cāgatās tebhyaḥ sarvebhya ujjvālikā

children.translated_text: lit [a fire] and offered it, with faith, during the winter-cold season."

body.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, when we had departed from the city of <s>Vaiśālī</s>, we arrived in the territory of a certain countryside. We went to that town. A certain wealthy merchant, [seeing] us arriving exhausted by cold wind—

body.text: bhagavān āha // mahāphalānuśaṃsā ujjvālikāyāḥ śiśirāgame 'mṛtopamā tasmān mahāphalānuśaṃsā ujjvalikāyāḥ śṛṇuta bhikṣavaḥ kathayāmi //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One) said: "Of great fruit and benefit is the warming fire at the onset of winter, like nectar; therefore, of great fruit and benefit is the warming fire. Listen, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, I shall tell you:

body.text:
nānāsāraṅgarūpaprabhavamṛdumahadromasaṃślāghyavastrā
hemante garbhagehe priyatamavanitābāhuyugmopagūḍhāḥ /
yat krīḍanti kṣitīśā vividharasavarair annapānaiḥ samṛddhās ta

children.translated_text: that is the exceedingly sweet fruit of the warming fire offered to the <s>bhikṣu-saṃgha</s> (community of monks)."

body.translated_text: "That kings sport in winter in inner chambers, embraced in the arms of their most beloved wives, clad in praiseworthy garments of various soft, great furs of diverse animals, with food of various delightful flavors—

body.text: jvālātaraṅgavikasaddahanopagūḍhāṃ bhīmasvanāṃ śiśiraśītavināśakartrīm / ujjvālikāṃ munivarapravarāya dattvā dīptaprabho bhavati devamanuṣyaloke //
body.translated_text: "Having offered a warming fire—embraced by billowing waves of flame, terrifying in sound, destroyer of the cold of winter—to the supreme among sages, one becomes radiant in the world of gods and humans."

body.text:
gandharvāsurakinnaraiḥ sahacarā dedīpyamānānanā
vidyujjvālaśaracchaśāṅkasadṛśā

children.text:
kāntābhir āliṅgitāḥ /
svarge yad vicaranti dīptavapuṣo līlāyamānāḥ surās
children.translated_text: embraced by beautiful women, that the gods of radiant bodies wander in heaven, sporting—

children.text: tad dattvāryaganāya śītasamaye cojjvālikāṃ śraddhayā // Dak_17.17 //
children.translated_text: that is from having offered a warming fire to the noble community with faith during the cold season."

body.translated_text: "Accompanied by <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), <s>asuras</s> (demons), and <s>kinnaras</s> (celestial beings), with blazing faces, resembling lightning-flames and the autumn moon,

body.text: jitvā ripūn ye gajavājiyuktā

children.translated_text: rule the earth on every side,

children.text: dīptānanā hemavibhūṣitāṅgā ujjvālikāyāḥ phalam eva teṣām // Dak_17.18 //
children.translated_text: with blazing faces and bodies adorned with gold—that is indeed the fruit of the warming fire."

body.translated_text: "That those who have conquered their enemies, yoked with elephants and horses,

children.text: te tādṛśaṃ cet phala prāptukāmā ujjvālikāṃ ye manujāḥ pradeyuḥ /
children.translated_text: "Those humans who desire to attain such fruit should give the warming fire,

children.text: hemantaśīte 'gnimaṭhāni kṛtvā bhikṣvādaye cāryagaṇāya nityam // Dak_17.19 //
children.translated_text: building fire-halls in the cold of winter, always for the noble community headed by <s>bhikṣus</s>."

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyām ujjvālikādānakathā saptadaśamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the story of offering the warming fire, the seventeenth chapter.

body.text: XVIII. dīpakathā
body.translated_text: XVIII. The Story of Lamps

body.text: atha khalu maitreyo bodhisattvo mahāsattvo bhagavantam etad avocat //
body.translated_text: Then indeed the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>mahāsattva</s> <s>Maitreya</s> said this to the <s>Bhagavān</s>:

children.text: bhagavañ chrotum icchāmi, dīpadānasya yat phalam /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, I wish to hear the fruit of the gift of lamps—

children.text: stūpe vā buddhabimbe vā vada lokārthahetave // Dak_18.1 //
children.translated_text: whether at a <s>stūpa</s> or at a <s>Buddha</s> image—speak for the benefit of the world."

body.text: bhagavān kṣaṇaṃ tūṣṇīm āsthāya parṣadaṃ samālokya ca maitreyam āmantryaivam āha //
body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed One), remaining silent for a moment, surveying the assembly, and addressing <s>Maitreya</s>, spoke thus:

children.translated_text: "Listen, O <s>Maitreya</s>, I shall speak for the benefit of the worlds;

children.text: yac chrutaṃ tatkathāṃ bhavyāṃ śrutvā prāmodya jāyate // Dak_18.2 //
children.translated_text: having heard this auspicious story, great joy will arise."

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte

children.text: dhvāni ekanavatikalpe vipaśvī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaranasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ puruṣadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca manuṣyānāṃ ca buddho bhagavān // sa bandhumatīṃ rājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati sma // yāvad vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddhaḥ sakalabuddhakāryaṃ kṛtvendhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinirvṛtas tasya rājñā bandhumatā śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojanaś catūratnamayaḥ stūpaḥ pratiṣṭhāpito 'bhūt krośam uccatvena //
children.translated_text: era, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic age), a perfectly and fully awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśvin</s> arose in the world, endowed with knowledge and conduct, well-gone, knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of men to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans—

body.translated_text: "Long ago, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past

body.text: yatrānekāni prāṇiśatasahasrāṇi kālaṃ kṛtvā svargamokṣaparāyaṇāni bhavanti //
body.translated_text: where many hundreds of thousands of beings, having died, were destined for heaven and liberation.

body.text: tatra stūpe mahotsāho vartate

children.text: śraddhā brāhmaṇagṛhapatayo vicitrair gandhamālyavilepanaiś chattradhvajapatākābhiḥ pūjābhiḥ kurvanti sma //
children.translated_text: faithful <s>brāhmaṇas</s> (priests) and householders were performing worship with various fragrant garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags.

body.translated_text: At that <s>stūpa</s>, a great festival was taking place;

body.text: athāpareṇa samayenāsyāṃ nagaryām anyatamaḥ puruṣaḥ karacaraṇayihīnaḥ kuṣṭhaśarīraḥ kutrāpi gamanam asamarthaḥ

children.text: tām eva vārttāṃ pratiśrutya tasyaitad abhavat //
children.translated_text: Having heard that very news, this thought occurred to him:

body.translated_text: Then, at another time, in that city there was a certain man, deprived of hands and feet, his body afflicted with leprosy, unable to go anywhere.

body.text: aho brāhmaṇagṛhapataya imaṃ stūpaṃ pratipūjayanti / tathāham evaṃ pūjayeyaṃ pādapāṇivihīno gamanāsamarthaḥ kathaṃ gaccheyam

children.text: ity uktvā tasya buddhir utpannā // adya rātrau svakāyavibhavabalasthāma saṃjanayya gṛhān niṣkramayeyaṃ niṣkramya ca yadi samartham asti tāvat pradakṣiṇīkrīyate //
children.translated_text: Having said this, a thought arose in him: "Tonight, gathering the strength, vigor, and power of my own body, I shall crawl out of my house; and having crawled out, if I am able, I shall at least circumambulate—"

body.translated_text: "Ah, the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> and householders worship this <s>stūpa</s>! I too would worship in such a manner, but deprived of feet and hands, unable to walk—how shall I go?"

body.text: ity uktvā rātrau candracandrikāvirājamāne prabhāsvare kāyasthāmabalaṃ saṃjanayya stūpasya samīpaṃ balādhānenānuprāptaḥ // sa styānamiddhavyathayā paripīḍitagātro niśvasya bhūmau nipātitaḥ // atha sa puruṣa imaṃ stūpaṃ namaskṛtya svayam evam aṅgaparivartanena pradakṣiṇīkartum ārabdhaḥ / tatas tām eva rātriṃ sampūrṇam aṣṭottaraśatapradakṣiṇaṃ cakāra // athāsya puruṣasya bauddhaprabhāvāt tatkṣaṇaṃ pādāṅgulī samyak bhūtvāgatāḥ

children.translated_text: and likewise, the sprouts of his hands
were restored;
the leprosy on his body was pacified;
his obstructions from past <s>karma</s> were destroyed, and by this root of merit from arduous vows, he became pure of body.

body.translated_text: Having said this, at night, when the moon was shining brightly with its radiance, gathering the strength and power of his body, he reached the vicinity of the <s>stūpa</s> by the force of his will. He, overcome by torpor, lethargy, and pain—

body.text: atha sa puruṣaḥ prasādajātaḥ punar api stūpe 'ṣṭāṅgapraṇāmaṃ kṛtvātha prabhāte manohlādita

children.text: prahasitavadanaḥ svagṛhaṃ pratyāgataḥ // atha svagṛhe patnyādiparijanas tam āgataṃ dṛṣṭvāvarjitamanā ūcuḥ // aho kva gato 'si
children.translated_text: with a smiling face, returned to his own house. Then at his house, his wife and other family members, seeing him returned, their minds captivated, said: "Ah, where have you gone?

body.translated_text: "Formerly, there was a <s>Bhagavān</s>, a <s>Tathāgata</s>, an <s>Arhat</s>, a perfectly and fully awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Candravimalasūryaprabhāsaśrī</s> (Splendor of the Radiance of the Moon-Pure Sun). The lifespan of that <s>Bhagavān</s>, perfectly and fully awakened <s>Buddha</s>, was forty-two hundred thousand <s>kalpas</s>. The lifespans of those <s>bodhisattvas</s>, <s>mahāsattvas</s>, and <s>śrāvakas</s> were likewise. For his worship, a <s>bodhisattva</s> named <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>, at that time, having entered a <s>samādhi</s> (meditative concentration) called <s>Sarvasattvarūpadarśana</s> (Vision-of-the-form-of-all-beings) — by the power of that <s>samādhi</s>, immediately upon attaining it, from the sky above, a great shower of <s>mandārava</s> and <s>mahāmandārava</s> flowers rained down. body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>, mindful and fully aware, arose from that <s>samādhi</s>. Having arisen, he reflected thus: 'The worship of the <s>Bhagavān</s> is not so [well] accomplished by displaying miraculous powers as by the renunciation of one's own body.'

children.translated_text: ...having drenched [his body] with fragrant oil, he set his body ablaze for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and for the worship of this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Law). Then, by the light of the flames released from his body-lamp, world-realms equal in number to the sands of eighty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers were illuminated. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> in those world-realms, equal in number to the sands of eighty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, gave their approval: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! This is the supreme, most difficult heroic effort of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — true worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, worship of the <s>Dharma</s>! Likewise, worship with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags — this, O son of good family, is foremost giving; whereas the giving [that consists in] the renunciation of kingdom, beloved son, wife, and the like is not [its equal].'

body.translated_text: Then the <s>bodhisattva</s> <s>Sarvasattvapriyadarśana</s>, at that time, having consumed <s>aguru</s> (aloe), <s>turuṣka</s> (frankincense), and <s>kunduruka</s> (olibanum), drank <s>campaka</s> oil. Continuously eating fragrance and drinking fragrant oil — twelve years passed. Then, after the passage of twelve years, he wrapped his own body in divine garments, drenched it with fragrant oil, and set his body ablaze for the worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s> and for the worship of this <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> (Lotus of the True Law). Then, by the light of the flames released from his body-lamp, world-realms equal in number to the sands of eighty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers were illuminated. The <s>Tathāgatas</s> in those world-realms, equal in number to the sands of eighty <s>Gaṅgā</s> rivers, gave their approval: 'Well done, well done, O son of good family! This is the supreme and extremely difficult heroic effort of <s>bodhisattvas</s> — true worship of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, worship of the <s>Dharma</s>! Worship with flowers, incense, fragrance, garlands, ointments, parasols, banners, and flags — O son of good family, this is foremost giving; the giving of renouncing kingdom, beloved son, wife, and the like is not [equal to it].'

Then that man, with joy and delight arisen, having gazed into the sky, having bowed with joined palms, stood there. Then that man, having truly resolved, wrapping his own body in divine white cloth, anointing it with fragrant substances in the measure of his own body, saying 'great lamp,' lit a lamp at the relic-<s>stūpa</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Vipaśvin</s>. And they also made a garland of lamps,

body.text: tataḥ sa puruṣas tena kuśalamūlena ca praṇidhānavaśād dīpārciṣalokadhātau dīparājo nāma pratyekabuddha upapannaḥ pañcābhijñāprāptaḥ // tataḥ sa pratyekabuddhaḥ saṃsāram asāram iti jñātvā vidyud iva prātihāryaṃ kṛtvā vihāyasaṃ saptatālamātram abhyudgamya ca tejodhātuṃ samāpadyolkeva parinirvāti sma // yat tasya pittaśleṣmamāṃsāsthisnāyurudhiraṃ tat sarvaṃ tejasā paryavadātam agamac chuddhaśarīro 'bhūt // evaṃrūpeṇa saṃsāre 'nantasukham anuprāpya nirvāṇabhūmiṃ gacchati sma //
body.translated_text: Then that man, by the power of that root of merit and his vow, was reborn as a <s>pratyekabuddha</s> (solitary awakened one) named <s>Dīparāja</s> (King of Lamps) in the world-realm <s>Dīpārcis</s> (Lamp-flame), having attained the five supernatural powers. Then that <s>pratyekabuddha</s>, knowing <s>saṃsāra</s> to be without essence, performing a miracle like lightning, rising into the air to the height of seven palm-trees, and entering the fire-element, he attained <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (final passing) like a meteor. His bile, phlegm, flesh, bones, sinews, and blood — all of that was completely purified by the fire, and he became of pure body. In such a manner, having attained infinite happiness in <s>saṃsāra</s>, he went to the ground of <s>nirvāṇa</s>.

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: "Listen, O <s>Ajita</s> (<s>Maitreya</s>), well and attentively; I shall speak. The merit born from honoring <s>stūpas</s> is exceedingly great."

body.text: tadyathānuśrūyate //
body.translated_text: "As is traditionally heard:"

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ maitreyaikasmin samaye kapilavastuni mahānagaryāṃ nyagrodhārāme mahatā saṃghena sārdha

children.text: viharati sma / tasminn avasare tatra kapilavastuny anyatamaḥ śākya āḍhyo mahādhano mahābhogo vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇadhanapratispardhī
children.translated_text: of [monks]. On that occasion, there in <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> [clansman] — wealthy, of great riches, of great possessions, of extensive and vast property, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> (Kubera), rivaling the wealth of <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s> —

children.text: tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam / sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramati paricārayati / tasya krīḍato ramataḥ paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā saṃvṛttā
children.translated_text: brought a wife from a family equal [to his]. He enjoyed, sported, and dallied with her. As he enjoyed, sported, and dallied, his wife became with child.

children.text: sā aṣṭānāṃ vā navānāṃ vā māsānām atyayāt prasūtā
children.translated_text: After the passage of eight or nine months, she gave birth.

children.text: dārako jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko 'tikrāntamānuṣyavarṇaḥ saṃprāptaś ca divyaṃ suvarṇa
children.translated_text: A boy was born — handsome, beautiful to behold, pleasing, surpassing human complexion, and he had attained a divine golden [hue],
like a gold coin of <s>Jāmbūnada</s> [gold].

children.text: suvarṇavarṇayā cānena prabhayā sarvaṃ kapilavastu nagaram avabhāsitam / taddarśanān (
children.translated_text: By his golden-colored radiance, the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was illuminated. At seeing that, (
[Page] 203
) the parents and other beings who came out of curiosity

children.text: paraṃ vismayam āgatāś cintayanti ca kuto
children.translated_text: were filled with the utmost wonder and thought: 'Whence

children.text: yam īdṛśaḥ sattvaviśeṣa iti // tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpyate / kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti // jñātaya ūcuḥ // yasmād anena jātena suvarṇavarṇayā prabhayā sarvaṃ kapilavastu nagaram avabhāsitam, tasmād bhavatu dārakasya suvarṇābha iti nāma // tataḥ suvarṇābho dāraka aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo 'nupradattaḥ / dvābhyām aṃsadhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ kṣīradhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ maladhātrībhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ krīḍanikābhyāṃ
children.translated_text: has this special being [come]?' At his birth, having celebrated the birth-festival, a name was established: 'What shall be the name of the boy?' The kinsmen said: 'Since by his birth the entire city of <s>Kapilavastu</s> was illuminated with golden-colored radiance, let the boy's name be <s>Suvarṇābha</s> (Golden-radiance).' Then the boy <s>Suvarṇābha</s> was entrusted to eight nurses — two arm-nurses, two milk-nurses, two bathing-nurses, and two play-nurses.

children.text: so 'ṣṭābhir dhātrībhir unnīyate vardhyate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍenānyaiś cottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣair āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam / sa ca paṇḍito vyakto medhāvī śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipannaḥ kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ // yāvad apareṇa samayena rūpamadamatto bahir adhiṣṭhānasya krīḍati
children.translated_text: He was raised and nourished by eight nurses with milk, curds, fresh butter, clarified butter, the cream of ghee, and other specially prepared provisions — he grew quickly, like a lotus in a lake. He was wise, discerning, intelligent, faithful, virtuous, of wholesome disposition, pursuing his own benefit and the benefit of others, compassionate, great-souled, and desirous of <s>dharma</s>. Then, at another time, intoxicated with the pride of beauty, he was playing outside his residence.

children.text: tatas tasyaiva mārgāt saṃbahulāś ca śākyā nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchanti / tatas tena suvarṇābhena dṛṣṭāḥ pṛṣṭāś ca kva bhavanto gacchantīti / tair uktaṃ nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchāmo buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ draṣṭum iti / suvarṇābhasya (
children.translated_text: Then, along that very path, numerous <s>Śākyas</s> were going to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park. Then <s>Suvarṇābha</s> saw them and asked: 'Where are you going, sirs?' They said: 'We are going to the <s>Nyagrodha</s> Park to see the <s>Buddha Bhagavān</s>.' <s>Suvarṇābha</s>'s (

children.text: ) buddha iti śrutvāśrutapūrvaṃ nāma śrutvā sarvaromakūpāny āhṛṣṭāni paramaṃ ca kutūhalam utpannam
children.translated_text: Upon hearing the name 'Buddha,' a name never heard before, all the pores of his body bristled with joy and the highest curiosity arose in him.

children.text: tasyaitad abhavat / yan nv aham api bhagavantaṃ darśanāyopasaṃkrameyam iti / so 'pi nyagrodhārāmaṃ gacchati / tataḥ sa dadarśa suvarṇābhakumāro buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ dvātriṃśatā mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaiḥ samalaṃkṛtam aśītyā cānuvyañjanair virājitagātraṃ vyāmaprabhālaṃkṛtaṃ sūryasahasrātirekaprabhaṃ jaṅgamam iva ratnaparvataṃ samantato bhadrakam
children.translated_text: He thought: 'Let me also approach the <s>Bhagavān</s> for an audience.' And so he went to the <s>Nyagrodhārāma</s> (Banyan Grove). There, <s>Suvarṇābha</s> beheld the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, adorned with the thirty-two marks of a great person, his body resplendent with the eighty minor characteristics, ornamented with the radiance of a fathom's length, surpassing the brilliance of a thousand suns, like a moving mountain of jewels, auspicious on all sides.

children.text: sahadarśanāc cāsya bhagavataḥ pādābhivandanaṃ kṛtvā purastān niṣaṇṇo dharmaśravaṇāya / tasya bhagavatā dharmo deśitaḥ
children.translated_text: Immediately upon seeing him, having paid homage at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he sat before him to hear the <s>Dharma</s>. The <s>Bhagavān</s> taught him the <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: sa taṃ dharmaṃ śrutvā pravrajyābhilāṣī saṃvṛttaḥ
children.translated_text: Having heard that <s>Dharma</s>, he became desirous of going forth into the monastic life.

children.text: yāvan mātāpitarāv anujñāpya bhagavatsakāśam upasaṃkrānta upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasā vanditvā yena bhagavāṃs tenāñjaliṃ praṇaṃya bhagavantam idam avocat / labheyāhaṃ bhadanta svākhyāte dharmavinaye pravrajyam upasaṃpadā
children.translated_text: Then, having obtained permission from his parents, he approached the <s>Bhagavān</s>, and having approached, bowing his head at the feet of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, extending his joined palms toward the <s>Bhagavān</s>, he said to the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'May I, venerable sir, receive the going forth (<s>pravrajyā</s>) and full ordination (<s>upasaṃpadā</s>)

children.text: bhikṣubhāvaṃ careyam ahaṃ bhagavato 'ntike brahmacaryam iti // tato bhagavān gajabhujasadṛśaṃ suvarṇavarṇabāhuṃ prasārya suvarṇābhadārakam idam avocat / ehi kumāra cara brahmacaryam iti //
children.translated_text: in the well-proclaimed <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>; may I live the holy life (<s>brahmacarya</s>) in the presence of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.' Then the <s>Bhagavān</s>, extending his golden-hued arm resembling an elephant's trunk, said to the boy <s>Suvarṇābha</s>: 'Come, young one, live the holy life.'

body.translated_text: "In former times, O <s>Maitreya</s>, at one time I was dwelling in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, in the <s>Nyagrodha</s> (Banyan) Park, together with a great community

children.text: ehīti coktaḥ sa tathāgatena muṇḍaś ca saṃghāṭiparītadehaḥ /
children.translated_text: Addressed by the <s>Tathāgata</s> with 'Come!', shaven-headed, his body clad in the monastic robe,

children.text: sadyaḥ praśāntendriya eva sthāne yathā sthito buddhamanorathena // Dak_20.2 //
children.translated_text: immediately with senses calmed, he stood in his place as one established by the <s>Buddha's</s> wish.

body.text: yāvat saptāhāvaropitakeśaśmaśru

children.text: dvādaśavarṣopasaṃpanneryāpathaḥ pātrakaravyagrahasto bhagavataḥ purastāt sthitaḥ / tasya bhagavatā manasikāro dattaḥ / tena yujyamānena vyāyacchamānena ghaṭamānena idam eva pañcagaṇḍakaṃ saṃsāracakraṃ calācalaṃ viditvā sarvasaṃskāragatiṃ śatanapatanavikaraṇavidhvaṃsanadharmatayā parāhatya sarvakleśaprahāṇād arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam
children.translated_text: having attained the deportment of one fully ordained at twelve years of age, standing before the <s>Bhagavān</s> with bowl and robe in hand — the <s>Bhagavān</s> gave him a subject for meditation. Striving, exerting, and endeavoring, having understood this five-pronged wheel of <s>saṃsāra</s> as unstable, having overcome all conditioned states through the nature of breaking, falling, scattering, and destruction, through the abandonment of all <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s>.

children.text: arhan saṃvṛttas tejodhātuvītarāgaḥ samaloṣṭakāñcana ākāśapāṇitalasamacitto vāsīcandanakalpo vidyāvidāritāṇḍakośo vidyābhijñāpratisaṃvitprāpto bhavalābhalobhasatkāraparāṅmukhas sendropendrāṇāṃ devānāṃ pūjyo mānyo 'bhivādyaś ca saṃvṛttaḥ //
children.translated_text: He became an <s>Arhat</s>, free from passion regarding the element of fire, regarding a clod of earth and gold as equal, with a mind as impartial as space and the palm of the hand, like a razor to sandalwood, his egg-shell of ignorance shattered by knowledge, having attained the <s>vidyās</s> (knowledges), <s>abhijñās</s> (superknowledges), and <s>pratisaṃvids</s> (analytical knowledges), turned away from attachment to existence, gain, greed, and honor — he became worthy of worship, reverence, and salutation by the gods including <s>Indra</s> and <s>Upendra</s>.

body.translated_text: Then, with hair and beard of seven days' growth removed,

body.text:
bhikṣavaḥ saṃśayajātāḥ sarvasaṃśayacchettāraṃ buddhaṃ bhagavantaṃ papracchuḥ /
kāni bhadanta suvarṇābhena puṇyāni kṛtāni yenaivaṃvidhaṃ mahottamaphalaṃ prāptam iti // bhagavān āha /
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s>, having doubts, asked the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>, the cutter of all doubts: 'What merits, venerable sir, were performed by <s>Suvarṇābha</s> that he obtained such a supreme and excellent fruit?' The <s>Bhagavān</s> said:

body.text:
suvarṇābhenaiva karmāṇi kṛtāni labdhasaṃbhārāṇi pariṇatapratyayāny oghavatpratyupasthitāny avaśyaṃbhāvīni / suvarṇābhena karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni ko 'nyaḥ pratyanubhaviṣyati / na bhikṣavaḥ karmāṇi kṛtāny upacitāni bāhyadhātau
pṛthivīdhātau vipacyante nābdhātau na tejodhātau na vāyudhātāv api tūpātteṣv eva skandhadhātvāyataneṣu karmāṇi kṛtāni vipacyante śubhāny aśubhāni ca /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>karmas</s> performed by <s>Suvarṇābha</s> himself, having their requisites gathered, their conditions matured, presenting themselves like a flood, inevitably coming to fruition — the <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated by <s>Suvarṇābha</s>, who else shall experience them? O <s>bhikṣus</s>, <s>karmas</s> performed and accumulated do not ripen in the external element of earth, nor in the element of water, nor in the element of fire, nor in the element of wind — but <s>karmas</s> performed ripen only in the appropriated aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), and sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), both auspicious and inauspicious.

children.translated_text: <s>Karmas</s> do not perish even in hundreds of <s>koṭis</s> of <s>kalpas</s>;

children.text: sāmagrīṃ prāpya kālaṃ ca phalanti khalu dehinām // Dak_20.3 //
children.translated_text: having met with the right conditions and time, they indeed bear fruit for embodied beings.

body.text: bhūtapūrvaṃ bhikṣavo 'tīte 'dhvani ekanavate kalpe vipaśvī nāma samyaksaṃbuddho loka udapādi vidyācaraṇasaṃpannaḥ sugato lokavid anuttaraḥ purusadamyasārathiḥ śāstā devānāṃ ca mānuṣyāṇāṃ ca buddho bhagavān

children.text: sa bandhumatīrājadhānīm upaniśritya viharati / yāvad vipaśvī samyaksaṃbuddho buddhakāryaṃ kṛtvā indhanakṣayād ivāgnir nirupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau parinivṛtaḥ / tato rājñā bandhumatā bhagavataḥ śarīre śarīrapūjāṃ kṛtvā samantayojana
children.translated_text: He dwelt near the royal capital <s>Bandhumatī</s>. Then the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, having accomplished the <s>Buddha's</s> work, like a fire whose fuel is exhausted, passed into <s>parinirvāṇa</s> in the <s>nirvāṇa</s> realm without remainder. Then King <s>Bandhumān</s>, having performed bodily worship of the <s>Bhagavān's</s> relics, established a <s>stūpa</s> one <s>yojana</s> in extent,
made of four kinds of precious substances, a <s>krośa</s> in height.
A <s>stūpa</s> festival was instituted.

body.translated_text: Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, in the past, in the ninety-first <s>kalpa</s>, a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> named <s>Vipaśyin</s> arose in the world — endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone), knower of the world, unsurpassed, charioteer of persons to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s> <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: yāvad anyatamo gṛhapatis tasmin stūpamahe vartamāne nirgataḥ

children.text: tena tasmāt stūpāt sauvarṇa ādarśaḥ patito dṛṣṭaḥ
children.translated_text: He saw a golden mirror that had fallen from that <s>stūpa</s>.

children.text: sa tenāvataṃsakaṃ kārayitvā tatra stūpe āropitaḥ
children.translated_text: Having had it made into an ornamental crest, he placed it on that <s>stūpa</s>.
Having made offerings of incense, fragrant substances, and flowers, prostrating at the feet, he made a vow

children.text: kṛtam / aham apy evaṃvidhānāṃ guṇanāṃ lābhī bhaviṣyāmi / evaṃvidham eva śāstāram ārāgayeyam iti //
children.translated_text: (<s>praṇidhāna</s>): "May I too become the recipient of such qualities. May I please just such a Teacher."'

body.translated_text: Then a certain householder came forth during that <s>stūpa</s> festival.

body.text: bhagavān āha // kiṃ manyadhve bhikṣavo yo

children.text: sau tena kālena tena samayena gṛhapatir āsīd ayaṃ
children.translated_text: at that time, on that occasion, was that householder — he
is this very <s>Suvarṇābha</s>.

children.text: yat tena vipaśvinaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya stūpe kārāḥ kṛtās tenāsyaivaṃvidho rūpaviśeṣaḥ saṃvṛtto yat praṇidhānaṃ kṛtaṃ tad ihaiva janmany arhattvaṃ sākṣātkṛtam iti //
children.translated_text: Because he performed those acts of devotion at the <s>stūpa</s> of the Perfectly Awakened <s>Vipaśyin</s>, therefore he obtained such distinction of form; and because of the vow he made, he directly realized <s>Arhatship</s> in this very birth.'

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'What do you think, O <s>bhikṣus</s>? He who

body.text: bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇānāṃ karmaṇām ekāntakṛṣṇo vipāka ekāntaśuklānām ekāntaśuklo vyatimiśrāṇāṃ vyatimiśras tasmāt tarhi bhikṣava ekāntakṛṣṇāni karmāṇy apāsya vyatimiśrāṇi ca ekāntaśukleṣv eva

children.text: sv ābhogaḥ karaṇīya ity evaṃ vo bhikṣavaḥ śikṣitavyam
children.translated_text: <s>karmas</s> — thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train.'

body.translated_text: 'O <s>bhikṣus</s>, the ripening of entirely dark <s>karmas</s> is entirely dark; of entirely bright ones, entirely bright; of mixed ones, mixed. Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, having abandoned entirely dark <s>karmas</s> and mixed ones, one should make effort only toward entirely bright

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān āttamanasas te bhikṣavo bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti //
body.translated_text: This the <s>Bhagavān</s> said. Those <s>bhikṣus</s>, delighted in mind, rejoiced at the <s>Bhagavān's</s> words.

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ suvarṇābhāvadāna viṃśatitamaḥ paricchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the <s>Suvarṇābhāvadāna</s> (Tale of <s>Suvarṇābha</s>), the twentieth chapter.

body.text: XXI. vapuṣmānavadāna
body.translated_text: XXI. The <s>Vapuṣmānavadāna</s> (Tale of <s>Vapuṣmān</s>)

children.translated_text: Then spoke the Lord of Sages, the Lion of the <s>Śākyas</s>, the mine of virtues,
surveying the assembly of <s>bhikṣus</s>, the tale of <s>Vapuṣmān</s>.

body.text: bhikṣava ūcuḥ //
body.translated_text: The <s>bhikṣus</s> said:

children.text: bhagavan sarvavic chāsta śrutvāsmākaṃ śubhāṃ giram /
children.translated_text: "O <s>Bhagavān</s>, omniscient Teacher, having heard our auspicious words,

children.text: yad buddhe kṛtapuṇyānāṃ punar vaktuṃ tvam arhasi // Dak_21.2 //
children.translated_text: you should again tell of the merits performed toward the <s>Buddha</s>."

body.text: bhagavān āha // śṛṇuta bhikṣavaḥ punar apy ekasmin samaye tatra kapilavastuni mahānagare 'nyatamaḥ śākyaḥ prativasati / sa āḍhyo mahādhano mahāparivāro vistīrṇaviśālaparigraho vaiśravaṇadhanasamudito vaiśravaṇapratispardhī / tena sadṛśāt kulāt kalatram ānītam / sa tayā sārdhaṃ krīḍati ramate paricārayati

children.text: tasya krīḍato ramamāṇasya paricārayataḥ patnī āpannasattvā putro jāto 'bhirūpo darśanīyaḥ prāsādiko gaura atikrānto mānuṣyavarṇam asaṃprāptaś ca divyavarṇaṃ cāsyavapuḥ śūkṣmatvaṅ maheśākhyaḥ prāptocchuddhakāyaś ca
children.translated_text: While he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself, his wife conceived and a son was born — handsome, fair to behold, pleasing, of golden complexion, surpassing the human color yet not attaining the divine color, with a body of fine skin, of great renown, and of a perfectly pure body.

children.text: tasya jātau jātimahaṃ kṛtvā nāmadheyaṃ vyavasthāpitaṃ kiṃ bhavatu dārakasya nāmeti //
children.translated_text: At his birth, having held a birth celebration, a name was determined: 'What shall the boy's name be?'

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Listen, O <s>bhikṣus</s>. Once again, at one time, in the great city of <s>Kapilavastu</s>, a certain <s>Śākya</s> dwelt. He was wealthy, of great riches, with a great retinue, of extensive and vast possessions, equal in wealth to <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>, rivaling <s>Vaiśravaṇa</s>. He brought a wife from a family of equal standing. Together with her he sported, enjoyed, and amused himself.

body.text: jñātaya ūcuḥ / yasmād asya divyavapus tasmād bhavatu dārakasya vapuṣmān iti nāmeti //
body.translated_text: The relatives said: 'Since he has a divine form (<s>vapus</s>), let the boy's name be <s>Vapuṣmān</s> (the Handsome One).'

body.text: vapuṣmān dāraka aṣṭābhyo dhātrībhyo datto dvābhyām aṃsadhātrī

children.translated_text: two as milk-nurses,
two as bathing-nurses,
and two as play-nurses.
He was raised by the eight nurses, nourished

children.text: ate kṣīreṇa dadhnā navanītena sarpiṣā sarpimaṇḍ
children.translated_text: with milk, curds, fresh butter, ghee, and the cream of ghee,

children.text: aiś cottaptair upakaraṇaviśeṣair āśu vardhate hradastham iva paṅkajam / sa ca śrāddho bhadraḥ kalyāṇāśaya ātmahitaparahitapratipanna
children.translated_text: and with other excellent provisions he grew quickly, like a lotus in a pond. He was faithful, virtuous, of good intentions, devoted to his own welfare and the welfare of others,

children.text: kāruṇiko mahātmā dharmakāmaḥ sarvalokaiś ca pūjyo mānyo
children.translated_text: compassionate, great-souled, desirous of <s>Dharma</s>, and worthy of worship, reverence,
and salutation by all the world.
Then <s>Vapuṣmān</s>, wherever
he went and walked,

'Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: "We shall honor the Teacher, respect [him], revere [him], worship [him]; having honored, respected, revered, and worshipped the Teacher, we shall dwell relying upon [him]." Thus, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, should you train.' This the <s>Bhagavān</s> spoke. Delighted, those <s>bhikṣus</s> rejoiced at the word of the <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.translated_text: The <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'Once upon a time, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, there was a Perfectly Awakened One (<s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>) named <s>Kāśyapa</s>, endowed with knowledge and conduct, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), knower of the world, unsurpassed, trainer of those who are to be tamed, teacher of gods and humans, the <s>Buddha</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s>. Having fulfilled all the duties of a <s>Buddha</s>, he was established in the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of nirvāṇa) without remainder. There, this <s>Candana</s>, in a former time, had a hair-and-nail <s>stūpa</s> built; having been filled with faith in the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Kāśyapa</s>, he went forth [as a monk]. He made an offering of fragrant water at that <s>stūpa</s>, planted flowers, and cultivated the path toward <s>Pratyekabodhi</s>. Then,

body.text: iti dvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ candanāvadāna dvāviṃśatitamaḥ pancchedaḥ //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the twenty-second chapter: the Narrative of <s>Candana</s> (<s>Candanāvadāna</s>). //

body.translated_text: This thought arose in him: 'Is this King <s>Śibi</s> doing this for the sake of beings, or out of compassion? Let me test him.' Then, creating himself in the form of a vulture, dark as crushed collyrium, he approached King <s>Śibi</s> and began to gouge out his eye with his beak. But even then, the king did not become frightened. Rather, looking at that vulture with his two eyes broad with loving-kindness, he said: 'Dear one, take what you need from my body — let affection be maintained.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, favorably impressed, created himself in the form of a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, stood before King <s>Śibi</s>, and said: 'Well done, O king! Give me your two eyes.' The king said: 'O great <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, take what pleases you. No obstacle to this exists for me — take them!' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, with even greater faith, having made the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> form disappear, standing in his own form, encouraging the king, said: 'Well done, well done, O king! children.text: ) dharmasyārthe yakṣāya dattavān // tato yakṣeṇarddhibalādhānād rājñaḥ parṣadaś ca yathādarśitaṃ yathāṅgāni pratyaṅgāni pṛthag vikṛtya vikṛtya bhakṣitāni rudhiraṃ ca pīyamānam
children.translated_text: patient, to the <s>Yakṣa</s> for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>. Then, by the <s>Yakṣa</s>'s supernatural power, the limbs and minor limbs [of the boy] were separately torn apart and eaten, and his blood was drunk, as shown before the king's assembly.

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rājā dharmābhilāṣī na viṣādam āpannaḥ // sa guhyako rājānām uvāca // atṛpto 'smi bho pārthiva bhūyo me prayaccheti // tato rājā tasmai dayitāṃ bhāryāṃ dattavān / sāpi tenaivākāreṇa darśitā / tato bhūyo rājānam uvāca // bhoḥ pārthivādyāpi tṛptiṃ na labhata iti // tato rājā yakṣam uvāca // vatsa datto me ekaputrako bhāryā ca yāvat kiṃ bhuyaḥ prārthayasa iti // guhyaka uvāca //
children.translated_text: Seeing this, the king, desirous of the <s>Dharma</s>, did not fall into despair. That <s>Guhyaka</s> said to the king: 'I am not satisfied, O king! Give me more!' Then the king gave him his beloved wife. She too was shown [being consumed] in the same manner. Then again he said to the king: 'O king, even now I have not attained satisfaction.' Then the king said to the <s>Yakṣa</s>: 'Dear one, my only son has been given, and my wife too — what more do you desire?' The <s>Guhyaka</s> said:

body.translated_text: Hearing this, the king was seized with extreme despair. 'Rarely, perhaps some day,

body.text: svaśarīraṃ me prayacchānena tṛptim upayāsyāmīti // rājovāca // yadi svaśarīraṃ te pradāsyāmi kathaṃ punar dharmaṃ śroṣyāmi / kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ me dharmaṃ vada paścād gṛhītadharmā śarīraṃ parityakṣyāmīti // tato guhyakena rājānaṃ pratijñāyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpyānekaśatāyāḥ pariṣadaḥ purastād dharmo deśitaḥ //
body.translated_text: 'Give me your own body — by this I shall reach satisfaction.' The king said: 'If I give you my own body, how then shall I hear the <s>Dharma</s>? Rather, first teach me the <s>Dharma</s> — afterward, having received the <s>Dharma</s>, I shall renounce my body.' Then, having established the king in his vow, the <s>Guhyaka</s> taught the <s>Dharma</s> before an assembly of many hundreds:

body.translated_text: Then the king, upon hearing that verse, with a gladdened mind, with joy and happiness of the faculties arisen, said to the <s>Yakṣa</s>: 'O <s>Guhyaka</s>, here is my body — do with it as you wish.' Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, knowing the king to be immovable like <s>Meru</s> [in his resolve] for unsurpassed perfect and complete awakening, making the <s>Yakṣa</s> form disappear, standing in his own form, with eyes blooming with faith, holding the son with one hand and the wife with the other, encouraging the king, said: 'Well done, well done, O good man! Your armor is firm — before long, by this determination, you shall attain unsurpassed

body.text: tato rājā śakraṃ devendram idam avocat // sādhu sādhu kauśika kṛto 'smākaṃ dharmābhiprāyapūritaś ceti //
body.translated_text: Then the king spoke thus to <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods: 'Well done, well done, O <s>Kauśika</s>! You have fulfilled our aspiration for the <s>Dharma</s>.'

children.text: sau tena kālena tena samayena surūpo nāma rājā babhūvāhaṃ saḥ

Prince <s>Sundara</s> was <s>Ānanda</s>;

Even then, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s>, I made the renunciation of dear relatives and the renunciation of my own life — how much more now! Therefore, O <s>bhikṣus</s>, you should train thus: "We shall honor the <s>Dharma</s>, respect it, revere it, worship it,

body.text: XXIV.
body.translated_text: XXIV.

body.text: puṇyotsāhāvadānasūtra
body.translated_text: The <s>Sūtra</s> on the Encouragement of Merit (<s>Puṇyotsāhāvadānasūtra</s>).

body.text: atha śrībhagavān buddhaḥ sarvajñas tān sabhāśritān sarvāṃl lokān samālokya punaḥ saddharmam ādiśat //
body.translated_text: Then the glorious <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Buddha</s>, the omniscient one, surveying all the people present in the assembly, again proclaimed the true <s>Dharma</s>:

children.translated_text: "Listen, O sons of good family, to that which is the means for the attainment of the wisdom of awakening —

children.text: saddharmaṃ tan mayākhyātaṃ sattvānāṃ bhadrakāranaṃ // Dak_24.1 //
children.translated_text: the true <s>Dharma</s> declared by me, which is the cause of welfare for beings.
First, by the <s>bodhisattva</s>, for the accomplishment of the wisdom of awakening —

children.text: saṃbodhipraṇidhiṃ kṛtvā kartavyaṃ dānam īpsitam // Dak_24.2 //
children.translated_text: Having made the vow of supreme enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhipraṇidhi</s>), one should give the desired gift.
Then, having refrained from the ten sins with diligence,
having established pure moral conduct (<s>śuddhaśīla</s>), one should practice good restraint (<s>susaṃvara</s>).
Then, having conquered the afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>), abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s> (divine abodes),

children.text: kṣāntivrataṃ sadā dhṛtvā caitavyaṃ jagaddhitam // Dak_24.4 //
children.translated_text: always holding the vow of patience (<s>kṣānti</s>), one should act for the welfare of the world.
Then, holding great zeal for the <s>Dharma</s> in accomplishing the welfare of beings,
having abandoned delight in evil companions, one should cultivate great virtue.
Then, having abandoned attachment to desired objects, being dispassionate toward sensual enjoyments,
having established a firm and courageous mind, one should meditate for the welfare of the three worlds.
Then, having abandoned attachment to non-friends, being devoted to enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>),
in the ocean of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), one should accomplish the jewel of enlightenment for the good of the world.

body.text: etāḥ pāramitāḥ ṣaḍḍhā

children.translated_text: having fulfilled in due order,

children.text: sarvān māragaṇāñ jitvā saṃbodhijñānam āpsyate // Dak_24.8 //
children.translated_text: having conquered all the hosts of <s>Māra</s>, one shall attain the knowledge of perfect enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhijñāna</s>).

body.translated_text: These six <s>pāramitās</s> (perfections),

children.translated_text: Then, thus possessing great supernatural knowledge, endowed with the excellent qualities of glory, prosperity, and vigor,
having accomplished the welfare of all beings, one shall attain the state of a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s> (<s>saṃbuddha</s>).
Thus, having understood this, if you desire Buddhahood (<s>saṃbuddhatva</s>),

children.text: evaṃ pāramitāḥ sarvāḥ pūrayedhvaṃ yathākramam // Dak_24.10 //
children.translated_text: fulfill all the <s>pāramitās</s> in due order.
Holding the vow of supreme enlightenment, abiding in the four <s>Brahmavihāras</s>,
having devoted yourselves to the Three Jewels (<s>Triratna</s>), conduct yourselves for the welfare of the world.
By the power of this merit, all of you, with senses conquered,

children.text: arhantaḥ prāpya saṃbodhiṃ saṃbuddhapadam āpsyatha // Dak_24.12 //
children.translated_text: having attained <s>Arhatship</s> and enlightenment (<s>saṃbodhi</s>), shall reach the state of a Perfectly Awakened <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: ity ādiṣṭaṃ munīndreṇa śrutvā sarve 'pi bhikṣavaḥ /
children.translated_text: Having heard this instruction spoken by the Lord of Sages (<s>Munīndra</s>), all the monks,

children.text: evam asty iti prābhāṣya prābhyanandan prabodhitāḥ // Dak_24.13 //
children.translated_text: saying 'So it is!', rejoiced, being awakened.
That entire assembly too, having heard this, were filled with faith,
and saying 'So be it!', having expressed their agreement, they rejoiced, being awakened.

body.text: iti śrīdvāviṃśatyavadānakathāyāṃ puṇyotsāhāvadānasūtraṃ samāptam //
body.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Dvāviṃśatyavadānakathā</s>, the <s>Puṇyotsāhāvadānasūtra</s> (Scripture of the Narrative of Zeal for Merit) is completed.

children.translated_text: and that which is their cessation — thus speaks the Great Ascetic (<s>Mahāśramaṇa</s>). May there be auspiciousness!
